Did you guys do anything together in the off season, have conversations with one another just so you came in to camp maybe a little bit more focused this year? >> I think even this OTAs was something of asking the QBs, "Hey, what do you guys like from us? Um, what do you want?" And I think with receivers, all the QBs, everyone's throwing after practice. If they want to look, we get another we get a throw out of after. We don't just call it like what it is, what it is. And I think um communicating that early in the spring, going to summer. I know Bryce had a bunch of guys out in Cali and was having a session with them. I was I was on vacation, so I couldn't make it. But um whatchamacallit, I think everyone being um just wanting the same thing, success, and being able to work on it not only during practice but after practice, I think that's a big difference and um just builds that kind of um what would you say? Kind of connection that each guy uh has with uh each QB. >> Talking about receivers, Xavier Gipson so far has had a couple good days of practice. What have you seen out of him? >> Oh man, he's balling, man. He's worked about his butt off this offseason and he's been making plays, man. It's been fun to see and I see him just keep on an upward trend and I love seeing that stuff, man. He makes plays uh for us and we love seeing it every single day. >> Different position, obviously, but from your vantage point, um what are your observations of Monroe Ben on the on the right side of CJ Stroud? >> First training camp and that was a >> [clears throat] >> position he wasn't really drafted for. >> Mhm. I think he's um being like we were talking about earlier, pro's pro. He's he's taking it in strides. He's communicating with us really well. Um I think that's hard to do as a rookie. I think there's a bunch of things that kind of come at you when you're, you know, first year in the league. It's a lot different than college, but he's taking it in strides and he's working his butt off and I can always appreciate that. Um he's making good plays here and there and so I'm I'm happy for him. He's on a steady growth and we love seeing that from a young guy. >> What kind of dude is he? >> He's cool. He's cool, man. I like him. He's he's a He's funny. He's uh but he's a hard worker, too, and I like someone who likes football, so it's been fun playing with him. >> Any example of that that humor in the huddle you got? >> Uh we got a thing going on where he always says it down a distance. He's like, "I got you, man." I'm like, "I I appreciate it every time, man." So he's he's a cool guy. He's a cool guy, man. He's funny. Yeah, in the huddle every time. There you go. I was like, "There you go. And so, he's a cool kid, man. >> Do you prefer to take things day by day or week by week, and how will that shift next week going into pads, like your focus and your goals week by week? >> I really think that um football you have to take day by day cuz you can't get too high on the high days, too low on the low days, or try to look too much into the future. Every time you do that, you get distracted from the day. And so, um I think the objective every single day, not only for myself, but everyone on the team is just to get better that day, whether it's 1%, 10%, anything. You just got to always move forward every single day in something. And if you don't have a goal that day to do, you're not going to get better at it. And so, um I think that's how we're all kind of heading into this camp is we're taking it day by day. Once the game week starts, start game planning, take it still day by day, and I think if we continue that, this uh sky's the limit. >> Having now had a a year of kind of watching Trayvon Meurig and facing him practices now in training camp, like from the perspective of a tight end, what is the most difficult part of reading what he does pre-snap? >> Mhm. I think just him being kind of a jack-of-all-trades is something that's hard to do at safety position. I mean, that dude, he'll knock your block off, too. Like, if you're not on your Ps and Qs, he can hit, man. But at the same time, you don't know if he's coming down to blow you up, doesn't know if he's trying to come down trying to lock you up. And so, I think that's something that he's even gotten better from last year on is his coverage and everything. He's He's done uh He's done something this off season, but he's been really really good at uh both so far. And so, it's something you can always respect in a player. >> How much of working with Brad has It's It's been different now that he's got a new role? How much of it has it been the same since you guys have known him for years? >> Mhm. I mean, Brad has always kind of run our team offense meetings. And so, him jumping into the role OC, it's been fun. I think the offense has um been blossoming. You know, we've been comfortable with him because he's uh been a part of the offense for the last few years. But him taking that next step, it's been a lot of fun him being a OC calling the plays and all that. And like you said, our offense has been going off lately, so he's he's doing a great job. >> During OTAs, we asked Jaelan Phillips who among the young guys has kind of stepped up into a leadership role. And Jaelan said, well, I don't necessarily know about the young guys, but Chuba is a guy who's stepped up as a leader and he's he just kind of made himself known as someone who just kind of runs the locker room. When you hear that, what are your reactions? >> I mean, you know, Chuba, we've been here for shoot, going on 60 years now, and he's definitely earned that. And you know, he's a big rah-rah guy and I love it cuz I'm no, I'm not a rah-rah guy, but he's he's awesome, man. He gets the guys going every single day. He sets it straight. He sets our goals for every beginning of practice, let's get to work. We got focus on what you can focus on, just get better today. And he preaches to the young guys, he picks young guys out with him. And it's it's awesome to see cuz he's a dude who works for that. >> Anyone else? Thanks, Tom. >> Appreciate y'all. >> [music] [music]

title: Devin Lloyd: 'It's going to be difficult to deal with us' | Carolina Panthers
text: David David's talking a second ago about kind of your impact on the defense as a whole, specifically with the the linebacker room you've got. How are you trying to help, whether it's Travon Walker and whoever it is, through this process? >> Yeah, for sure. Um I mean, every day, you know, we're obviously uh very critical of what we put on film, uh how we attack the weight room, you know, even just talking about little things off field. So, um every day we're all looking to improve, um you know, and uh it's really just, you know, being honest and evaluating ourselves every day. That's really what it comes down to. >> We read about your film session with Luke Kuechly. Do you tell us a little bit about that and um how it came to fruition and maybe some of the things you you picked up from him. >> Yeah, so um obviously him being, you know, somebody who's going to the Hall of Fame this year and you know, everything I heard he was a great person and somebody I reached out to. So, I texted him um you know, a couple weeks ago and uh this is actually before I left for the break and uh while I was gone, um for a little bit, you know, we planned on a day for me to meet with him when I came back. And so, [clears throat] that's what we did. Um and he's just really responsive and uh you know, just he's a guy that loves ball. So, I'm grateful um that he was willing to do that and hopefully, you know, I'm pretty sure it won't be the last time. Um but it was great, you know, we really just talked about leadership, we talked about ball, talked about life a little bit, really just um just trying to find that 1% to, you know, take my game to the next level on and off the field. Um and uh it it was a great talk. >> What was that film session like? I I I assume that you both are uh you both study the game, but just tell me a little bit about the film session. >> Yeah, I mean, we're just talking ball. Uh some technique, uh just some on the field, just overall awareness type stuff. Um Just talking ball, you know, I mean, we we talked to good about um just just everything. It wasn't just one specific thing, just went over we uh threw on a game and just basically, hey, what do you see on this play? Okay, you know, what what do I see on this play kind of thing and just went through the went through the tape. >> Did you watch a lot of Luke Kuechly growing up? >> I watched a good amount, yeah. I mean, you know about his highlights. And when I was growing up, I mean, film wasn't really accessible for me up until I got to college. But definitely saw a lot of his highlights growing up. >> Your position is position is uh it's kind of a torch that's been passed in Carolina for a long time. I mean, how much of that were you aware of before getting here? How much more aware of it are you after being here? >> Yeah, I knew about Luke. I knew about Thomas Davis. And then Sam Mills, you know, I learned more about the guys. Obviously, Dan and Jon Beason. I mean, Shaq. You know, you go down the line and you look at the history of the linebackers. And I know I missed a couple, but um I I learned more about it as I came here, but I already knew about some of the mainstays, some of the the big names. And then looking at it even deeper as I, you know, with here a little longer, you really realize that yeah, there's a lineage of of great linebacker play. And that's special to be a part of. And I want to just continue to do everything I can to to be the best player I can be, best leader, best everything I can for this team to carry on that torch. >> Do you Do you let yourself think about it that often and I guess like take on that pressure? Or do you have to kind of put it out of sight, out of mind once you're on the field and not worry about it? >> I don't think about it until you guys bring it up. I mean, for me it's just attacking the process every day. And ultimately, it doesn't really matter. Like, I don't focus on anything outside. I don't go on social media, especially right now. It's really just every, you know, second of the day, how can I get better? And just being efficient with my time really is what it is. Like, time is valuable. So, just making sure that always doing something to, you know, take that one step in the right direction. >> Coach Canales mentioned like you've got your training figured out. How long did it take you to figure it out and what was the process in getting there? >> I'd say really took 3 years going into my fourth season. So, last off-season. All the way up throughout the really just all of last year was really the first time like from the end of the 2024 season. Started that off-season. Excuse me. All the way through is really when I kind of found my process. And I just needed some refining throughout the years and that really just come from learning what my body needs, what my mind needs, what my spirit needs in order to really it's it's a lifestyle. It's not even just necessarily about training camp or the season. Like it's a lifestyle. So, just just finding the best way to do something that's sustainable for me. >> Understanding that pads haven't even come on yet in training camp so far. How good could this defense be? Dave just talked about how the defense was dominant the first 2 days of training camp and so on. Um How how would you approach that question? How? >> Yeah. I mean I don't like to over-promise and under-deliver, but I do have very high expectations. I'm very optimistic about what we can be. Um I mean it's been a great competitive last 4 days of training camp. OTAs same thing. Now we're playing real ball next time we come out when we put the pads on and then that's when we can get an even better gauge, but I will say that it's been very competitive on our side of the ball and for us especially once we get everybody back healthy and we're at full strength. You know, it's going to be very difficult to deal with us when we're doing what we need to do and you know, I think we're going to be able to do that. >> As a vet coming into a new system, are you instantly a leader in that linebacker room or could it take some time to find your voice as a leader? Have you found that voice and and what How process been like working with Trev and and other guys in the group? >> Yeah, I would say so for sure. And that just comes from uh building the relationships with the guys on the team, which has been super easy. I mean, from top to bottom, the whole roster. Uh I'm just just so much love in that locker room and uh just grateful for for all the guys, offense, defense, special teams, whatever it is. Um so, it's been really easy just to build those relationships, get to know the guys. Um they've accepted me for who I am, and uh it it's been a lot of fun. Um so, um yeah, I would say so, and then obviously it starts in the linebacker room. Uh really just trying to make sure that I'm doing my part to elevate the room, but uh I'm not the only one in that room. You know, everybody else um is a leader in their own right. So, it's really just us learning from each other. Um obviously being uh humble enough to It doesn't matter what year you're in, um being able to uh learn from each other. But But yeah, I definitely feel like I've found my voice. >> Devin, now that you've been here, I guess 4 or 5 months, uh anything you've learned about Jaylen? Probably a lot, but uh and some interesting things you've picked up that you didn't know about Jaylen coming in. >> Yeah, I mean, first of all, he's a great dude. You know, he's funny to be around, always cracking jokes, but um just uh incredible athlete. You can tell uh he takes great care of his body. Um and then yeah, he's passionate about the game. You know, he's a guy that that loves football. I mean, we got a ton of guys that love football, and he's one of them. Um so, just you know, a really good teammate, and you know, I'm glad to be around him. >> Devin, what has your process been like? When you're the one calling plays, but you're also learning a new defense. Like, what do you go through to [clears throat] get yourself ready? Is it flash cards, talking out loud? What do you do? >> So, this is my fourth defense going into my fifth season. So, um I've had to essentially relearn a new defense every year, and in doing that, you kind of um find a way that works best for you. For me, uh it's really just, you know, looking at the playbook, looking at the film, looking at the playbook, looking at the film, um talking it out with the coaches. Uh I think now I'm at a point now where I kind of uh visualize it in a way where it all makes sense. So, for me, yeah, I need the reps on the field. That's probably the most valuable thing. Um, but, you know, I always tell, you know, some of the guys in the room like the best way I learned early on was drawing on the board, drawing the offensive formation, drawing the defensive uh, formation, and then drawing the play, everybody's assignments. Um, I think that's one of the best ways to learn, and I'll do that sometimes. Um, but going into year five now, uh, you know, I do a little bit of everything. >> As you've learned it, is there someone you've maybe leaned on more to help, or or are you just kind of figuring it out as you go? >> Yeah, I mean, look, like, uh, football's football, so it's not too much different than what I've done in past defenses. The biggest thing is, uh, okay, like we call it this instead of this here. You know, it's like, okay, but this is the technique we're doing here. Um, this is who we're dropping off of. Oh, this is our run gap. Okay, um, just all the, you know, different checks as well. So, it's not too far off from what I've done in the past. Um, but like you guys always hear, it's it's literally just the terminology is the only thing. So, it's a new language. >> How is this terminology? >> Uh, pretty simple. I mean, they do a really good job of making it, um, easy for everybody to understand at all different levels. And I'd say overall it's um, been very clear. There's not been gray area as far as how we're fitting certain plays, concepts, whatever the case may be. So, um, it's it's been good. >> You uh, last one, endured, I'm sure, a lot of hot training camps in Jacksonville. What do you make of all the rain here this first week? >> We've been getting blessed. It's I know it's not going to last for long, but, uh, I mean, it's definitely been the easiest as far as weather-wise training camp that I've ever been a part of. Um, just, you know, with the overcast and even the rain, but it's not raining or more than like 10 minutes or whatever the case may be. So, I know eventually it's going to start to creep up on us here and then once we go out to Jacksonville, we're definitely going to feel it. So, um but we need that and, you know, that's what comes with training camp. >> Thanks, Devin. >> All right, thank you guys. >> [music] [music]

title: Dave Canales breaks down Day 3 of training camp | Carolina Panthers
text: Uh great day. Uh just a bounce back for the offense. So we keep score um on every period and the defense pretty dominant the first two days um with some flashes by the offense, but a good response um by Bryce and the guys. Got the run game going a little bit, hit some balls down the field and um you know did a decent job in the move the ball at the end and I just love that. Love the uh the competitive competitiveness that's happening that they're bringing out in each other. And that's the way, you know, we get our best football is is by challenging each other every day. Um the matchups up front, the matchups on the edges, all those things. So really pleased with uh the work that way and and uh and the bounceback. >> Pretty great day for Xavier Leg. What have you seen from him so far during the first week of camp? >> Yeah, just a great carryover from the spring at this point. Now X knows the system. Um that's the cool part is as we bring free agents, as we bring rookies in, you know, they see X and he knows how to do it all. whether it's uh in the base game plan, third downs, uh nuances in the red zone, all the different things. He knows how to do it, but just matching it with his consistency. He looks fast. Um he looks powerful. He's having a great camp so far. Um as we get started, and I'm excited to see where he goes from here. >> On the injury front, um do you have an update on Rob, uh Mike, Jack, and Brazle as well? >> Yeah, I mean, all all good stuff. So, uh Rob's trending in the right direction. He should be back pretty quickly. Uh Mike too. Mike had a really good day running out there. Um they were able to treat him up and uh you know didn't look like anything significant. Um but both of those guys, you know, camp back is what they call it. You know, you get in and it's first time you're competing. You're going against each other. Um and fortunately for us, we have this bonus week, you know, with the Hall of Fame game where a lot of the things that end up popping up early on in camps happening for us about a week earlier. So we can get ahead of it. We can get a treatment plan and then we can dose them the right way and get them back out there. Chris, a little knee soreness. Um just something that we're being aware of and we're going to get him some treatment, get him out there as quickly as possible. >> Dave, uh the union has asked to look at the film with Nick's injury. >> How confident are you that you guys were doing things the right way in terms of the acclamations? >> Yeah, we teach the guys uh we're aware that they're looking into it. Um you know, we we have the rules, we have the standards, we let them know. And I think from there, you know, that's kind of more of a Bruce question just in terms of what's happening and what questions might be asked. But um you know, all we can do is really just lay the lay the groundwork out, show the guys good examples of what it looks like, and then go from there. >> Have you ever been through a process like that before where the PA or maybe the NFL looked into something you guys practice? >> Yeah, we had a couple uh just in Seattle, we had a couple of situations where, you know, they were pretty critical of what we were doing in our practices. We had to adjust, you know, and there might have been some fines thrown out there and, you know, uh OTAA practice or something lost. Uh but you know I think that was kind of early on um really it was after 2011 sometime when the you know when the CBA and they all got together and kind of said hey here's how here's the modes and uh we learned we grew and um so fortunately for me coming into you know my first time being a head coach in the last couple of years I've had history and experience with how to do it and how to educate the guys by showing great examples of what we're looking for. >> Reed uh made a pretty impressive catch over three defenders today. What is it about his game that you that sticks out to you? >> Really? Um, he's consistent, so he knows the concepts. He's a really smart guy and he's been that way since we got him. A guy we have a lot of trust in. And then he just keeps making plays. You know, uh, Tater uh, Carl Smith is here as one of our uh, senior offensive adviserss and um, he said, you know, you know, a receiver is good when you throw it, they catch it. And he does. So he makes the play whether somebody's close to him or he's got space. um he's got an ability to bend, get out of his breaks either way. So, he's given him a a great chance to compete to make this roster with a lot of other guys. And so, I'm proud to just see him where he's at right now. >> When you go to pads, um what do you want to see out of Jonathan Brooks? >> Uh really just, you know, nothing different than what he's doing now is be stay on your track in the run game. Uh be on top of your protections. Um we're not telling guys to go to the ground. Once you get in pads, it gets more physical. those types of things. The trip up might happen. You know, you get knocked off balance, he'll go to the ground and and really just to kind of get that uh contact adaptation. You know, it's not just about taking the hits and absorbing, but it's also about hitting the ground um and just feeling your legs and and getting comfortable with that. So, just, you know, encouraging him to be confident, play fast, and and all all the rest of it in his time will come back. He's been playing the position for a long time. >> Just to confirm, when will you go to pads? >> I believe it's Tuesday. Mhm. >> What you seeing from Monroe on the right side now that he's had a couple days to like know that's kind of his role and how did the stuff over there in the spring? >> Yeah, I I've seen great physical ability. I've seen his his uh athleticism, length, sheer strength and power. Um you know, he's gotten really strong, especially this summer, too. He spent a lot of time on that. So, I've really seen him, um he's got all the tools to do an excellent job over there. Now, it's just about getting comfortable on the right side. Um, getting your sets right, getting your targets right in the run game. And that's the part that's been up and down a little bit for him. If he'd be up here telling you the same thing, there's stuff that he wants to work on. And, um, and again, just getting challenged by, you know, Jaylen Phillips every day over there on the right side. And, you know, Pat Jones flips over, Princeley, these guys challenging him and and bringing out the best. You know, that's one of the parts of competition is is when guys are going against each other and challenging each other, it uh it shows kind of the holes in your game and the techniques you need to work on. That's exactly what we need. And uh that's what Monroe's getting >> With Monroe in that regard, does that even become more apparent that some of the things he needs to work on as you transition to pads? >> Uh probably will. Uh there now I will say this the transition from being in just jerseys or or a spider to pads there's more of a surface for the offensive lineman to grab onto. So, it's actually kind of to the offensive line's advantage once you do get to pads, you know, and that's where also just with these first couple of days while we're taking in all the information and it's so important, we don't want to make any judgments about any of our guys, whether it's a pass rusher or a pass protector, even at even outside at receiver, you know, in DB once there's that extra surface, you know, can the guy continue to play this combative type of football, this is a little bit different, you know, so um that's where we really get to have, you know, the the clear picture of of people that are going to be able to help us. >> We're going to talk to Deon Lloyd. >> Yes. >> And you talked about him, I guess, a couple of days ago and how impressed you were. What have you seen from him? >> Yeah. Um, you know, just a pros pro, the way that he prepares, the way he takes care of his body. >> He's a guy you have to pull back because he's going to want to do more. Um, loves to be in the gym, in the weight room, working on his body, aqua therapy, whatever it is, massage, different. he's got his whole plan figured out. And then just as a player on the field, there's a there's an energy about him. There's a there's an excitement. There's a focus and engagement that he brings to walkthroughs to the practice that's great. And especially when it's coming from that inside linebacker position, you know, and we've had some great ones here. And um he's one of the guys that really brings that brings the whole group together and has them all talking and communicating and uh great leadership. on a new team. It's kind of hard to kind of establish your voice. Yeah. Immediately. Has he begun to do that >> from the time he got here? And um first of all, the guy his reputation precedes him. So, a lot of the guys knew who he was and and the type of football that he was capable of playing, but then just the way he carries himself. Um it's a it's a it's it's a posture where you want to respect the guy and you know that he's he's here to work. He's here to do it together um with the guys. And I know they can see that and he fits right into a lot of the guys we have here already. And so, um, really it was an immediate impact, but now that we're back at camp and the guys are excited about the season coming up and all that, you know, it's just a daily reminder for all them guys. We got to be on it and that's the type of urgency you got to have. >> Uh, John Meti and Bryce obviously played in college. Yeah. >> U, have you seen that chemistry kind of manifest itself in camp so far? And then just generally, what are your early impressions of? >> Yeah, absolutely. There's there's a big- time uh trust factor there. whether it's just knowing he's going to break the route at the right time or even after the play with some of the scramble opportunities Bryce has found him on. There's this immediate chemistry. And then um you know just from a personal standpoint too, another veteran guy. Uh another guy who I love that's here um because again just talking about Devin, I got to talk about John too. Just the way he approaches every day and and uh regards this opportunity and and is willing to you know compete but also willing to talk to guys and help. So, uh, I love that he's here and I love that he's, uh, bringing a lot of competition to that room. >> Going back to Devin, how does he, how does he kind of rub off on Trevan or the guy next to him? How does he sort of change their role? >> Well, it takes some pressure off first of all, but it also sets an example for this is how the position is played. It's meant to be played cerebrally. Got to know what's happening pre- snap and then once that ball snap, do your job. But at the end of the day, go attack the ball wherever it's at, whether it's on the perimeter, whether it's up inside. And it's that urgency, it's the aggressiveness, the way he plays. That's such a great example for that room. Um, but it also just allows Trevan, allows Claude, it allows Bam to just play ball. Um, because he's getting everybody sorted out. He's making the calls. He's got the command in the huddle. Um, and what I've seen over the years is is that's very comforting for guys. Dave, we always talk about how players develop, but from your coaching staff, who's the guys that have grown the most with with you since you came here to >> Well, I got to talk about our coordinators first. You know, Brad's doing a fantastic job of just putting the whole thing together, building concepts off of concepts, making sure guys are prepared to go out there and um you know, in our move the ball uh periods and situations, you know, one of the critical things is make sure you get that call in early. and he's been on top of the personnels's, the DNDs, and and doing a great job of maintaining that rhythm. Um, I love just where where E's got the defense and the guys talking and communicating, uh, troubleshooting different concepts, run concept, pass concepts. You know, there's a lot of familiar language that's carryover. And so, I feel a lot of preparation there. And then with Tracy, just continuing to push the envelope. We do some things different um, in some of our phases than a lot of teams. And I love that. It keeps the guys engaged and you know there's a point where when you start to master the the basics and the core of what you're doing, it's so important that we push our guys and we throw new concepts at them, throw different ways to cover kicks, to return kicks. It keeps them um interested in it and it's fun and uh challenging at the same time. So, he's done a great job of just, you know, bringing that unit together. So, it's really just all three phases. the the level of comfortability that I have with these guys that we've been working with together to build here's how we play and then here's what we do and we've captured all those things at this point right now and the challenge for us is can we make sure that that shows up every single day and that's always where I'll be pushing them. >> We asked Dan I I don't think we've asked you about any the thought of perhaps bringing in a a fourth quarterback sometime between now and I don't know middle of August. >> Yeah, I mean it's it's always on our radar. Um, we're looking for how we can make that fit in. As we all know, we have a number of guys that we're counting on to come back to us in short order. And then there's a couple of guys that'll be back further down in the future. But because of those guys, they all count towards our 90man roster. It makes it really challenging to carry four quarterbacks when we have depth concerns at at some other positions just to throw a practice. So, we have to keep that in mind. But we're always looking. We're always looking at all the different positions because we have to be ready, you know, when when this is or that kind of show up throughout camp. We got to be ready to pivot and bring people in. >> Last question. >> Everybody good? >> Good. >> Thank you, coach. >> All right. Thank you.

title: Tetairoa McMillan: 'We're very slept on' | Carolina Panthers
text: Hey. What up? What up? >> You told us that you gained some weight, but you know, we just had to see you zoom until now. Your fans are just kind of getting a full look at, I guess, kind of like your re-comped body for season two. >> I mean, I I don't know. This is just what I played out in college, so I just feel a lot more comfortable at, you know, the weight I'm at right now, and I'm I feel a lot bigger, stronger, faster, and I'm moving well right now, so um so the added weight was was good, for sure. >> What's the difference coming in year two when you're more comfortable with everything and and as opposed to last year's rookie year? >> Uh I mean, first off, the the standards the standards are higher, obviously. Um you know, just coming off of uh entering the playoffs and one year with Bryce, chemistry's a lot different. Um a lot more confident. Bryce has it me, and we all having each other, so um you know, I'm just looking forward to year two and and what it brings. >> What are you noticing any differences with with Brad as as coordinator? I know it's early, and but are you noticing any type of differences in play calls and >> Uh I mean, at the end of the day, the playbook is still the same, but um obviously, you know, I feel like Coach Canales and and coach uh Coach Brad, you know, they feed off each other, you know, as far as their ideas, their opinions, so um on the field, I think it's just both of them at the end of the day. >> Team Mike, you had a chance to go back to the island and have that back giveaway. Can you talk about your foundation and just being able to go back and um and give back to that community? >> Yeah, obviously, you know, that's a blessing. Just being able to um start my foundation, but also, you know, launch it in, you know, the city that I'm from, uh you know, my people, so just did a little backpack giveaway, uh like you said, and um I just being able to see the the the smiles it puts on, not really the kids, but the the parents as well, so um you know, obviously being that that role model that light um that little kids can look up to even grown-ups. Um you know, that's a blessing. >> How long have you been >> Circling off of that um with the role model piece of it. You saw the stories about the camp and the miscommunication with uh sports flex and flex sports. Just I want to just kind of give you a chance to kind of speak on that and just kind of tell people what happened and how that kind of fell apart. >> Yeah, I mean I don't want anybody to think that I don't like kids or anything like that. You know, I I love the kids. Um obviously, you know, they're the next generation, so um try to give back as much as possible, but um yeah, I don't know where that came from. I never committed to that, so but you know, I I I look forward to seeing all the kids that expected me to be at that camp either at a game or come out to a practice or you know, just so I can make up for it. >> So, where did the miscommunication happen? >> I have no idea. I would I would I wish I knew. >> You said you would never committed to the So you sounds like you'd like the kids to come I don't know. Come to a game or what's that going to look like? >> Yeah, I mean for sure. You know, obviously there's there's a lot of people that wait wait for us on the practice either before practice or after practice, so um you know, just stop by or you know, just come to the game. Uh fill up the Bank of America Stadium, do whatever we can just to give back. >> Just want to clarify where this camp the in at AC Reynolds in Asheville. >> I have no idea where it was. >> [snorts] >> Greg, you mentioned the chemistry with Bryce Brown in the past year and everything that goes along with that. What's something that that you know now that you didn't know in your rookie year that you might have told yourself in your rookie year like, this is what you're going to learn in your first season. sure, I mean just just as anything you know, anything new that you start, you know, you obviously tiptoe into it. You're not really um very confident. You know, I feel like I'm a lot more confident just, you know, in my speed, my mind, just confident in Bryce, and in the play calling, and my teammates, so I feel like that's that's one thing that I would have told myself last year is just you know, just be confident. You don't have to be You don't have to do everything. You just just be you, really. >> Tua, what do you think about Chris Olave so far? That was you just a year ago, being that rookie in the receiving room, and he's starting to look pretty good so far. >> No, for sure. I I I like Chris a lot, and you know, outside of him being a good player, he's a good person. You know, he he brings light into that room. You know, he likes to joke around, have fun. He's still a little kid at the end of the day, but you know, when it comes to the field, he he takes care of business, so I'm looking forward to playing alongside of him, for sure. >> Do you think that will allow you to play a little bit more in the slot than Chris Olave? >> Um who knows? I'm not too sure. You know, I I I won't know what the coaches have planned for me in this in this offense, so but whatever whatever chance I get to to make to have opportunities to get the ball, you know, I'm all for it, so I'm looking forward to it, for sure. >> You said that he's like that kid when you just said that in response to Do you feel older now coming into this new season? Do you feel like a sense of Oh, I'm a little bit more more better and more confident? >> Um yeah, for sure. I I don't care what anybody says, I'm a vet now, so But I mean, yeah, for sure. Just having one one year under my belt, and I was fortunate enough to play all 18 games last year, which is, you know, uncommon, so you know, I have a lot of experience, um you know, I try my best to just, you know, give some knowledge, give some wisdom, at least the the knowledge and wisdom that I have to all the young guys. >> Tua, Bryce Bryce said yesterday that you know, you guys had a chance to work out together a lot this summer, and stuff like this. What was the nature of those workouts, and what did you learn about him? >> Uh shoot, it's really just you know, we just playing football at the end of the day. Just trying to get that that timing right, you know. And you know, it it definitely translates onto the field. I was definitely surprised by some of the things that he's been doing the couple these last few days. So, it feels good though. You know, the chemistry is you know, it it's black and white right now. So, there's no gray area. And we look good right now. So, hopefully we can continue this. >> You came in as part of the same draft class with Nick. How difficult was that and emotional yesterday both on a personal level and just from a team standpoint? >> I mean, for sure. That's obviously a a big loss for us, but you know, at the end of the day it gives somebody a chance to step up. And I'm sure we have a a lot of young guys and vet guys that can that can do the job just as well as he did. So, obviously that hurt, but at the end of the day we all got to go. You know, we all want to pursue something. We all want to go somewhere. So, you know, and I'm I'm sure Nick understands that and he you know, he's he's he's he's with us. You know, we're we're with him and we're praying for him >> Everyone else had that emotional scene where you you spoke to him or backed him up before he left. Did you have any specific message for him then or in the hours since? >> Uh shoot, I mean, no. I didn't really get the chance to talk to him. I tried to be, you know, optimistic as far as, you know, before his imaging or whatever whatever the case may be, but you know, just man, just be confident. Just you know, God never makes a mistake. You know, even though he's out for the season, he'll be out for a while. You know, just you know, it happened for a reason. You know, God like they say, God gives his toughest battles to his his toughest I don't I don't even know, but you know what I mean. But no, you're right. Exactly. I got I got lost. But you know, just you know, just Uh, you know, stay prayed up. And that that's it. >> Does it feel different? Do you feel, you know, a little more grown man? >> Man, I've been grown. Nah, but uh, I guess it feels a little different just as far as my confidence. Um, you know, and obviously as far as the team as well, you know, they they seen this past year what I'm able to bring to the team, uh, what what I'm able to do for everybody. So, um, feel like they're a lot more confident me as well. >> Have you had a chance to look back and what you did last year and kind of appreciate what you did? And I know you're never happy, you always said that, but and any goals numerically, uh, statistically this year? >> Uh, nah, I'm I mean, I I I didn't get a chance to really take a look at what I did last year and to be honest, I don't really care. But, uh, you know, I just want to be, um, better for the team this year. Um, you know, we we obviously, like I said in the in the beginning of this interview, you know, the standard is set a lot higher. So, um, everybody's holding everybody to a higher standard, so just looking forward to meet the expectations or exceed them. >> Personal goals? Personal goals, stats? >> Nah, I don't got any. >> I was going to ask if you could expand on your advice to yourself about just being you. It sounds like an easy thing, but probably a difficult thing. What helped you to get there? Do you feel like you have? I mean, I try to I pride myself in being myself, being authentic. Uh, so I feel like I, you know, I did a good job as far as coming in, uh, just being who I am, you know, being the guy that you know, they picked, uh, being the guy that they brought to the team. So, um, so I'm just try to continue that, but as far as just the younger guys just be yourself as far as, you know, they they picked you for a reason, you know, I'm sure they picked you obviously for the ability the abilities you have on the field, but um you know, just the light that you can bring be to the locker room, be to your your room. Um and you know, I got to give a big shout out to the rookies so far. They they did a phenomenal job and um I I'm I'm excited to see what what happens for sure. >> Talked about Brown, talked about your connection with Young. A lot of plays out there today. Just how powerful do you believe this wide receiver group can be? >> Uh shoot, I mean we we're we're pretty good. I feel like we we're we're very slept on, you know. We have a lot of guys that may not have got the opportunities past up couple years or even the rookies that haven't got any opportunities yet, but you know, I'm looking forward to seeing what the future holds for us and you know, I'm excited. I'm excited we're going to make plays this year. >> Nice seeing you, Mack. >> All right, y'all. Appreciate it. >> [music] [music]

On the injury front, um, do you have an update on Rob, uh, Mike Jack and Brazle practice as well? >> Yeah, I mean, all all good stuff. So, uh, Rob's trending in the right direction. He should be back pretty quickly. Uh, Mike, too, Mike had a really good day running out there. Um, they were able to treat him up and, uh, you know, didn't look like anything significant. Um, but both of those guys, you know, camp back is what they call it. You know, you get in and it's the first time you're competing, you're going against each other. Um, and fortunately for us, we have this bonus week, you know, with the Hall of Fame game where a lot of the things that end up popping up early on in camps happening for us about a week earlier. So, we can get ahead of it. We can get a treatment plan and then we can dose them the right way and get them back out there. Chris, a little knee soreness. Um, just something that we're being aware of and we're going to get him some treatment, get him out there as quickly as possible. >> Dave, uh, the union has asked to look at the films with Nick's injury. How confident are you that you guys were doing things the right way in terms of the acclamations? >> Yeah, we teach the guys uh we're aware that they're looking into it. Um, you know, we we have the rules, we have the standards, we let them know, and I think from there, you know, that's kind of more of a Bruce question just in terms of what's happening and what questions might be asked, but um, you know, all we can do is really just lay the lay the groundwork out, show the guys good examples of what it looks like, and then go from there. Have you ever been through a process like that before where the PA or maybe the NFL looked into something you guys practice? >> Yeah, we had a couple uh just in Seattle, we had a couple of situations where, you know, they were pretty critical of what we were doing in our practices. We had to adjust, you know, and there might have been some fines thrown out there and, you know, uh OTAA practice or something lost. Uh but, you know, I think that was kind of early on. Um really it was after 2011 sometime when the you know when the CBA and they all got together and kind of said hey here's how here's the modes and uh we learned we grew and um so fortunately for me coming into you know my first time being a head coach in the last couple of years I've had history and experience with how to do it and how to educate the guys by showing great examples of what we're looking for uh made a pretty impressive catch over three defenders today. What is it about his game that you that sticks out to you? >> Really, um, he's consistent, so he knows the concepts. He's a really smart guy and he's been that way since we got him. A guy we have a lot of trust in. And then he just keeps making plays. You know, uh, Tater, uh, Carl Smith is here as one of our, uh, senior offensive adviserss and, um, he said, you know, you know, a receiver is good. When you throw it, they catch it. And he does. So, he makes the play whether somebody's close to him or he's got space. um he's got an ability to bend, get out of his breaks either way. So, he's given him a a great chance to compete to make this roster with a lot of other guys. And so, I'm proud of just seeing where he's at right now. >> When you go to pads, um what do you want to see out of Jonathan Brooks? >> Uh really just, you know, nothing different than what he's doing now is be stay on your track in the run game. Uh be on top of your protections. Um we're not telling guys to go to the ground. Once you get in pads, it gets more physical. those types of things, the trip up might happen. You know, you get knocked off balance, he'll go to the ground and and really just to kind of get that uh contact adaptation. You know, it's not just about taking the hits and absorbing, but it's also about hitting the ground um and just feeling your legs and and getting comfortable with that. So, just, you know, encouraging him to be confident, play fast, and and all all the rest of it in his timing will come back. He's been playing the position for a long time. >> Just to confirm, when will you go to pads? >> I believe it's Tuesday. >> What are you seeing from Monroe on the right side now? a couple days to like know that's kind of his role. And how did the [clears throat] stuff over there in the spring? >> Yeah, I I've seen great physical ability. I've seen his his uh athleticism, length, sheer strength, and power. Um you know, he's gotten really strong, especially this summer, too. He spent a lot of time on that. So, I've really seen him um he's got all the tools to do an excellent job over there. Now, it's just about getting comfortable on the right side. um getting your sets right, getting your targets right in the run game. And that's the part that's been up and down a little bit for him. If he'd be up here telling you the same thing, there's stuff that he wants to work on. And um and again, just getting challenged by, you know, Jaylen Phillips every day over there on the right side. And you know, Pat Jones flips over, princely, these guys challenging him and and bringing out the best. You know, that's one of the parts of competition is is when guys are going against each other and challenging each other, it uh it shows kind of the holes in your game and the techniques you need to work on. That's exactly what we need and uh that's what Monroe is getting right now. >> With Monroe in that regard, does that even become more apparent that some of the things he needs to work on as you transition to pads? >> Uh probably will. Uh there. Now, I will say this, the transition from being in just jerseys or or a spider to pads, there's more of a surface for the offensive lineman to grab onto. So, it's actually kind of to the offensive line's advantage once you do get to pads, you know, and that's where also just with these first couple of days while we're taking in all the information and it's so important, we don't want to make any judgments about any of our guys, whether it's a pass rusher or a pass protector, even at even outside at receiver, you know, in DB once there's that extra surface, you know, can the guy continue to play this combative type of football, this is a little bit different, you know, so um that's where we really get to have, you know, the the clear picture of of people that are going to be able to help us. >> You talked to Deon Lloyd. >> Yes. >> And you talked about him, I guess, a couple of days ago and how impressed you were. What have you seen from him? >> Yeah. Um, you know, just a pros pro, the way that he prepares, the way he takes care of his body. >> He's a guy you have to pull back because he's going to want to do more. Um, loves to be in the gym, in the weight room, working on his body, aqua therapy, whatever it is, massage, different. He's got his whole plan figured out. And then just as a player on the field, there's a there's an energy about him. There's a there's an excitement. There's a a focus, an engagement that he brings to walkthroughs to the practice that's great. And especially when it's coming from that inside linebacker position, you know, and we've had some great ones here. and um he's one of the guys that really brings that brings the whole group together and has them all talking and communicating and uh great leadership. >> When you read on a new team, it's kind of hard to kind of establish your voice immediately. Has he begun to do that >> from the time he got here? And um first of all, the guy his reputation precedes him. So, a lot of the guys knew who he was and and the type of football that he was capable of playing. But then just the way he carries himself, um it's a it's a it's it's a posture where you want to respect the guy and you know that he's he's here to work. He's here to do it together um with the guys and I know they can see that and he fits right into a lot of the guys we have here already. And so um really it was an immediate impact. But now that we're back at camp and the guys are excited about the season coming up and all that, you know, it's just a daily reminder for all of them guys. We got to be on it and that's the type of urgency you got to have. >> Uh John Miy and Bryce obviously played in college. Yeah. >> Uh, have you seen that chemistry kind of manifest itself in camp so far? And then just generally, what are your early impressions of? >> Yeah, absolutely. There's there's a big time uh trust factor there, whether it's just knowing he's going to break the route at the right time or even after the play with some of the scramble opportunities Bryce has found him on. There's this immediate chemistry. And then, um, you know, just from a personal standpoint too, another veteran guy, uh, another guy who I love that's here. Um because again just talking about Devin, I got to talk about John, too. Just the way he approaches every day and and uh regards this opportunity and and is willing to, you know, compete, but also willing to talk to guys and help. So, uh I love that he's here and I love that he's uh bringing a lot of competition to that room. >> Going back to Devin, how does he how does he kind of rub off on Trevan or the guy next to him? How does he sort of change their role? Well, it takes some pressure off first of all, but it also sets an example for this is how the position is played. It's meant to be played cerebrally. Got to know what's happening pre- snap. And then once that ball snap, do your job, but at the end of the day, go attack the ball wherever it's at, whether it's on the perimeter, whether it's up inside. And it's that urgency, it's the aggressiveness, the way he plays. That's such a great example for that room. Um, but it also just allows Trevan, allows Claude, allows Bam to just play ball. um because he's getting everybody sorted out. He's making the calls. He's got the command in the huddle. Um and what I've seen over the years is is that's very comforting for guys. Dave, we always talk about how players develop, but from your coaching staff, who's the guys that have grown the most with with you since you came here, too? >> Well, I got to talk about our coordinators first. You know, Brad's doing a fantastic job of just putting the whole thing together, building concepts off of concepts, making sure guys are prepared to go out there and um you know, in our move the ball uh periods and situations, you know, one of the critical things is make sure you get that call in early. and he's been on top of the personnels's, the DNDs, and and doing a great job of maintaining that rhythm. Um, I love just where where E's got the defense and the guys talking and communicating, uh, troubleshooting different concepts, run concept, pass concepts. You know, there's a lot of familiar language that's carryover. And so, I feel a lot of preparation there. And then with Tracy, just continuing to push the envelope. We do some things different um, in some of our phases than a lot of teams. And I love that. It keeps the guys engaged and you know there's a point where what when you start to master the the basics and the core of what you're doing. It's so important that we push our guys and we throw new concepts at them, throw different ways to cover kicks, to return kicks. It keeps them um interested in it and it's fun and uh challenging at the same time. So he's done a great job of just you know bringing that unit together. So, it's really just all three phases. The the level of comfortability that I have with these guys that we've been working with together to build here's how we play and then here's what we do. And we've captured all those things at this point right now. And the challenge for us is can we make sure that that shows up every single day and that's always where I'll be pushing them. >> We asked Dan, I I don't think we've asked you about any the thought of perhaps bringing in a a fourth quarterback sometime between now and I don't middle of August. >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean it's it's always on our radar. Um we're looking for how we can make that fit in. As we all know, we have a number of guys that we're counting on to come back to us in short order. And then there's a couple of guys that'll be back further down in the future. But because of those guys, they all count towards our 90man roster. It makes it really challenging to carry four quarterbacks when we have depth concerns at at some other positions just to throw a practice. So, we have to keep that in mind. But we're always looking. We're always looking at all the different positions because we have to be ready, you know, when when this is or that kind of show up throughout camp. We got to be ready to pivot and bring people in. >> Last question. >> Everybody good? >> Good. >> Thank you, coach. >> All right. Thank you. >> Yeah. Heat. Are you ready? >> here. Bring it up. Down here. Fire away, guys. Dave was talking a second ago about kind of your impact on the defense as a whole specifically with the the linebacker room you've got. How are you trying to help whether it's Tra, whoever it is through this process? >> Yeah, for sure. Um I mean every day, you know, we're obviously uh very critical of what we put on film, how we attack the weight room, you know, even just talking about little things off the field. So, um, every day we're all looking to improve. Um, you know, and, uh, it's really just, you know, being honest and evaluating ourselves every day. That's really what it comes down to. >> We read about your your film session with Luke Keequley. Can you tell us a little bit about that and um, how it came to fruition and maybe some of the things you you picked up from him? Yeah. So, um, obviously him being, you know, somebody who's going to Hall of Fame this year and, you know, everything I heard, he was a great person, somebody I reached out to. So, I texted him, um, you know, a couple weeks ago and, uh, this is actually before I left for the break and while I was gone, um, for a little bit, you know, we plan on a date for me to meet with him when I came back. And so that's what we did. Um, and he's just really responsive and, uh, you know, just he's a guy that loves ball. So, I'm grateful um, that he was willing to do that. And hopefully, you know, I'm pretty sure it won't be the last time. Um, but it was great. You know, we really just talked about leadership. We talked about ball, talked about life a little bit. Really just um just trying to find that 1% to, you know, take my game to the next level on and off the field. Um, and it it was a great talk. >> What was that film session like? I I assume that you both are uh you both study the game, but just tell me a little bit about the film session. Yeah, I mean we were just talking ball. Uh some technique. Uh just some on the field, just overall awareness type stuff. Um just talking ball, you know. I mean, we talked good about um just just everything. It wasn't just one specific thing. Just went over we threw on a game and just basically, hey, what do you see on this play? Okay, you know, what do I see on this play kind of thing and just went through the went through the tape. >> Did you watch a lot of Luke Kiku growing up? >> I watched a good amount. Yeah. I mean, you know about his highlights and when I was growing up, I mean, film wasn't um really accessible for me up until I got to college. Uh but definitely saw a lot of his highlights growing up. >> Because how much of that were you aware of before getting here? How much more aware of it are you after being here? >> Yeah, I knew about Luke. I knew about Thomas Davis. Um and then Sam Mills, you know, I learned more about the guys obviously, um Dan and John B. I mean, Shaq, you know, you go down the line and you look at the history of the linebackers, and I know I missed a couple, but um I I learned more about it as I came here, but I already knew about some of the main stays, some of the the big names. Um and then looking at it even deeper as I, you know, um was here a little longer, you really realize, yeah, like, yeah, there's a lineage of of great linebacker play, and that's special to be a part of. And I want to just continue to do everything I can to to be the best player I can be, best leader, best everything I can for this team. to carry on that torch. >> Do you do you let yourself think about it that often and I guess like take on that pressure or do you have to kind of put it out of sight, out of mind once you're on the field and not worrying about it? >> I don't think about it until you guys bring it up. Um I mean for me it's just attacking the process every day and ultimately it doesn't really matter. Like I don't focus on anything outside. I don't go on social media. It's especially right now it's really just every, you know, second of the day, how can I get better? Um, and just being uh efficient with my time really is what it is. Like time is valuable. So, just making sure that I'm always doing something to, you know, take that one step in the right direction. >> On that note, can Alice mentioned that like you've got your training figured out. How long did it take you to figure it out and what was the process of getting there? >> I'd say it really took three years going into my fourth season. So last off season all the way up throughout the really just all of last year was really the first time like from the end of the 2024 season start of that off season, excuse me, all the way through is really when I kind of found my process and I just needed some refining throughout the years. Um and that really just comes from learning uh what my body needs, what my mind needs, what my spirit needs in order to uh really it's it's a lifestyle. It's not even just necessarily about um training camp or the season like it's um a lifestyle. So just just finding the best way to do something that's sustainable for me. >> Understanding that um pads haven't even come on yet in training camp so far. How good could this defense be? Dave just talked about how the defense was dominant the first two days of training camp and so on. Um h how how would you approach that question? Yeah, I mean I don't like to overpromise and underdel, but I do have um very high expectations. I'm very optimistic about what we can be. Um I mean it's been a great competitive last four days of training camp. OTAAS, same thing. Uh now we're playing real ball. Next time we come out when we put the pads on and then that's when we can get an even better gauge. But I will say that it's been very competitive on our our side of the ball and for us um especially once we get everybody back healthy. Um and we're at full strength. You know, it's going to be very difficult to deal with us when we're doing what we need to do. And you know, I think we're going to be able to do that. >> As a vet coming into a new system, um you're probably instantly a leader in that linebacker room. It could be takes some time to find your voice as a leader. Have you found that voice and and what has that process been like working with Trevan and and the other guys in the room? >> Yeah, I would say so for sure and that just comes from uh building the relationships with the guys on the team which has been super easy. I mean from top to bottom the whole roster um just just so much love in that locker room and uh just grateful for for all the guys offense, defense, special teams, whatever it is. He's he's done uh he's done something this offseason, but he's been really really good at uh both so far. How much of it hasn't been the same since you guys have known him for a few years? >> Mhm. He sets our goals for every beginning of practice. Let's get to work. We got focus on what you can focus on. Just get better today. And he preaches to the young guys. He picks young guys up with him. And um it's it's awesome to see because he's a dude who works for that. >> Appreciate y'all.

Like I feel like I'm the strongest I've ever been right now. So it just gave me time to really work on myself in the inside and out. >> Was there a point where you thought maybe you wouldn't play anymore? >> Uh just knowing myself. I just knew when I when I had my mind set on something, my mind set and I just looked at it as adversity and I I never I've always been the type to look adversity in the face and to just tell him like I'mma conquer you. Like so nah, like maybe them thoughts creeped in a little bit, but when they did, I just knew it was the devil. So I knew that God had big plans for me. So I knew that I'll come back. >> When stuff like that happen to change a person? >> Yeah. >> Has it changed you and in what ways? And then how did it feel to to come back and and be back on the field that first practice? >> Oh yeah, it changed me just gratitude wise. Uh when I first came back out here, I I damn near almost cried. I went on a uh I went on the ground, took a knee, just start praying cuz stuff like that when it gets taken from you, you think it's gone. It really hurt, man. It really do. >> We saw yesterday emotions team watching it go down and you talk obviously what you went through last year. You say there was guys who were in your corner. Yeah. >> Is there anyone in particular within this locker room who really helped guide you through what you went through last >> Yeah, just all the guys. Uh even when I would come in here and I'll just be in a crazy mood. I'll just be like, "Dang, man." Like, I just don't know what's going to happen next. Uh just all the guys, they be cracking jokes and it just made me feel so much better. And like I just started looking forward to like waking up in the morning and getting up and just coming in here and just being around my team. And it just like all of them, even coach AC, all the other coaches, just seeing everybody smiling, it just made me feel better. Just lifted up my spirits. >> You getting emotional talking about it right now? >> I really am a little bit. I'm not going to lie. Just cuz it's just like God is so good. Like just everything he do like he could just like you just never know. Like he could just bring you through whatever and you lean on him, you going to be okay. So it's definitely getting me a little emotional for sure. You said to us earlier that her especially [snorts] last year knows you felt like you're going to have a big year. >> What are you trying to hoping to show this year that you that you're going to show last year? >> Uh I'm hoping to show more. Uh really just come out healthy and just show everybody what I could really do. Uh I was in Minnesota for a long time behind a lot of great players most of my career. So it felt like last year was like my chance to really uh really show everybody. And I felt like when I started to heat up that happened. So it kind of hit me at like a hard time. And it just Yeah. It was hard for real. What was your game day routine when you were hurt? Like were you trying to come to the games here or did you want to be away and just watch at home? >> Yeah. No, my game day routine I would uh I didn't look at as a as a uh opportunity feel bad for myself. I looked at as opportunity for improvement. So I come in here, I work out. I work my ass off. I've been there for like two, three hours really just working. Like people would see me in there working. I really just had to get that pain off me. And I really just had to really just work and work. And I would love coming to the games cuz I felt like Nick when he was doing good, I was trying my best just to help him and to just pour everything I had into him. So when I seen how good Nick was doing, it just truly made me feel good. So I just I would just always be at the games just trying to support him and just help him out >> before games on Sundays or did you meet during the week? >> No, it was before the games on Sundays. I'll come in here early and I'll work out because I knew I had a big journey ahead of me. So I really put everything I had into it. And uh you you were next to Princeley last year. I don't know if you still are, but obviously he's got a great sense of humor, great energy. >> You brought up how guys would crack jokes and and do that stuff. How what >> what benefit does the group have with him, not just on the field, but from a personality standpoint, and how have you seen him respond to last year this off season? Yeah, I mean Princeley Princeley is one of those guys like he don't he don't necessarily talk too much but when he does it's always hilarious and he kind of the type of person he'll make you laugh without like even saying anything and it's just he's just a very unique individual and just playing out there with him you know he he talented so it's just it's going to be cool. you saw some of your workout videos um during the off season. >> Take us through what that was like and and and um the the grind that it was physically to to get back to where you were. >> Yeah, it was hard. Um I worked out a lot. Uh I probably work out at least two times a day. Uh when I'm really getting it in, I hit three times, three workouts a day. But uh I just knew I had a big journey ahead of me. So I just knew what I had to do. And that's really like all I did. I just dedicated like everything I had to it cuz I knew if I didn't if the moment came I I knew I had to take it. >> Off of that. Was there anything particular about your game that you wanted to kind of focus a little bit more on on that time off? >> Yeah. I just wanted to become like just just really fix everything. I had so much time off. It wasn't necessarily just one thing I wanted to focus on. I just wanted to fix everything. I definitely learned a lot. Uh, I can say my football IQ is probably the highest it's ever been just because I literally had to sit back and just watch for a whole year. So, I I learned like so much. I could go out there, read plays. Most of the plays I could see him before they even happened. Uh, just stuff like that. >> You mentioned like you know what he's about to go through it. Is there like a piece of advice or one thing you share with him maybe above all what he's about to go through the next year? >> Yeah. Uh, I actually just talked to him. I told him, I said, "Bro, you pretty much this a time like the main thing you got to focus on right now." I told him, I said, "This is time you got to take about you." I told him, I said, "When you're when you're down right now, you got to take this time about you. You got to make sure your leg get back right. Then you got to build yourself up internally first and then make sure your mind's right and then you got to get yourself physically back." And you really just got to lean on God. Do you have any specific uh personal goals or number of sacks or pressures that you uh are setting for yourself? >> Uh I have really big goals. I do I have really big goals this year. Uh cuz I I believe I could do a lot uh just from coming back off my injury and overcoming that adversity and my mindset. I could feel like I could do anything I put my mind to after defeating that. So my goals I don't really want to put no number on it. Whatever God has for me, God has for me and I'm gonna let God handle that. >> How much slimmer? Are you slimmer? >> I did. I worked out a lot. I'm the same weight though. I just dropped some I dropped a lot of body fat and got a chance to just recmp my body. >> How How much does rushing inside kind of help your rhythm in the game kind of moving around and being able to do that because not a lot of the guys can rush outside inside? >> I love doing it. Uh I could just find different mix matches. Uh I could really put pressure on those guards when I get off get off the ball fast. Uh, really just get them moving, get them on the island. I feel like it allows me to just go and you're really closer to the quarterback, too. >> For sure. All right, y'all have a good one. >> Hey, >> what up? What up? >> Listen, you told us that you gained some weight, but you know, we just had to see until now. Fans are just kind of getting a full look at I guess kind of like your recmped body for season. >> I mean, I don't know. So, this is just what I played at in college. So, I just feel a lot more comfortable at, you know, the weight I'm at right now. And I'm I feel a lot bigger, stronger, faster, and I'm moving well right now. So, um, so the added weight was was good for sure. >> What's the difference coming in year two when you're more comfortable with everything and as opposed to last year's? >> Uh, I mean, first off, the standard the standards are higher obviously. Um, you know, just coming off of, uh, entering the playoffs and, um, one year with Bryce, chemistry is a lot different. um a lot more confident Bryce has in me and we all have in each other. So um you know I'm just looking forward to year two and and what it brings. >> Are you noticing any differences with with with Brad as as coordinator? I know it's early and but are you noticing any type of differences in play calls? Uh, I mean, at the end of the day, the playbook is still the same, but um, obviously, you know, I feel like coach Canales and and co uh, Coach Brad, you know, they feed off each other, you know, as far as their ideas, their opinions. So, um, on the field, I think it's just both of them at the end of the day. >> T-Mac, you had a chance to go back to the island. You had a backpack giveaway. Can you talk about your foundation and just being able to go back and um, and give back to that community? Yeah, obviously, you know, that's a blessing just being able to um start my foundation, but also, you know, launch it in, you know, the city that I'm from, uh, you know, my people. So, just did a little backpack giveaway, like you said, and, um, just being able to see the the the smiles it puts on, not really the kids, but the the parents as well. So, um, you know, obviously being that that role model, that light, um, that little kids can look up to, even uh, grown-ups. Um, you know, that's a blessing. backing off of that um with the role model uh piece of it. You saw the stories about the camp and the miscommunication with uh sports flex flex sports. Just I want to just kind of give you a chance to kind of speak on that and just kind of tell people what happened and how that kind of fell apart. >> Yeah, I mean I don't want anybody think that I don't like kids or anything like that. You know, I I love the kids. Um, obviously, you know, they're the next generation, so um, try to give back as much as possible, but u, yeah, I don't know where I came from. I never committed to that. So, um, but, you know, I I look forward to seeing all the kids that expected me to be at that camp either at a game or come out to a practice or, you know, just so I can make up for it. >> So, where did the miscommunication happen? >> I have no idea. I I I wish I knew. You said you had never committed to it. >> Sounds like you'd like kids to come. >> I don't know. Come to a game or one second. >> Yeah. I mean, for sure. You know, obviously there's there's a lot of people that wait for us on the practice either before practice or after practice. So, um, you know, just stop by or, you know, just come to the game, uh, fill up the Bank of America Stadium, do whatever we can just to give back. I just want to clarify, was it camp at AC riddles in Asheville? >> I have no idea where it was. >> You mentioned the chemistry in the Bryce and the past year and everything that goes along with that. What's something that that you know now that you didn't know a year ago or that you might tell yourself a year ago like this is what you're going to learn your first season? >> Uh, sure. You know what I mean? Just just as anything, you know, anything new that you start, you know, you obviously tiptoe into it. You're not really um very confident. You know, I feel like I'm a lot more confident just, you know, in my speed, my mind, just confident in Bryce and and the play calling and my teammates. So, um I feel like that's that's one thing that I told myself last year is just, you know, just be confident. You don't have to be you don't have to do everything. You just just be you really. T, what do you think about Chris Rogers so far? That was you just a year ago, uh, being the rookie in the receiving room, and he's starting to look pretty good so far. >> No, for sure. I like Chris a lot. And, um, you know, outside of him being a good player, he's a good person. You know, he he brings light into that room. Um, you know, he likes to joke around, have fun. He's still a little kid at the end of the day, but, you know, when it comes to the field, he he takes care of business. So, I'm looking forward to playing alongside of him for sure. Do you think meadow allows you to play a little bit more in the slot person? >> Um, who knows? I'm not too sure. You know, I I don't know what um the coaches have planned for me in this in this offense. So, um but whatever whatever chance I get to to make to have opportunities to get the ball, you know, I'm all for it. So, um looking forward to it for sure. >> You said like about a kid when you just said that uh in response to do you feel older now coming into this new season? Do you feel like a sense of, "Oh, I'm a little bit more more better and more confident." >> Yeah, for sure. I I don't care what anybody says. I'm a vet now. So, but I mean, yeah, for sure. Just having one uh one year under my belt. Um and I was fortunate enough to play all 18 games last year, which is, you know, uncommon. So, um you know, I have a lot of experience and um you know, I try my best to just, you know, give some knowledge, give some wisdom, at least the knowledge and wisdom that I have to all the younger guys. Um, Bryce Bryce said yesterday that you and him got a chance to work out together a lot this summer and stuff like this. What was the nature of those workouts and what did you learn about it? >> Uh, shoot. It was really just, you know, it was just playing football at the end of the day, just trying to get that that timing right, you know. Um, and, you know, it it's definitely translated on the field. Um, I was definitely surprised by some of the things that he's been doing a couple uh these last few days. So, um, it feels good though. you know, the chemistry is, you know, it's black and white right now. So, there's no gray area. Um, and we look good right now. So, hopefully we can continue this. >> You came in as part of the same draft class obviously with Nick. How difficult was that and emotional yesterday both on a personal level and just from team stand? I mean, for sure. That's obviously a big loss for us, but you know, at the end of the day, it gives somebody a chance to step up, and I'm sure we have a lot of young guys and vet guys that can that can do the job just as well as he did. So, um, obviously that hurt, but um, at the end of the day, we all got to go, you know, we all want to pursue something. We all want to go somewhere. So, um, you know, and I'm I'm sure Nick understands that and he, you know, he he's he's uh he's with us, you know, we're with him and we're praying for him for sure. and everyone else had that emotional scene where you you spoke to him or dapped him up before he left. Did you have any specific message for him then or or in the hours since? >> Uh so I mean now I didn't really get the chance to talk to him. I tried to be you know optimistic as far as you know before his imaging or whatever whatever the case may be. But you know just uh man just be confident just you know God never makes a mistake you know even though he's out for the season. Um, he'll be out for a while, you know, just, you know, it happened for a reason. You know, God, like they say, God gives his toughest battles to his his toughest I don't I don't even know, but you know what I mean. But >> but no, right. Exactly. I I got lost. But, you know, just you know, just uh you know, stay prayed up. That's it. >> Does it feel different? Do you feel you know, a little more grown, man? >> Man, I've been grown. No, but uh I guess it feels a little different just as far as my confidence. Um you know, and obviously as far as the team as well. You know, they they've seen this pasture what I'm able to bring to the team. Uh what what I'm able to do for everybody. So, um feel like they're a lot more confident in me as well. >> A chance to look back and what you did last year and you kind of appreciate what you did. I know you're never happy. you always said that, but and any goals numerically uh statistically this year? >> Uh no, I'm I mean I I didn't get a chance to really take a look at what I did last year. And to be honest, I don't really care. But uh you know, I just want to be um better for the team this year. Um you know, we we obviously, like I said in in the beginning of this interview, you know, the standard is set a lot higher. So, um, everybody's holding everybody to a higher standard. So, just looking forward to meet the expectations or exceed them. >> Personal goals, stats. >> I don't got any. >> I was going to ask if you could expound on your advice to yourself about just being you.
