It sounds like an easy thing, but probably a difficult thing. What helped you to get there, or do you feel like you have? Uh, I mean, I try to I pride myself in being myself, being authentic. Uh, so I feel like I, you know, I did a good job as far as coming in, uh, just being who I am, you know, being the guy that, you know, they picked, uh, being the guy that they brought to the team. So, um, so I'm going just try to continue that. But as far as just the younger guys, just, you know, just be yourself as far as, um, you know, they they picked you for a reason. you know, I'm sure they picked you obviously for the ability the abilities you have on the field, but um you know, just a light that you can bring be to the locker room, be to your your room. Um and you know, I got to give a big shout out to the rookie so far. They they did a phenomenal job and um I I'm I'm excited to see what what happens for sure. >> You talked about you talked about your connection with Young. A lot of good plays out there today. Just how powerful do you believe this wide receiver can be? Uh, shoot. I mean, we we're pretty good. Uh, I feel like we we're we're very slept on. You know, we have a lot of guys that may not have got the opportunities past couple years or even the rookies that haven't got any opportunities yet, but you know, I'm looking forward to seeing what the future holds for us. And, you know, I'm excited. I'm excited. We're going to make plays this year. >> Thanks, man. >> All right, y'all. Appreciate it. Oh,

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: [music] >> back on. Heard some great things about this summer off season. Josh Stinks, Danny Callington talking about the group that was here working together. Unprecedented in my 17 years in the NFL to hear that there was, you know, I think the most we had one day there in the summer is about 36 guys. Um And what does that mean? I don't know. I just know that they like being here. They like being together, working together. I know that that means something. So, and a lot of guys were other places training hard as well. So, this is nothing against that, but I do know that that's something special that we're doing something here. And I really give Josh and Danny and the crew a lot of credit because those are the the guys that they're primarily working with. And they have that trust for them to get prepared for the season. >> What did you see >> when Nick went down? >> I honestly I haven't I was looking at the other side of the field. You know, I just heard him go down. They're they're going to take him and go get imaging this afternoon and we'll have more information on that. >> To see the entire roster kind of come off the field after a drill to go see him. What does that say about how tight this locker room is? But also the magnitude of what this this injury could do for this team? >> Yeah, they care about each other. You know, this is whenever you're in a group of people doing something hard together. You know, it's it's has a way of creating a special bond and you know, between all the workouts and going through a full season and off season and all that, you know, it means something to the guys and I'm proud of that. I'm proud of the fact that you know, the first thought in guys minds isn't you know, are we going to have Nick for the season? It's how is Nick doing? You know, and guys are checking on him. And so, again, as we have more information, we'll let you know what that is. >> Do you know if it was his knee? Can you tell us anything? >> It was his right knee and they're going to look at that and get some imaging and then and we'll let you know once we have more. >> I'd never ask you to speculate, but you always hear this expression. Players know when or at least usually know when they think it's not great. Was that your kind of Did you feel that on the field at all? >> I I don't want to speculate. I'm hoping for the best. Um and so, we'll just get the full imaging and before we make any, you know, announcements that way. >> You made the call to stop practice in that moment. What went into that decision? >> Well, I just know how much these guys mean to each other and and um if we go up there and I go up in front of the guys and preach, you know, the fact that we we lead with love and respect and connection and relationship, you know, this moment, while we can certainly move the drill and and keep the practice going, you know, we had enough time. Um Jeff and I kind of talked about We had enough time in the practice to just, you know, to get a kickoff and everybody come up and just make sure that they send them some love, you know, for um who knows. Who knows Who knows what it is, but um it's a chance for the guys to connect and I wanted to make sure they had a chance to do that. >> And whatever comes out of that, can you just talk about what that can do to that linebacker position? >> We got guys. Um that's why we keep bringing in uh depth and and talent and different guys, you know, it's Jaelan Phillips in that room. Pat Jones is back and Princely's coming along and we got a whole group of guys that we're counting on. And so, you know, if it comes to that, we have guys that we trust and and we're going to ask to do different things, but let's hold off on that until we know what's what's going on. >> Uh Jonathan Brooks' first-ever training camp practice in his career. Uh it seems like you gave him a lot of work. How did he look out there? Uh how excited are you about how he attacked this entire rehab process getting here? >> Really looking forward to um just the hard work that JB has had to do over the last couple of years to get him to this point. He feels great. He feels strong. He looks fast. Um he looks like the guy that I remember and I'm really excited for that, but more so just uh for a guy to go through things and and to be able to have the emotional mental resiliency to go through that training twice um to get himself back, you know, this is a celebration and um you can feel the gratitude on him. You can feel the focus and uh how important this opportunity is for him. >> You guys brought back Brady Christensen last week. Obviously, he's not on NFI or pup. Where is he at physically after I think he was last year? >> He looked good. He practiced today was an individual, took a couple of reps and you know, brought him in for his physical and he looks as strong as ever and he's excited. He's he's we're excited to have him back of course as you all seen over the last couple of years the versatility he brings, you know, and then of course with you know, Teemo not being available just his versatility and depth there and and of course, you know, drafting Monroe having Stone Forsythe in the building all things that we didn't know. We didn't know what to expect. We just know on the offensive line or wherever you're at in football, you know, it's good to have guys that are familiar with your system and the guys that you can trust. >> How do you feel about the rookies and the way they're blending in? It seems like he's getting real comfortable on the sideline there. >> Yeah, you know, what's interesting is is just looking at the full group. It doesn't feel like there's a lot of rookies. You know, I know we added a full draft class and and free agents and all that but it feels like a bunch of guys who have been around us and know what to expect and it makes it a lot easier for the rookies to just kind of blend in and you know, find their space knowing we don't need them to be vocal right now. We just need you to do your job and and earn that trust and respect from your teammates. So I think that takes a that takes a lot of pressure off of the guys to be able to just go out and focus on their job and perform. So >> Monroe has experience playing on the right side but moving him over as a rookie, how do you not sort of overload him? >> Yeah, we you know, going into it obviously with with Teemo not being available to us for a for a certain amount of time. We just kind of evaluated the group and you know, we feel great about Rashid and Rashid's played high quality football for a long time at left and um I think Rashid could play in different positions as well. Starting off with the rookie, you want to let a guy focus in on on one way on one spot or another, you know, and we gave him a little bit of exposure Monroe in the spring just playing on both sides and really, you know, he and I had a conversation and I don't mind telling you this, but just said, you know, I in in my mind I wanted him Monroe to go out there earn the job, win the job and now we're in a situation we need him to go now and we have guys behind him that can offer that depth part, but he didn't blink and he starts smiling and he even said, you know, at one point in the summer you know, just he and Rob who were some of the guys working out together and Rob was like you should come play over next to me and just kind of recruiting him to play on that right side. Can you imagine those two monsters next to each other? So we're excited about it, you know, and and there'll be a learning curve on either side for him and so we made that decision and felt good about the group by leaving Rashid at left and having Monroe go over to right. >> Inkum, T-Mac, Trevon Wallace, Ben Martin Scott all were pretty limited during OTAs. Are they all full go? Are they all ready to go? And if so, what did you see from T-Mac today during team drills? >> Yeah, these guys have been cleared. They were pretty healthy coming out of the spring. So but we were again just being a little cautious with the red jersey just trying to make sure that they can get fully strong and stable and you know, they just you know, fell right into the group and flew around as far as I could tell. Again, I'm going to go and watch the practice right now and dive into the details of it, but I'm really encouraged by just the way that they went out there and attacked it and and you know, T-Mac looked great, you know, and he's he's gotten stronger and he knows the system and that was one thing I'll comment to you which is on the offensive side. First and foremost just watching them come out of the huddle. There wasn't a lot of uncertainty. Guys that are familiar with the system where to line up, what we're trying to get done. I could feel that. I could feel the tempo and there's just there's an attacking mindset. There is there's an aggressiveness. When you know, then you can just go out there and play free and play fast and that's what it felt like and on the defensive side just kind of taken a quick snapshot of what it felt like out there just having Devin in the middle of that defense bringing them together getting things communicated quickly before they take the field getting together having that focus for this play for this rack for this period it's great to have that kind of energy and that juice out there and I could feel that was a noticeable a noticeable feeling that I got from Devin and his leadership out there and so I was excited really about both groups where we're at just on day one to be able to capture the way we practice the speed with which which way that we practice and then the preparation and guys knowing what to do. >> The first practice feel for you without the responsibility of play calling. >> It was great just bouncing around you know just I got a you know a group of guys that I you know certainly have my eye on and I'm I'm going share that but I just come trying to test myself with making sure that I can affect not just the coaching staff but a couple of players you know that I really want to challenge to take steps and take strides and so going into each practice with that mindset I feel can really you know sharpen my focus on a couple of guys and then be able to see the whole thing but Brad did an excellent job in in preparing these guys to the point where they came out and you know we had a really smooth pre-practice walk through and the guys were ready and then we hit the ground running in the team periods. >> Do you focus on change daily is that >> Yeah yeah it will and you know there's there's battles right there's there's depth battles there's starting position battles all those things that are happening and so I just want to make sure that I'm connected to those and then of course following back up after we watch the film with the staff this evening to just kind of process where we see the progression of our players. >> Do you have a better idea on the time tables for Diggy Turk and Matthew Golden? >> Not really >> optimistic with with Icky's recovery. But again, I don't know what that specific timetable looks like. Traditionally, this is a 9 to 12-month injury. So, somewhere in that zone. I just know that he's doing really well in his rehab. So, um and then with Teemo, um it's just a matter of of just continuing to have checkups and going through that. Same thing with uh Turk. You know, Turk has some some regularly scheduled checkups to make sure things are going in the right direction. But for the guys, I can say they're all doing as much as they could possibly can. Um they're itching to get back. And I know that we're going to have to hold them back from wanting to come back too early from this or that. You know, we just have to be really smart with the process and just ask them to show up every day and, you know, just go through their routine and and whatever being asked of them and um just keep taking the next step in their recovery. >> When would you expect to see these guys? >> Uh JC pretty quickly. Um it was uh it was a laceration. So, you know, there's it was uh as good as it could be, I guess, from from what the injury was. But he was out there doing some things today. Um he was backpedaling and uh there wasn't a lot of change of direction. Just trying to be smart with it cuz it's it's pretty fresh. But um we're optimistic we'll get him back in, you know, in the next couple of weeks. >> What have you seen out of rookie Chris Brazwell since OTAs? >> Yeah, speed. Um again, you know, wrestling with the concepts, wrestling with where to be and what time to get to this route and that. Um that's natural. That's a normal part of this. But you know, he had made a great play today. You know, kind of got up in the air. Mike Jack on the sideline carried him out of bounds. So, beautiful play on both guys. The high point 6'4 guy running down the field like we thought he could. And then, of course, the veteran Mike Jack just kind of carrying him out of bounds in a very legal way. It was a brilliant play. So, but I love that he brings that element to our offense. I believe that that can and things up for T-Mac, for Coker, uh for Xavier. And um you know, when Chris gets his chance, you know, as he tells us he's ready for roles, we'll continue to give him roles. Um so, I'm excited for him this camp. >> Okay, with the preseason game and the two joint practices, what is your balance for making sure guys get live reps during the preseason, but also not overworking guys? >> Just trying to have a uh a certain amount of in-game reps goals for each guy. Not every two guys are the same. Speaking to the starters first and foremost. Um some guys need to play a little bit more. Some guys may not need to play as much, but I would like all of them to get a good dose of that. The science says the more that they're exposed to those game time reps, the the more likely they are to be uh durable as you go into the beginning part of the season. Just having even in the joint practices, which I think are gold, and because we can control them, and uh the the cup the couple of teams that we're practicing with, we have a lot of familiarity. I have a lot of familiarity with those coaches, and we practice similar. So, we're very accustomed to that physical type of nature and and all that. But, even with those practices, we all know when it's game time and those lights are on or that ball's kicked off and there's fans there, it goes up another notch. And um that's the nature of it, and you want to be able to expose your team to a good dose of that. Um how much that is, I think that'll be a week-to-week decision. >> Coach, I'm sorry, one more real quick. >> Yep. >> Coach, the uh one of the biggest sports event just wrapped up, the World Cup. Did you get a chance to watch it with the guys? And who watched which game? Did you watch that? What's your reaction to this? >> We didn't watch it together as a team, but my family, we were certainly following it and uh watched it with friends and family, but it's really inspiring to see a group of guys come together uh who all play on different teams most of the rest of their careers um who can rally together in pursuit of a goal. And uh that part certainly will be used in our team meetings, um Um, Saturday night meetings, and just uh the ability in a short amount of time to all be connected on a common goal and uh that was exciting. And also to just see, you know, watching Argentina and watching the resiliency in the finish, um the way that they were able to finish strong in most of their games till the last one. Um but, you know, they played with a lot of passion and um and they never made an assumption about who's going to win the game early on in the first half or even in the 70th minute. They didn't make an assumption even if they were behind, you just keep playing. And what a great message and something that I try to share with our team. Let's not make an assumption on what's going to happen good or bad with this game, let's just keep playing until there's no time left. And so, that was a really good uh example and a lesson for all of us. >> All right, thank you, coach. >> All right, thank you. >> Thanks, Jay. >> [music] >> All right, welcome back. Um it's great to be back going. Heard some great things about >> How's everyone doing? Good. Good. Doing good. Yeah. >> About how you got that news and your and your response to it being thrust into this role as a rookie. >> Yeah, you know, it was probably like last week they told me um you know, after they found out the news of Teemo that I'd be working on the the right side and you know, I was really just psyched for the opportunity. So, any anywhere they would have put me I would have been happy to go and you know, it's just how it is now like I got to step up and be ready. >> Okay, coach Allen kind of recruits you to the right side. What [clears throat] was that What is that relationship like between you two? >> Yeah, like after um they found out like the Teemo uh news, he just kept on saying cuz he was here working out and I was here working out. And you know, every single day he's like, "Hey, you're coming with me. Like you're coming to my side. Like I'm going to I'm going to talk to them." And I don't know if he did talk to them or not, but you know, I texted him whenever I found out the news and I was like, "Hey, you got you got what you wanted. Let's work." >> Bro, you told us in the spring that obviously you have experience on both sides, more on the left. But what is your com- comfort and confidence level on that right side? >> Yeah, I think it's just you know, for me it's just flexibility. Might take a few practices or whatever just to get flexible cuz a lot to do with ankle flexibility, hip flexibility, but you know, at the end of the day it's just football. So, I'm going to go and do the same thing I was doing on the left side, just playing ball. >> Guys, where do you feel like you've made the biggest strides in your game since coming in and what are some of the main things that you work on now as you take this big step? >> Uh a lot of it is just you know, getting out especially cuz I'm going over this right side is just still staying just as explosive and also um my hand placement and also just you know, watching film and knowing my opponents and who I'm going against and everything like that and really just my preparation too, you know, I'm a pro now. I don't have to go to school anymore. So, I'm taking all that time and dedicating it to my craft. >> Speaking of school, did it feel like the first day of school today with being in your you know, first training camp? How would you explain the first day uh for training camp? >> I mean, it's awesome that it rained, but I know it's going to get hotter for sure. Uh it's been awesome, you know, it kind of felt like OTA part two, but the intensity's definitely uh picked up a little bit and you know, I'm excited for all the competition and just being around the guys for extended extended period of time, so. >> You've known Taylor a short time. What's it like kind of living through this with him and and having those conversations about A his health and and B how he's helping you? >> Yeah, he's super helpful. I mean, he I sit in the right next to him in the meeting room and so, you know, it's always been the days he hasn't practiced, whenever he had the vet days we'd be talking the most and I think they might have already gave him a warning about not to talk so much in meetings, but um he he's in my corner all the time and I actually went golfing with him and Luke Fortner one time and you know, getting outside of the football, you know, environment has been good to just kind of get to know him. >> said he would be around you'd be able to be around. How important is that over these next couple of weeks um until he's he's back to his >> I mean, having someone that's been there and played extensive amount of games and you know, has all that experience is awesome. Just having him in my corner, any question I have, technique and him even just watching my reps and I can come and ask somebody cuz I know coaches have to watch a lot. Just having somebody in my corner kind of throughout this whole process and you know, new position really um it's good. >> Why did you make the decision Go ahead. >> Is he like talking to you about football or is he like distracting you or >> [laughter] >> It's So, sometimes it's both like maybe I'll have like a bad rep or something, he'll crack a joke about it, but it's all lighthearted and he he keeps me focused. Whenever there's something that he thinks I should work on, he's going to let me know. So, it's kind of a you know, good relationship. Just lighthearted, but also like he's got my best interest in mind. >> Why did you make the decision to stay here this summer and train? >> Really, it's like I wanted number one, you know, get to know the city I'm going to be living in and also it's like it's an easy decision just to be in the environment and just kind of get used to the day-to-day. Especially, you know, we had so many guys here working out and then just being around the guys and Rob was there, too. So, you know, I didn't know that I get to go play next to him, but the fact that I stayed and we got to work out together, I think it's good to just, you know, get the camaraderie and work together with all the guys. >> Are you a little leaner than when we saw you in the spring? >> Uh not really. I might be a little heavier. I think I might be sitting at like 325. Fluctuating 330, 320, so definitely a little heavier. >> Everybody good? >> Monroe, yeah, I believe you were on the field when the injury happened today to Nick Bosa. Um did you see it happen? And but then also just in general, can you speak on how that impacted the vibe among the players? >> I mean, you hate to see it anytime anybody gets injured, you know. I didn't really see what happened, but, you know, I'm praying for him and I'm hoping he gets better and, you know, the whole team is just going to rally around him and it just gives us more of a reason to fight to be a better team. >> All right. >> Thank you. >> Thank you all. >> I know. >> Hello. >> Hello everyone. How's your first day at camp? Good turnout today. Definitely. Of course. Miss you guys. Anyone any updates? Anyone major life milestones? Anything uh Talk Congratulations. Congratulations. Anyone else? >> Empty nester. >> Empty nester. Ah, is that a congratulations or is that a >> Yeah, check with me and the company. >> Yeah, fair enough. Me? Nah, I'm just happy to be here. Yeah. Nothing. Nothing. Oh, yeah. Um, yeah, I was that was a really really fun, really great opportunity. Um, myself and CJ and our foundations just able to give back to um to Pasadena. Um, everyone uh who was affected by eating fires and all the LA fires. Um, you know, I know it probably from the rest of world that feels like a really long time ago, but uh you know, that being you know, my community and having a lot of family, friends uh affected, you know, it's it's something that's still really ongoing, you know, a lot of people are in battles with insurance. A lot of people are still suffering from, you know, losing everything, you know, it's not a just, you know, uh you know, big news for a week and then go over, you know, a lot of people's lives they're they're still trying to adjust to the new normal. So, we just wanted to um be able to provide some resources, um have just a day of of fun and recognition and um community. So, yeah, very very grateful to be able to do that. >> Your um fourth training camp, fourth day one of training camp, how comfortable did you feel out there? >> Yeah, I feel great. Um, I'm I'm super excited for this team for this year. Um, I really just being able to come back here um and just be a part of this building. It it's special. The the locker room is special. Coaching staff is special. Everyone in front office, um just how we've been able to build and grow and evolve, um you know, now this being year four, it's been, you know, it's definitely been a a blessing to be able to see that and be a part of that. Um, and I'm so excited for is just our mentality. Um, there's so much work for us to do, so much for us to to grow in, so much obviously day one of camp. So, there's so much that we have in front of us and I wouldn't want to, you know, face that with any other group. We all embody that. We all embrace that. We all are excited for that work. Um so, um I'm super super grateful to yeah, to be a part of that. >> You were right there when a couple of guys were gathering people up after the thing with Nick. What are those moments like for you guys as a team >> Um I mean Yeah, obviously just happened, you know, obviously don't know any details. Um but uh you know, Nick's our brother. It's when you see someone, you know see someone down, you know, it's just first off, it's human nature. You know, you I would just we all care. We all feel for him. Um obviously as athletes, we just you know, we all yeah, we're all just just praying for him. Uh we all are there for him. Um you know, it it speaks to how we all are in the locker room. Um but you know, obviously early, don't know anything or anything like that. It's just obviously we're just just praying. >> Bryce, did you see it happen? You were right there. >> Um Yeah, yeah, I didn't I was in on the play. So, um you know, I was looking down field and then obviously just saw him down. Um have an amazing medical staff. Um you know, great great doctors. Um so, you know, I'm certainly not a doctor, don't know anything, but we just just just praying over the the situation. >> Bryce, can you speak to just Nick's development as a leader on the practice field? >> Yeah. Um Yeah, Nick is it's been really cool just to see him coming to his own, to be comfortable, you know, obviously, you know, when you first get somewhere it's just you know, just a feeling out process and then over the that the time he's been here, just evolving the footprint he leaves in the locker room. Super high motor guy, great energy, um you know, fun to be around. Um and you know, he has that, you know, he it it he turns into that that different competitor when he's on the field and we feel that in practice. It's it's raised many a practice we've been in, you know, everyone's been, you know, matching that and we we match each other when stuff like that happens. So, um yeah, again, uh obviously don't don't know anything, >> But nothing changed totally but but but you mentioned sort of the size of of the community here. There's a lot of excitement, there's a lot of buzz around this team. Is that something you really feel in the off season and how do you approach things understanding that that this is a team that's looked at with a different lens? >> Um approach doesn't doesn't change. For us, uh coach talks about all the time in the meeting, it's about finding our best. Um you know, how people view us, how we're talked about, um you know, whatever that is, we can't control that. That's not something that we can, you know, we can we can base how hard we work or our mindset off of. We have to try to find our best every day. We have to, uh you know, search for right now just in training camp, having the best practice. Right now we get done having the best lift, having the best meeting. Um so regardless of what that is, um it doesn't affect our approach and I think our all of our guys feel the same way, which again I'm I'm grateful to be a part of. They all have that just keep it in the building, um have our best day we can mentality and coach did a great job of instilling that. >> John, you had a pass played down in the corner where it goes up and he gets it. What did you see on that one? What does that kind of show? >> Yeah, just trust. Um obviously it's just a one-on-one shot, just want to put it up there um where uh you know, my guy can make a play on it and for him to go up and get it like that. Um that that speaks to the player he is, the competitor he is. Um you know, I think especially now, um it's just great work. Mike Jack doing a great job of, you know, having the awareness and and pushing out of bounds. That's what camp's about, you know. Um you know, great great competitors going at it. Um I think all of that's going to make us better. Um CB's looked great. Um he's been working working super hard in in the off season. Um you could see him getting just more and more comfortable every practice. Him starting to think less and and and you know, when you get more reps at this level and this speed it just you see, you know, who he is just come out more and more and um we're super excited for for what he can bring. >> Winning the AFC South last year and end that playoff drought here and then, you know, take the Rams to the to the limit there. Um how much confidence does that give you guys going forward that you can kind of build you know, a championship? >> Yeah, we're super confident, but you know, that that doesn't come from any sort of looking at last year. That doesn't come from, you know, from that. We know it's a it's a new year. Um you know, it's a new page. That doesn't entitle us anything. Right now we feel like it's where we're building that confidence. You know, right now is where, you know, we feel like it's imperative for over these these next few weeks over the preseason. That's where we build the confidence to feel like heading to week one, you know, we're where we want to be. We we're, you know, we're we're able to, you know, I've take a week by week, but but just be in a good space. So I think that right now that's what what it's all about is making sure we can try to stack good days. We can try and stack good meetings. Um have the conversation we need to to build that confidence and whatever happened last year, you know, that doesn't entitle us to to anything and we all embrace that. >> Bryce, you and the Cardinals were the first teams to report. It's going to be a long camp with a couple of joint practices. What's your mindset as this this camp will look a a little different, be a little longer than last year? >> Yeah, just taking one day at a time. Um like you said, there's a couple of different moving parts. you know, you get the extra week. Um we're here. We got to, you know, take advantage of it. Um you know, we we we get that more time to compete. We get the, you know, for the young guys, they get time to more time to showcase what they can do, put out film, things like that. Um but for us uh coach talks about it all the time, just being where your feet are, taking it one day day time and regardless of all that stuff, um, you know, we're all just committed to having our best day, um, resetting, and then next day comes, and having to recommit again. >> This was Jonathan Brooks' first training camp practice of his entire career. Um, was it a Was it kind of You used the word joy uh in in the spring describing him and his return. Was it joyful again today, and did did he appear to be enjoying himself? >> Yeah, for sure. Um, yeah, I mean, just the way the way JB's been working ever since he got here, obviously, um, has dealt with a lot of adversity, and the way he's carried himself, the way he's been a pro about it, the way he's supported all of us, the positivity he's had despite, you know, having to deal with some some really difficult stuff. Um, I couldn't be happier to see him out there being himself, moving around, having fun, and yeah, and I think you see that in him, too. Um, he's so ready for the moment. It It's the work he's put in throughout the season. Um, you know, it's easy, especially, you know, last year, you're not playing the year, it's easy to just phone it in in practices, and when you're in, you know, you're in your two and a half, you know, it's two and a half hours into a meeting that you know you're not for a game you're not going to be in, it's easy to turn it off and and and just zone out. All last year, you could ask him anything. Um, yeah, game plan specific, playbook, whatever it is, and he would know exactly what was going on. He was that focused. So, you know, he's ready. Um, he's not over there trying to feel out certain plays or remember stuff. He's been putting the work in, so, um, we're all super excited for him to be back. >> Right. >> Last season, you guys had to deal with a lot of combination on the offensive line, uh kind of week in and week out, it felt like. How did that help you guys with the adaptability and knowing that you're going to have to go into this season with two new starters at tackle on that line? >> Yeah, I think it just it speaks to the culture of that room, um, the coaching staff, all of them. They hold themselves to an extremely high standard. Um, obviously, you know, football is a tough sport. Um, you know, last year there was, like you said, a lot of movement. We're going to have some stuff going into this year. Um, but they make sure that, you know, regardless of who might be be up, the standard is a standard. And, you know, I commend them for that. Um, that's themselves, you know, holding each other accountable. Um, hold themselves to again that standard. So, uh we know what it what it's going to be. I'm going to have all the confidence in the world in that group. >> the line and knowing that you kind of saw them piece it together last year like that? >> For sure. Yeah. Um, you know, I've always respected but even that, you know, you just just grow more respect for that group. So, yeah, definitely have all the confidence in the world. >> So, what are some takeaways um from today or what you've seen out there that you might want to put a little bit of focus on tomorrow? >> Um, well, first off, I love the way we competed. Um, day one of camp, first day back playing football for everyone for a while. It's you're going to have some, you know, some some ups and some downs. But, the way that both sides competed, the way that you could tell it it it means it meant something for everyone out there. Um, you know, you go out there, it's a little rainy. It's not what you think of for first day of camp. That not affecting the the pace or the tempo or the mindset, um, that's huge. Um, and then of course, there's some little X's and O's. There's, you know, route stuff that I can't wait to go over with the uh with with in the guys in in meetings. Um, you know, there there's little specific details and tempos and timings that, um, you know, you got to got to tweak and work on. But, that's what what camp is for. So, we're excited for that process. >> Coach has talked about the speed um just from Razzle and maybe opening up some of those other players. How have you seen this group just kind of improve? >> Yeah. Um, they've really really grown. It's super young group. And it's it's all of them, you know, they've done a great job of of of stepping up, of being, you know, wise beyond their years, having that feel, doing a lot of stuff at a way quicker timeline than what's average. And, um, you know, I think because of that the coaching staff does a great job of trying to call plays and design plays based off our personnel and what we can bring. I think we have a a super, super talented group out there. I think there's a lot that we can do and then uh for all of us as a unit, it's on us to kind of prove it to our coaches, to the play play callers. When they they're going to let us try everything and it's on us to kind of form that identity, uh put it on tape for them. Um and that's what training camp's for. >> Bryce, with coach Itzig now calling the plays, how different is it is from your perspective all the way from the team meetings, even the play selection, all the way to the play calling? >> Yeah, um you know, it's it's obviously it's different people, but it's it's the same process. Um you know, they they work hand in hand. They've always had a close relationship. Uh Brad's always been in there with us in QB meetings and you know, has always, you know, obviously been been on it and under stood everything. So, um it's it's really similar. Um it's a seamless process. Um even he was doing a lot behind the scenes last year that, you know, outside world probably didn't see, but us as a as a as a building we we we obviously felt. So, um they're they're one and the same. They work together. There's obviously going to be a lot of communication there. So, um yeah, we're excited for the next steps. >> Following up with that, Darrell Bevell's role in this new play calling with with Brad, how helpful he's been with the coaches and >> Yeah, Brad's been great um coming in, obviously being in a couple different systems and places, it's always nice to get fresh perspective, get um you know, to to learn a little bit about um you know, what what other other places have done, what he's had success in, try to marry that and add um and then um also he's been a great sounding board for me. Um he's had a ton of uh you know, a ton of experience in a lot of different places, been a lot of been around a lot of quarterback plays, seen a lot of ball. So, um I've just been trying to pick his brain as much as I can. I appreciate him for always allowing me to do that, always being open to conversation. So, um yeah, we're really excited for his role. >> Bryce, obviously team Mac um accomplished a lot in his rookie season. In what ways have you noticed him improve his game or work on his game? >> Yeah, um I mean, this off season, um like you said, obviously had a, you know, a win a rookie of the year. You know, having success he did, it's easy to kind of just phone it in and keep going. Being around him a lot this off-season, the work he's put in, the discipline he's had with his body, with his workouts, with his training, being able to kind of have those next-level conversations of, "Okay, we've established you know how to run these routes and you know what this is." You know, "How do you feel about, you know, this stuff? How do we feel about, you know, changing up these little nuances to, you know, try to give a defense a curveball." Just being able to do those things, he's super smart. So, that that's stuff that, you know, you expect from a vet and, you know, him going a year or two, I would already feel super confident with. So, I'm super excited for him. He's put in again a ton of work. So, it's just, you know, it's on all of us to make sure we we translate into our ultimately what what matters the most is winning. >> You around him? >> Yeah, around around him a good amount. Around him around him a good amount. So, again, just being able to see that work and that process get get even more reps, it's huge. >> Appreciate it very much. >> Appreciate you guys.

title: The top position battles to watch at training camp | Countdown to Camp
text: Welcome back into the Broncos podcast studio. I'm your host Eric Dala alongside the Hall of Famer Steve Atwater and our digital media contributor Susanna. We are That was enough hype for [music] you. >> Yeah, that was great. >> Okay, perfect. >> Got to got to match the energy for the Hall of Famer. >> Uh Susanna, >> we're we're here talking about Broncos training camp powered by Ford. It is a little more than a week away. Hard to believe it is uh almost here. >> It's coming. >> It's coming. And we uh we've still got some things to talk about over the next few days. One of those is what we're watching at training camp. And we've talked about the rookies. We've talked about Jaylen Wadd. We've talked about Bon Knicks. But what are we going to see out there on this field during training camp? And uh Susan, this wide receiver position, if you look at it, it might be more stacked than any group on the roster. When you look at this group, just there's a lot of talent, right? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think we'll be we kind of looking to see how the rotation and the reps shake out. I mean, obviously, you bring in Jaylen Wadd, which we've spent a lot of time this off seasonason talking about how that's going to change the entire offense, but then you also have players who are, you know, like Troy Franklin, who's coming off a second year where he took a huge leap from his rookie season. So, what's it going to look like for him? You have Pat Bryant who had a really promising rookie year and is probably going to look to get more involved. So, um, you know, really curious to see how the addition of Jaylen Waddle plays into all of that. obviously of Courtland Sutton who's been as reliable as possible for this team for several years. So, um you know, like you mentioned, I think we're going to be looking at those backend competitions, but then also seeing how the reps shake out with the with the group of who we think will be the established contributors. >> Yeah. And Steve, it sus right there about all the, you know, Wadd Sutton, all these guys. Pat Bryant, we'll talk in the coming days about who could be a breakout star for this team. I think Pat Bryant after the year he had could be a good choice for that. Steve, the the wide receiver room is interesting. And you talk about Hakee Butler, a little Jordan Humphrey. Just to me, this looks like such a stacked position group that like to make this team, you're going to have to really go out there and have a heck of a training camp, a heck of a preseason because you look at guys who were on the active roster a year ago in Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims, who had a heck of a playoff performance and we keep hearing Shawn Peyton say we got to get him involved more and more. um Pat Bryant, Lil Jordan Humphrey who caught a touchdown in that playoff win over the Bills. And then you add a guy like Hakeem Butler and and maybe um for those people listening if you're dialed in, you know who Butler is, but he was a guy that signed late in the offseason. June 16th is when he joined the team. Came over from the St. Louis Battle Hawks. Maybe Steve, that might be why you like him, right? The St. Louis. >> That's right. Home my home guy. >> Home St. Louis connection. But uh he led the United Football League in receiving yards and yards per catch. last year 29 uh catches for 641 receiving yards, three touchdowns. Former fourth round pick in 2019. Sounds like he dealt with some injuries. Uh but but he's definitely a guy that'll be interesting to watch. I just I think when you think about this group, it is in part who makes the roster, but then Susanna, like you said, how the reps shake out and when we get in a game, you know, how many targets is Jaylen Wild getting versus Courtland Sutton versus Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims, Troy Franklin, um LJ, whoever it might be. And we know with a Shawn Peyton offense, even though Davis Web's calling the plays now, that could change week to week. And I I do think the the thing I appreciate about this group is Portland Sutton in the offseason said, "I don't care how many targets I get. I just want to win." And it does seem to be one of the like there's no divas in this group. And you look around the league and a lot of times the receiver room, there's some personalities. These guys are incredibly unselfish. Um so excited to see how that plays out. And don't forget the practice squad, too. Like you could have a guy that doesn't make the active roster immediately, but then they bring him up three times from the practice squad, you know, then they uh you know, maybe then they they promote him and keep him on the active roster. So all these roster mechanics kind of kind of fit into that. But I think when you add Jaylen Wadd to the group, I I really think this this one of the better receiver rooms in the NFL in my mind and certainly deep in terms of those guys. >> Yeah. But the one thing you got to think about though is in the preseason the true starters aren't going to get a ton of time. They may get some time in you in the first half, but second half it's going to be all the third, fourth, fifth, sixth team guys. And those guys are going to get a chance to show. And uh I think that that's that's one of the battles I'm going to be watching just to see which of those guys is able to put up. Um because like I said um Hakee Butler has had some injuries and again I know Shawn Peyton has said out of his own mouth he loves the bigger receivers and um he fits that mold to a tea. Hakee Butler does. So uh it just be interesting just you know take a look at it. >> Yeah. No I mean we'll see he'll be got to watch it. And there's there's other guys too like Michael Bandy has made plays in regular season football games. You've got rookies coming in. Dne Kei, Devin Keyy's younger brother. uh Kobe Katsis, Jo Joseph Manjack, uh Cameron Ross, all trying to make the team as undrafted guys. So there and there's always an undrafted receiver it feels like in the preseason that that's the star, the darling. Um and so we'll see how that all pans out. Susa, any other position groups you're looking at where you think I can't wait to see this competition? >> Yeah, I'm really excited to see the tight end room. I think, you know, we Broncos drafted two guys, traded up to to draft Justin Jolie. um got Don Bentley towards the end of the draft and then you know just adding to you've already got Evan Ingram, Adam Troutman, uh Nate Atkins, Lucas Kroll, just a bunch of guys who have been you know shown that they can be consistent contributors for this team and so how are these new guys coming in going to fold into the mix there um and what can they bring. So uh really excited to see, you know, how the competition there shakes out, I would say. and a guy like Caleb Loner who Shawn Payeyton said he might have been the most improved player, the guy who stood out during rookie mini camp. Um, this is a room that you could look at and if you told me like four or five different combinations of players in terms of who makes the the active roster, I would believe it just in in terms of the different skill sets, like you've got a guy like Evan Ingram who could be unlocked, I think this year playing with, you know, a Davis web offense. Obviously, the the game last year that Davis Webb called in the preseason, Evan Ingram had a really good game. I think having a guy like Wadd, and we talked about this, Steve, like Wadd helps JK Dobbins, he helps Evan Ingram, he helps Corland Sutton, he helps all these guys. Like Evan Ingram could take a huge step, but behind him, like, and obviously you've got a veteran and Adam Trman, but behind those two guys, like Justin Jolie as a as a rookie who made some big plays at NC State, could he come in and have a a year one impact? Caleb Loner, does he show that he's ready to take that next step? Don Bentley in terms of a blocker. Like you could go on and on and and obviously you talk about Nate Atkins who kind of he does everything. Yeah. Um this is gonna be a position where I think it's gonna be hard to to make the team and and Steve, we heard George Payeyton and Shawn Payeyton say that around the draft like it's going to be a hard team to make and that that's a good thing when you're a football team that you don't want it to be an easy team to make. >> No, it really is a good thing to have. That means that you had you had a good football team the previous year and you don't have to make a ton of changes. you know, I think that uh is going to be a lot of great competition out there and yeah, that that tight end um those are going to be some great battles. Um and I'm I'm really looking forward to that. Yet, Don Bentley, Justin Jolie, um Caleb Loner, those will be some relatively new guys. Uh well, I mean, we we know we saw Caleb Loner last year, but the other two rookies that we drafted. Um it'll be interesting to see how uh how they are able to um play at this level. >> Yeah, absolutely. And I think when you look around the rest of the roster, there's there's some competitions for like reserve roles, like who who are going to be the inside linebackers behind Justin Sternat and Alex Singleton? Who's going to end up earning, you know, those those running back reps after a JK Dobbins? Who's going to be the reserve couple of safeties behind Brandon Jones and Talano Hufunga? I think if you're looking for one more kind of flashy competition, if you will, it might be a defensive end where John Franklin John Franklin Meyers leaves in free agency and now the Broncos have to find a guy to step in there and JFM played a lot of snaps. Vance Joseph said this offseason. Um, you look at the tape and you're like, "Wow, he had a he was a big reason why we had so much success." Um, but the Broncos have also invested there. They drafted Seavon Jones a year ago. They drafted Inomo Wazar a few years ago and he had a big year last year compared to kind of how he played the previous season. They obviously go and and draft Tyler Onetam with their first pick this year. And you've got a guy like Matt Hennington coming back. Um, and Vance Jo Joseph said, "Listen, we drafted these young guys. Now they got to go play." And that's kind of how the NFL works. Uh Steve, what are you kind of looking for at that position group? That that battle there for the defensive end spot. >> Oh man. Um yeah, losing JFM, uh you know, that that definitely was huge, but um you know, we have some young guys that can fill in there and I think that um Shawn Payeyton, George Pton, they both knew that otherwise we probably wouldn't have let him go. >> Yeah. Um and um uh Inoma Azarque I think is you know the guy who pops out of my mind as the the top person of that group that would be have the best opportunity of starting there as of right now right >> uh but hey anything can change and uh as we know you got to step up here in training camp and show what you can do and uh not only get the coaches respect but you got to get your teammates respect >> when you look at that group what what stands out to you about that uh that defensive line battle because it it also sounds like listening to Vance Joseph, they could also mix guys in there. Maybe you've got a one guy playing on early downs and another guy coming in on third downs. >> Yeah, I think it's just what Steve mentioned, you know, he he mentioned a couple weeks ago that they wouldn't have let JFM walk if there wasn't good guys in there who are going to be competing and have an opportunity to contribute. So, I just see a lot of top tier talent, a guy, a lot of guys who are going to be looking to carve out their roles and um you know, like you said, there's a lot of versatility in there that I think we'll we'll see kind of play out in the next couple weeks. >> Yeah. And I think like you know, one of the things Vance Joseph mentioned was do you have Seavon Jones in there on pass rush downs and you've got in there on on a first and second down and um you know, how how much is Onetta ready for as a rookie? I think the other thing that I'm a little bit interested in is is how creative can you get in terms of like DJ Jones so good in the middle of that defense, but could you put Malcolm Roach in the middle and shift DJ Jones outside or have DJ Jones in there as kind of that pass rushing specialist on a third down? I think there's some, like you mentioned, Sue, some versatility there. Um, but I I kind of like Steve when you've got these young guys and they all know they're going to be competing for a job and it's open and it's right there. Feel like it that brings out the best in guys. Yeah, because I guess when when people come in and they know that they have their position locked down, sometimes, you know, they don't show everything that they have during training camp, but I think these guys are going to going to be um you know, playing with uh with their with their pants on fire, you know, so to speak. They're going to going to really be trying to prove to their teammates and their coaches that they are the person for this job. >> That's right. And uh we are we're getting close to watching this unfold in real time. It'll happen in training camp in the preseason. We will [music] have you covered as it all unfolds. But for now, for the Hall of Famer Steve Atwater, our digital media contributor Susanna Weir, I'm Eric Dala. Thanks for listening to our countdown to camp on Altitude Advantage.

title: Dan Hoard Interviews Al Golden
text: It's always great to spend a few minutes with Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden. You did a news conference the day after the Dexter Lawrence trade. That was a couple of months ago. Now that you've been around him on a regular basis and watched him practice, what do you think? >> Yeah, I I remember I recall vividly just how excited I was and how I spent that Sunday. We ended up going to dinner that night, but I spent that Sunday watching his film from the previous year and how excited I was. And then I met the man. You know, um just an incredible human being. Selfless player. He'll do whatever we ask him to do. Brings energy every day. I don't know if it's common knowledge or not, but so we were at dinner that night, Zac's there. He says, "I'll be there tomorrow." And he he never left. So he didn't miss a he didn't miss a day in the off season. So that's a testament to his character and obviously what he wants to get done here in the next year. >> You've coached some great players, some great defensive tackles. Have you ever seen anybody with that combination of massive size but quickness and athleticism? >> Yeah, I I it's rare. It's very rare, but I think what separates him is just how disruptive he is. And even when he's not making the sack or batting the ball down or making the tackle, he's he's disrupting the course and the flow of the game and certainly the pocket and having that pocket presence inside and now we feel like you know, we have five guys that we can rotate inside that that can all push the pocket and obviously give us a better edge on the on the perimeter. >> You like the expression force multiplier. Is Dexter the greatest example of a force multiplier? >> Yeah, I just think the thing that's nice about him is you don't have to take him off the field. He can push the pocket on on third down or known passing downs. Get back on track if you will. Um and we have a good rotation, but I think what separates him is his ability to finish on the perimeter. When you watch his tackles and we studied his wrap and roll tackles and showed it to the unit um a number of times just uh his reach uh his mobility down the line of scrimmage and ability to finish in the C D gap or on the perimeters is is very unique for a man of his size. >> Duke Tobin did a news conference right after the season last year where he said the following, we have tons of leadership on offense, we need somebody, multiple people to step up and lead the defense. With the addition of Dexter and Bryan Cook and Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen and and others, do you see a change there? >> Yeah, what I see is the confluence of what we were talking about at the end of last year with the growth of of the guys that were here last year you know D Knight and and Jordan Battle and Zach Carter, Myles Murphy and I see that group continuing on their trend and then I see this other group coming in and uh it's great. Nobody stand offish, everybody's got you know focused on moving forward together and really combining forces and it's been great to see but I can tell you just from being back there during practice to hear those guys talk and solve problems and take ownership. They're empowered to solve problems. Uh Cook is a great example of that. He's he plays with so much poise and he's a great communicator and he's just fun to be around every day. Every every guy that Duke gave us in the off season um they're tremendous people off the field. They're obviously great athletes or we wouldn't have brought them here but they're great people and they've all added to the leadership of our building. >> Bryan Cook was the first free agent the Bengals signed on the first day of free agency. Was that just the way it worked out or was he at the top of the wish list? >> That was that was that was a great get for us and uh uh he's proved formidable since then. I mean whatever we ask him to do he can do um and and again just being around him um I'm not surprised, uh but I'm excited about, you know, his range and his ability to cover. Uh those are bonuses for all the other things that he does really well, disrupt the football, tackle in the alley, run the show. Uh so, uh he's got the complete package and obviously uh worthy of of uh you know, his price tag in the off season. >> I saw all of his games at USC. He's a physical tone setter. It's clean. He's only been called for one penalty the last couple of years and it it wasn't a personal foul. But did your defense need a dose of that? >> Yeah, I think uh again, I I see not just what he brings, but I see the just the guys from last year continuing to make that positive trend. And um and I see it in practice, you know, I see it when we're doing drills. Um there's an intentionality there. And I think what B. Cook does is um he brings a professionalism, an intentionality, and a purpose to every drill. And uh so, I quality control the tackling drills with the coaches and we show it to the guys and he's coming up time and time again. Now it's Jordan Battle. Now it's B. Carter, Demetrius Knight. So, uh we've got a run on guys now trying to really do things at an elite level and uh obviously um uh Brian's one of the stimulus for that. >> Staying in the secondary, Dax Hill thrived as an outside corner when you moved him to that spot last year. He would like to stay outside. Is that the plan? >> Uh it is the plan. I I think Dax has done a tremendous job and um uh JD's growth inside is is an allow is allowing us to do that. And then, you know, the growth of others, you know, whether it's Feg, DJ Ivy, the contributions that they make, especially in our dime package. Um and then obviously uh bringing someone like Bobo in. And uh I don't know if you were out there today, but he made a really nice interception um just before we broke in seven-on-seven and um he's another guy with want to and and uh a good football mind and he's learning quickly. So we got a good group there. Chuck and Jordan do a great job with the back end. And we'll continue to work and and some packages, you know, Dax will be wherever his match up is. So sometimes that will be inside. But certainly on early downs we're going to continue this course with him because it's working out really well. >> JD is Jaylen Davis. He was on the Super Bowl team. So he's been here longer than most of the guys on the roster. He's always been a valuable reserve. But was it a bit of a pleasant surprise when he moved into the starting lineup and had the impact that he did? >> I'm a big Jaylen Davis fan. Again, tremendous person, great work ethic, intellect, confidence when he's on the field, the ability to run it. He gives me so much confidence. On on the defensive side as a play caller because I know he's always going to write the ship and he's always going to communicate. Where he is aligned up and and what we need to get done. So obviously that's comforting from from my standpoint. The thing I'll say about JD is he had a great off season. And what I mean by that is before he got here. He came here when we started the off season program in tremendous condition and he couldn't wait to show me. The condition that he was in and and then obviously he's he's had a really really good spring for us and again Chuck does a good does a great job with those guys. >> DJ Turner played at a Pro Bowl level. You often had him shadowing the other team's best wide receiver and he didn't start in week one. Was that one of the most dramatic start of the seasons to end of the seasons examples of growth that you've seen? >> Yeah, maybe you know, you know, his career turned on that axis right there and I think uh it's not even that day to the end of the season. It's that day to maybe 2 weeks later and he started to climb. He became process driven. Doing all the little details off the field, making sure he's taking care of his mind his mental health, his mind. Um brings energy when he when he plays. Obviously has makeup speed. Really good at the catch point. So, I mean he's he uh he made a lot of great strides and I see it out there right now as he continues to make that progress for us. >> I feel like the addition of Kyle Dugger Dugger has kind of flown under the radar a little bit. The Patriots thought enough to give him a $58 million deal a few years ago, then he got hurt, then there's a coaching change. Now he winds up in Cincinnati at the age of 30. How does he fit with your >> Yeah, I'm excited about Dug. Again, just savvy. Just watching him operate. Safe for bringing him on a pressure and just how he plays with poise. He gets his quarterback indicators and then he comes and he disguises really well. He's a physical player. He's a big big body presence. Um again, we're teaching him everything right now, but the things that he did really well last year for New England and Pittsburgh was just play with savvy in the box and he can find the ball and get the ball carrier on the ground and he's a great addition for us and and again, he just brings guys that are that are ready-made professionals and ready for right now, built for right now. >> I've been watching the two second-year linebackers quite a bit in these off-season practices. It looks to me like they're being more vocal and communicating more. Is that accurate? >> Unequivocally. Again, they're both you know, really comfortable. They're solving problems. they're making choices, really good choices on the field. They're getting us lined up right. They're getting us in the adjustment or stunt. And again, I've said it to you multiple times. I I I could call the front. I can call the coverage, but I can't always call the stunt correctly. You have to do that based on formation, backfield set, and whatever the game plan or or whatever the indicators are and and they're doing that now. They're much more comfortable in that. Um and they can handle more. I think more importantly what I see is just they're able to focus on the technique cuz the mind is a little bit quieter. Um, so I knew there was going to be uh dividends and again, credit to Mike Hodges for really pushing through last year, pushing through. At the end of the day, it wasn't perfect. They continued to make growth, but we ended up with two guys with 100 plus tackles coming back uh on a on a group that's been fortified around them. So I'm really excited about those two. >> At practice, you've got the walkie-talkie, which I assume you're using to communicate with players on the field. Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight both have helmets on. In practice, do you talk to them both or is it like a game where you only talk to one? >> take turn We take turns with the green dot um and and uh Joe uh Giles will do it, too. Um, but we'll take uh turns with the green dot just to make sure everybody's trained with it and uh you know, again, so uh you know, that we you know, we we have some continuity there if if someone has you know, if there's a problem with a green dot or someone gets dinged for a couple plays that we can uh you know, continue to move forward. >> I spoke to an NFL analyst that did uh like a 10-year study of PFF data and he says that linebackers improve the most based on that data from first year to second year more than any other position. Does that track for you? >> Well, uh times two, right? >> Right. >> both. So uh I hope that's true. Uh I feel like it's true now and uh and again, uh we put those guys in a a a very precarious spot last year. Um, again, I've done it with one before part-time. Um, you know, with Logan. but he had Bynes as a backstop, you know, and then he had Jermaine next to him. Um, but to do it uh with both guys, um we threw them in the deep end. Uh Uh, fought, they battled, and uh somehow, you know, made their way home. And uh, I think we're going to be the I think that the Cincinnati Bengals are going to be the benefactors of that, and that's certainly playing out that way this spring. >> Speaking with second-year guys, I've been keeping an eye on Shemar Stewart as much as I can. Everything looks just a tick faster to me. Is Is that just knowing what he's doing? >> Yeah, I think so. And again, it was unfortunate. Um, missed, you know, the off-season program. So, missed all of this last year. Missed the majority of training camp. And then, okay, Shemar, now you got to go in and play for us. So, he goes in and plays for us. If you go back and look at this the Cleveland game, there there's some plays where you're like, "Whoa." Uh, then he gets dinged up uh, the second week, and now he's back. So, he ends up missing a whole bunch of time. Um, so yeah, I'm I'm excited about his progress. He's got to continue to just make it small, be process-driven, uh, be a pro, look at the iPad all the time, ask questions, be engaged, uh, own own his path to success. Everybody's is different. Uh, uh, for example, I'll give you one uh, a tidbit. Just DeJean, uh, just uh, the the the the amount of uh, process that he has right now and the growth that he's made. That's another good example of guys developing at different times or or have a different timeline. And that's what we're trying to teach Shemar right now is to own that timeline, own that process, and and really push forward here as we get into August. >> Myles Murphy took big steps last year. What's the next step? >> Just continue to do it. Like, here's what he did at the end of, you know, really from mid-season last year on. He's just made the game really small. Didn't press to get a sack. Didn't press. Got his eyes quiet. Wasn't ping-ponging pre-snap. Knew exactly where his technique was, where he needed to be. Uh, executed at a really high level, and the plays came. Uh, he knows he left a couple out there. Uh, as as did we all. Uh, me too as the play caller. And I think this year uh, we're seeing another level of him um, this spring and and obviously just continue that path and those plays he's too he's too talented, he's too long, he's too strong for those plays not to come if he continues this positive trend that he's on right now. >> You were asked about him during training camp last year. You said it's time. >> Mhm. >> Does that expression apply to Chris Jenkins this year? >> so. I think so. And again, I I think uh uh we talked about Doug being overshadowed by some of that, but I think Chris's growth this off season has been overshadowed a little bit. Um but we need him to come through. Like we need to play a lot of guys. We need to play 10 guys up front and uh we need to be able to roll guys in there and uh Chris is a valuable uh piece of that. I'm a big fan of his. He brings energy. Uh he's very intelligent. He's strong. Uh he can anchor down. Um we just got to take that next step in terms of uh being able to make plays and and uh and and uh get some negatives for us. >> After the first day of the draft, teams reorganized their board based on who was selected in round one. When the Bengals did that this year, Cash Howell was at the top of the day two board. And you were able to get him with the ninth pick of the second round. Why were you and this organization so high on Cashus Howell? >> Uh sudden player, versatility, you know, has the ability to drop, has ability to rush off the edge. Uh gives you an alley presence at any time. Uh so he's really a true hybrid in that okay, what are where what is this guy doing on this play? So I think uh between him and Boye, uh we have a good uh group there of guys that that can be versatile. Um and I'll I'll I'll give you a little uh uh a little sneak inside. So we're sitting there at at beginning of Saturday, the two guys that we have picked the two guys that we have at the top of the board uh are there. And so we say no to a million trades. >> And finally, uh uh Duke gets the trade that he wants. And uh lo and behold, we trade back, get a pick in the fifth round, and get the same two guys that we had in the top of the board of the fourth round. And I I think that gets overshadowed a lot. So, uh we were able to bring in um you know, two guys in the fourth round, a center and a wide receiver uh that we had really high grades on. So, that was a That was a pretty cool moment to see that play out uh live. It didn't impact us on defense, but it was just It was just awesome to see. Uh got the two guys in the fourth that we wanted and picked up a fifth uh without giving anything up, which was awesome. >> Is Landon Robinson a coach's dream? >> Uh he's a great kid. Uh super smart, strong, uh do whatever you ask him to do. I think the biggest thing is he the details are mean a lot to him. Uh so, he is a uh he tries to please Jerry in terms of this is the way Jerry wants it, and and that's it. He'll give you that. And I think there's something to be said for that in terms of technique, alignment, just the specifics. Um he does a really good job of uh you know, being able to make make those techniques his own, and then reproduce it on the field. And I And I think uh he's got a really good process. So, I'm excited about him. >> There's an advanced stat used to measure defense called DVOA. In the last eight games last year, the Bengals improved by 32%, which was the most in the second half of the season by any team since 2014. What was the key to such improvement? >> it starts with the the players. Uh obviously, a bunch of guys came together. Uh we talked earlier about the guys who grew as leaders. Um DJ Turner and uh Jordan Battle. Uh obviously, the two linebackers played different in the second half. Myles Murphy was on a different one. Then we got help from Cedric uh and and and and Dax looked more comfortable outside. And he was coming off the ACL, too. Uh Jaylen came in and and and fortified us uh in the alley. Um so, there was a lot of uh uh things that came together to make that happen. Coaches did a great job. Everybody stayed together. And uh again, that's what we're so excited about. I think it's easy for the outside world to say, "Okay, yeah, we added these guys." But let's not forget about what the the the the course that these guys plotted uh before that addition. And and again, I think it's that combination that uh you know, should be the perfect storm for us. >> Did you simplify things to get guys to play faster? >> Always try to simplify. Uh again, if if if it's too complicated, uh it's it's my fault. I got to make sure I continue to simplify. Um we're working hard right now to build a system that, you know, can endure everything that we'll see week in and week out. I think that's what the players want. Uh they don't want to walk in on a Wednesday and have, you know, eight new calls, nine new calls. So, uh I'm I'm I feel like I'm doing a better job. The coaching staff's input has been phenomenal. Um and we've just taken a a deep breath and a and and and and, you know, have a big purview on right now in terms of what we got to try to get done for our guys. Uh which, you know, sometimes is painful this time of year cuz it's a little bit more than you can handle on a three-day work week uh or if you're not meeting as much as you would during the regular season. Uh but we will be the benefactors once training camp hits on what these guys put in out there today and what we got to do next week. >> You use the acronym BEST for your defensive philosophy and the letter T in B E S T stands for tackling. >> That's right. >> Which didn't go very well last year, but not all missed tackles are created equal. Will better play on the defensive line make tackling easier? >> Yeah, it's not just that. It's that we have additional pieces that are going to allow us the freedom to do multiple things and give different looks. So, um but certainly uh then when you when you think of speeding up the quarterback, how that impacts time and distance, right? So, um space tackles the hardest tackle to make in this league. And, you know, the more the more time there is to throw, the more they get to the top of the routes, the more space either vertically or horizontally. Uh and then, obviously, that becomes more difficult. So, uh we got to get better technically. I got to do better job calling the game. Uh pass rush has to has to do their spot uh part and when we are uh in man, we got to contest the ball. And if we're in zone, we got to break a little bit faster. And and again, the all those things coming together is what's going to make us better at that. >> Between being on the Super Bowl staff in '21 and returning last year, did the NFL change much in the 3 years you were at Notre Dame? >> it's constantly changing. Um I think uh you know, we're seeing it's a different era, obviously. Uh pre-snap Star Wars, if you will. You know, there's so many different things going on pre-snap. Um people would have said, you know, uh bunch of years ago, man, it looks like Canadian football, but we got so many jet motions going on right now and halfbacks out, back in, you know, tight ends out, back in. You got so many different things going on pre-snap. I think the the personnel usage has changed. I I would bet if you looked at some of those stats that you look at, um I would bet, you know, 12 and 13 personnel is higher than it has been in quite some time with the the advent of the jet motions and just trying to change the numbers um you know, at the last second or post-snap. Uh you know, trying to get multiple guys over here when the defense can't move multiple guys over there. Uh just in a simplistic form, anyway. >> Last thing. A lot of the players say the vibe is different. Do you feel that? >> Uh again, it makes it fun to go to work every day. And again, it starts with the human beings that we have in the building building. Uh and I'm and I'm talking about the entire building now. Uh just the the offensive leadership, uh defensive leadership, the head coach, the way the guys, you know, uh attack the weight room, the way they're hanging out together in in the dining facility, um doing things off the field. I think there's a connectivity. I think there's an energy, and I think there's a great spirit. And I said it before, like you know, you're watching you're watching you're watching the film, and you know what you're getting in terms of a football player, but man, you know, Brian Cook, Jonathan Allen, Dugger, Dex, all these guys that we've brought in, and then the guys that we drafted, just really really good people. And and obviously that that that makes it fun to go to work every day. >> I always enjoy picking your brain. Thanks for the time. >> Thanks, Dan.

title: 2026 Training Camp Preview | Dallas Cowboys 2026
text: Hi, I'm Mickey Spagnola, one of the writers on dallascowboys.com, presenting you a short preview of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp, the 41st of my career. >> [music] [music] >> The Cowboys arrive via their American Airlines charter flight for their 19th training camp in Oxnard, California at the River Ridge Sports Complex. And if you can believe this, their 46th camp in the state of California, having spent 27 summers training up the 101 at California Lutheran University in Thousand Oaks. The lure of the Ventura County tempered weather and the most accommodating accommodations keeps them [music] coming back. And if the off-season workouts back at The Star in Frisco, Texas are any indication under second-year head coach Brian [music] Schottenheimer, these will be highly competitive practice sessions with starting jobs and roster spots up for grabs after a disappointing 2025 season, finishing 7-9-1 and out of the playoffs for an unaccustomed second straight season. There will be much anticipation to get a look at the Cowboys first three 2026 draft choices, first-round safety Caleb Downs, second first-round defensive lineman Malachi Lawrence, and third-round [music] linebacker Jay Shawn Barham. Every one of them in competition for a starting role. No surprise after the 2025 defensive [music] struggles, all three defensive players. And the Cowboys are working hard from a personnel [music] standpoint to refurbish this defense. And that starts not only with the numerous veteran free agents signed in the offseason, but the three acquisitions directly [music] acquired thanks to last year's trade of Micah Parsons, defensive tackle Kenny Clark, defensive lineman Quinnen Williams, and having traded for a defensive edge Rashaan Gary. Not only new defensive players, but an entirely new defensive coaching staff starting with first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker. And he'll be working all over the defense helping the school every position, teaching, inspiring competition, calling in the plays. As for important camp dates, the opening ceremony on August 1st, the first padded practice August 3rd, heroes appreciation day August 6th, a live practice streamed on dallascowboys.com August 8th, traveling to the Los Angeles Rams Village in Woodland Hills August 11th for a highly anticipated workout with those highly rated Rams and catching a glimpse of their newly acquired defensive end Myles Garrett from the DFW area. And then August 18th, joint practice at River Ridge with New Orleans Saints and former Cowboys backup quarterback and offensive coordinator Kellen Moore, now the Saints head coach. The high-powered Cowboys offense nearly returns intact. Dak Prescott at quarterback, Pro Bowl wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George [music] Pickens, running back Javonte Williams, and a seasoned offensive line. Defensively, the Cowboys are counting on a bevy of newcomers like linebacker D Winners, safeties Jaylen Thompson and corners Kobe Bryant and P.J. Locke.
