title: Fernando Mendoza on Signing His Rookie Deal, His Mindset for Training Camp and More
text: Hey, welcome to a special edition of Upon Further Review. We've got the number one draft pick, Fernando Mendoza, joining us here in studio. Fernando, thank you so much for for taking the time. Number one, congratulations. Uh you signed your contract, it's all official. What does it mean to sign that contract? To go from being a backup on the South Miami Grey Ghosts to the silver and black with as a Heisman Trophy winner and the number one overall pick. >> Well, first of all, Mr. Gutierrez, I appreciate you having me on. It means a lot. I always love talking to the silver and black, especially now that I'm a part of it. Having signed the contract, it was very big that I didn't miss any days, especially in training camp, cuz I want to make sure I take advantage of every opportunity that is presented in front of me and, you know, inspire with that with my teammates as well. So, I was able to sign a contract, which was an awesome experience, and ready to get to work. >> How different did that feel than from the first ever autograph you signed? And do you remember signing an autograph for the very first time? >> Ooh. I think the first legit autograph I signed was back at Cal. And I remember it was like, "Oh, this is cool." But it was a little It was a young It was a young kid who didn't really understand autographs, and he was getting autographs [laughter] for everybody. So, it wasn't like it was my It was like the whole team, and it was It was still awesome cuz, you know, the whole team. >> Yeah, yeah. How would you describe these last 6 weeks? I mean, not only just in signing the contract, but it's just been a whirlwind for you. Being the Heisman winner, being the number one pick, uh going through min- mini camp and OTAs and rookie mini camp, getting the ESPY, getting your degree from Cal. How would you describe everything that you've been going through the past few weeks? >> I would say I would use the word blessed. >> Okay. >> I've been very blessed through this opportunity and to be able to thrive and develop and evolve through different stages of my life, whether it's college, pre-draft, to the now my professional stage. It's been a great blessing, and I really see the ecosystem evolving around me as well, you know, and maintaining that dynamic equilibrium of football success, but then, you know, with family and teammates and then balancing those relationships as well. It has been and then studying the playbook is it's been a great challenge this offseason and I believe that we were able to rise to the occasion in that and then I'm excited to show what I have and compete with my teammates in in training camp. >> How would How are you able to compartmentalize all that? I mean, I guess that just comes with the territory, right? And that's all you've ever really known, but how are you able to compartmentalize? >> I think it's about being productive. I'm a very tight I have a very type A personality and I believe that you want to make sure that you have priorities and have a system for every day, every week so you know what you want to get accomplished. And when you do that efficiently, you usually have time left over and in that time left over you can talk to family, friends, and you know, and then you could you know, maybe go out to dinner with some of the teammates. And so with that, if you're efficient and really intentional with your time, I believe you can squeeze all the juice out of the orange for everything you can do in the possibly for football and then still get some extra family time. >> You said something in in rookie mini camp, Fernando, that really caught my attention. You talked about being positively stressed by a lot of information. What does that mean? >> Yeah, when I first got to mini camp, it was a whirlwind. You know, the playbook's thrown at you, you're you're learning the plays in the morning and then 30 minutes later you're on the field repping it against a live defense. So it's a lot coming at you, but that's that positively stresses your mind, your body, making you do new movements and it make it forces you to learn quick. You essentially hop on the train or get left behind. And at that point, your only option is to jump on the train. And then now having that stress and when you have stress, your body becomes more accustomed and more enabled to take in information. >> Okay. And so with being positively stressed in mini camp and then now evidently there's a lot more situations, so it's not like easy cuz you have to go against live defense and there's you know, different intricacies to each play, but at least it sets a good groundwork. >> Yeah. Before free agency, even before the draft when when Clint Kubiak was first hired as the head coach, he said in a perfect world a rookie learns behind a veteran and doesn't start from day one. And yet there is a quarterback competition here and you're learning a lot of things from not only Kirk Cousins, but Aidan as well. Uh how would you describe that quarterback room right now? >> Yeah, that quarterback room is great with Kirk, Aidan, and Jacob. I mean that is fantastic. And I believe everybody brings a different perspective. Kirk is a long-time veteran. Aidan's been in the league for I think around 3 to 4 years. And then Jacob and I both being rookies, it it just takes it's all their perspectives of how people have done things in previous offenses, how they tackle learning the playbook, you know, the play calls. There's so many different intricacies with an offense as a quarterback. You need to be essentially all-knowing of the offense. For your teammates to have confidence in you when you step out on that field and have such great resources of information, whether it be the coaches, my teammates especially in the quarterback room. It's it's it's basically all in the palm of my hand and I just need to take advantage of it. >> How would you describe how that's going to look going into training camp, the competition so to speak amongst all of you? >> Yeah, I think that Kirk, Aidan, Jacob, everybody in the quarterback room is a top-tier quarterback. >> And it's going to be competing with each other, not competing against each other. Competing with each other, pushing each other to be the best quarterback we can possibly be for the Las Vegas Raiders and to enable to then as win as many games as possible, rather than against, withholding information, wishing maybe not the best intent on somebody. It's more in wishing the best for, you know, "Hey, I saw this. Hey, I saw that." competing with each other and growing with each other. >> Got you. Speaking of the quarterback room and quarterbacks, you grew up up I didn't realize this. I didn't realize you were actually born in Boston. I mean, and you know, you grew up in South Florida, obviously, but but there's those New England roots and you grew up a Patriots fan, a Tom Brady fan. How would you describe that relationship and how strange was that when you got that first FaceTime call from him uh during the combine? He's like, "Hey, that's Tom Brady." >> Yeah. Although I was born in Boston, I do honestly consider myself born and raised in Miami because I was only I was only in Boston for 6 months while my dad was in medical residency. No [laughter] memories at all. So, I mean, I was there for like 6 months to a year at most, but still that gave me an excuse to become you know, earlier on it early stages as a quarterback fan it enabled me to become a little bit of an of a Patriots fan and a lot a bit of a Tom Brady fan admiring the situation. And the Dolphins are great, but at the time, you know, it wasn't, you know, what Tom Brady was doing over there in New England. So, I was able to admire that from a young age and have a little bit of a excuse to bandwagon a little bit. >> So, then to to have a like a personal relationship with him now. I mean, that's like kind of meeting your heroes, so to speak. A lot of people say, "Don't meet your heroes cuz you might not like what you see or what's what's what's what's there." What has that been like for you with Tom? >> It's surreal. It's surreal. He's been such a great resource and he's been from a young age it's been a big idol of mine and then now it's okay, Tom is a human being. Yes, he's an exceptional human being, but he's a human being. So, take what you can, learn from him, and make sure that you value our relationship. He's someone that, you know, has a lot of characteristics and values that I look up to as a football player and a character outside of football. Having that relationship is surreal and if you would have told me 10 years ago, I never would have believed you, but like I said, and I used this word earlier, blessed. >> Blessed. Now, you've been compared your skill set to not only Tom's, but Andrew Luck, Bernie Kosar, but you have that connection also with a Latino quarterback connection here with the Raiders, Tom Flores, Jim Plunkett. And I know when you first got here and you talked about you wanted to have the blessing of Tom to wear number 15. The Raiders don't retire numbers necessarily, but it meant something to you to to get his blessing. Let me read to you exactly what he said. I talked to Tom. He told me he deserves my blessing because if he's not the real deal, I don't know what the hell I'm doing. He's perfect. He can make every throw. He can make the plays. What can't he do? He does it all. He's fun to watch. Plus, he's a good-looking kid like me. Hall of Fame coach Tom Flores, the first quarterback in Raiders franchise history. When you hear him say that and welcome you and say, "Of course he deserves to wear number 15." What does that do for you? >> It means a lot and I believe that there is a price to admission with the Raiders and especially getting the blessing of wearing his number, like you said, a Hall of Fame coach here. And that means a lot. I mean, he's definitely better looking than I am, >> [laughter] >> but you know, he's something he's someone that is a legend, a Hall of Famer, and I believe that is important to pay respects to the ones that laid the foundation. >> And the ones that made and paved the path possible to now what the Raiders organization is now, cuz he put a huge part in it and I believe getting his blessing and being initiated and admitted into the silver and black, that was a very important part. It means a lot cuz, you know, like I said, Hall of Famer, it's a very nice message by him. >> Yeah, definitely. And lastly, >> Up to me to win that. >> Hope so. Yeah, definitely. And and lastly, Fernando, you're a Star Wars guy. I'm a Star Wars guy. My family's a Star Wars people. You're the Mandalorian. I got to show you something that my son drew for me for Father's Day last month. >> He drew that for me and I said, "I got to show this to Fernando." He's an art major at UNO and he did that. >> Your son is fantastic art. This is crazy. I was not expecting this. >> This is incredible. >> So, I guess the camera can see that. This is this is like >> We'll put it up there. >> It's like the real deal. This is that's awesome. >> So I will let him know what you said and I guess with only the best way to end this interview Fernando. Number one, Mr. Gutierrez was my grandpa so just call me Paul from here on out. But also this is the way. >> This is the way. >> All right Fernando, thank you so much for your time. If you want to stay up to date on all things silver and black you can check out the Raiders YouTube channel or go to raiders.com for more content.

Matt Derek, you're up. I just asked. >> Oh, you got your >> I know you had some injuries before, but how much have you learned about yourself throughout this whole this whole process? >> Um, I don't know if I ever have I really learned anything crazy. It's just it's just like a mindset you have to have in order to go about this process. And it it's hard. Like it's every day is hard and and you have to just continue to just stack days on days and and and stuff stuff kind of just builds and builds. And like I said, I think having my kids and being able to like after rehab go to T-ball practice and after rehab go to whatever with Sterling and and I think that kind of kept my mind off the just the repetitive repetitiveness. And so now it's just about um getting here and I've told some of the guys is like sometimes you come up to St. Joe and you're like, "All right, we're going to go to St. Joe or be in the dorm, stuff like that." I'm like, I'm I'm excited just to be able to play football. I've been I've been seeing cinder block walls rehabbing every single day in Kansas City. And so now um to get out to be on that practice field with my teammates and my brothers, it's going to be it's going to be a lot of fun. >> And you've been a pretty mobile quarterback. How much have you learned that you know you may not be able to do some things? >> I plan to be able to do everything I I did before. Um it's I I've been moving around and doing that stuff, but um I'm going to obviously try to take care of myself a little bit better than I did last season. I think I ran a little bit too much last season um in general. So I'll try to be better with that. Um, and then if all else fails, just give it to to K9 and let him just go out there and work. >> The injury aside, you all didn't have the year that you wanted last year. Does it feel different coming to St. Joe this year? Do you approach anything different? >> Um, it doesn't feel different in a sense of like what last happened last year because that happened last year. It's a brand new year. If you win the Super Bowl or don't make it, it's if you don't win the Super Bowl, you're in the same spot and you're coming to kind of do it again this next year. Um, I think it's just the longer break. I think you can just tell guys are more excited to be back in the building. You know, we've had a lot of short off seasons. And so having that extra six weeks, it sounds awesome until you're in the middle of summer, you're like, man, I really miss football. And so, uh, I think just seeing the guys around the building, especially this last week, those guys are kind of filing back into Kansas City. You can tell guys are really pumped to get back out here and play football. >> Todd, >> coach mentioned that Rashid had been up rehab after he got out. What do you expect from him? You think he's going to be up here at this rookie park now? I mean, what his mindset do this from. >> Yeah, he's he's excited to get back out here. He kind of the similar thing is he's ready to play football again and just get out here and be with the guys and I've been rehabbing with them a lot. He's been in the building as much as I have, him and Omar. Um and it's it's been I mean I I hate that they're injured, but it's been good for me because you have guys that you can work with and try to get better with together. And so um he's doing great. Like he's doing great. I've thrown to him. He's caught. He's he's done a lot all the stuff he needs to do. Um, and I don't know if he'll be out on the field or whatever, but he I know he's rehabbing and doing the way he needs to be to be on on the field whenever uh camp gets going. >> Last little thing you mentioned numbers with the you know doing the rehab yards and stuff. What are the little numbers you like to compete with Zack? [snorts] >> Well, it would start off as like like how much deadlift, you know, deadlift like what you're deadlifting, where you're at. Um, and then it's like you send little videos like he's he's jumping and doing certain acceleration things and I'm like sending them next week doing cutting and stuff like that. And so it keeps the competition going because it's a long process and you feel like sometimes you're you're lonely because you're just you're doing stuff by yourself and you're just competing against yourself. So it gave me someone that else I can compete with to kind of uh push my competitive drive. >> Jesse and Patrick, what's one area you want to be sure to improve this year after the season went through? >> Yeah, I think it's just about getting the ball out of my hands. I think obviously I like to make the big play happen and and sometimes I I won't take the the short one or I I won't take the first read because I'm trying to make a bigger play happen. It's getting the ball in my hands, making plays like that happen and then whenever the deep ball is there, you have to hit it. Like at the end of the day, that's just comes down to me uh throwing the ball and giving guys chances to make plays. Doesn't always have to be perfect, but give guys chances to make plays downfield. And so if we can do that, uh as well as the run game that I I'm excited for, I think we can get back to being a a dynamic offense. >> Last one, Sam. Andy says he plans on having you go through this camp as if it was any other. But have you had a conversation with him about, hey, you know, if you want to call, you know, under center plays more often that I'm ready for that. Do you want just the same routine as if you haven't gone through this? >> I mean, I want him to call call it like you we're going to call in the regular season. So, whatever that is, uh, that's going to be the best way for me to prepare myself. Um, and then I can always let them know if if I need to get pulled back or anything like that. But how I am as a competitor, I want to go out there and test it. You know, you want to test it now in training camp, see where you're at. Um, so when you get to the regular season, it's it's almost a little bit easier because you don't you've kind of been through it all. And so that's how he runs training camp. I don't think he's going to take it light on anybody, including me. And then uh I'm going to go out there and see what I can do. >> Okay. Thanks, Patrick. >> Appreciate it.

title: Alec Pierce, Daniel Jones & the 5 BIGGEST storylines of Colts training camp | The Colts Show Podcast
text: This is very underscored. Remember to throw your random one here. How much do you see him returning during camp? >> That's a really good question. Because that's a good segue to the under the radar storylines to follow. Lara's following the backup returner. [laughter] >> Nothing nothing says July football like that, right? Like we're >> Welcome into a bonus episode of the Colt Show. We are presented by Microsoft Surface Co-pilot Plus PC. I'm JJ Stankovits. Like heck yeah, let's go. >> Yeah, that was like a good little appetizer for you to get ready for the season, right? >> it's funny calling the World Cup an appetizer. Our European audience is going to be very mad about that. That's what a lot of our European >> don't get angry with us. [laughter] >> Lucas, I'm sorry about the Netherlands, man. I wanted them to beat Morocco. All right, anyways, let's get into it right here. We are going to do, Lara, the five biggest storylines we're following during training camp. So, these are kind of your I would call these your like daily check-ins. >> Okay. >> What are we checking in with every day of training camp? How is this progressing? How is that progressing? And how are these things going over the course of uh training camp from July 29th through August 20th when the Colts wrap up camp at Grand Park with a joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons. So, let's get right into it here. Number one. This is my number one storyline. It is >> It is the number one storyline. >> How's Alec Pierce doing? >> Right. I think that's what everyone is going to harp at. Between Daniel Jones and Alec Pierce, I feel like that you kind of you have five storylines, but those are absolutely like your kind of 1A 1B. >> Yeah, they're they're 1A 1B. I'm going with Pierce 1A though because it's we'll get into this with Daniel, but like Alec is almost a little more of an unknown. Right now as we sit here on Monday, July 27th. Like we don't know exactly how he's going to be during training camp, when he's going to get back on the field. >> really hasn't had a serious injury to recover from. >> Exactly, right. Like he's been relatively healthy throughout his time with the Colts. So, just for a little background, just to kind of catch us up here, Alec underwent a procedure on his ankle earlier this spring. He had a PRP injection in it back right after the season. This ankle's been bothering him, he said, Lara, since like the end of the 2024 season. >> Yeah. >> Didn't impact his production in 2025. He was awfully good last year, but it was bothering him and kind of at the the behest of the Colts doctors, trainers, Chris Ballard. >> Still eclipsed 1,000 yards last season. >> Right. He he you know, he and everyone came to the decision that surgery was the best option to kind of alleviate this issue. So, we we don't have a ton of information again, what the first part of training camp's going to look like for him. Is he on PUP? Is he not on PUP? Is he going to come back in a week or two? Is it going to be a couple of weeks? May he not even be out there during training camp at all. These are all questions that I think we'll get a better idea of when Chris Ballard speaks to the media on Tuesday. >> Mhm. >> But, I think just number one Lara, um this is going to be something we're probably going to be checking in with pretty frequently to start off training camp. >> Oh, there's no question that the status and how he starts camp and then how he progresses through are absolutely going to be things that from, you know, our coverage and then I think also from a national standpoint that's going to be a big point of conversation. He doesn't necessarily need the same amount of time with Daniel Jones, with the remainder of the offense. If anything, it's going to be a really great opportunity to look at the rest of the guys behind him, to look at the production of some of, you know, those guys who you have maybe more of who haven't seen as much time, who haven't had the same level of production because you know what Alec Pierce is going to give you. And Now, this being said, with the departure of Michael Pittman Jr., Alec's role will be heavier now within the offense. He's going to have to do a lot more things, but when you look at this is a guy who in consecutive seasons led the league in yards per catch. Like last year averaged 21.3 yards per reception, best of all, receivers in the league eclipsed 1,000 yards. There's just so like I'm not concerned if they're going to be a little more you know, conservative, so to speak, bringing him back in. That being said as well, he did nothing in OTAs and minicamp. He was not out there, right? Because of the recovery from that surgery. And then I was going back to this is a quote that he had when he talked during minicamp and he said, "I think obviously we want the return to be as early as possible, but you've kind of got to let your body guide yourself and see how you feel. Because what I'm learning with the rehab is the more you overdo it, the more sore you get, it kind of it kind of can sometimes be counterproductive." So, I think that's the absolute right approach cuz it's more important to have him early in the regular season than it is to start training camp. So, I wouldn't mind seeing him, you know, maybe starting to work his way in more in terms of that second or third week. >> Yeah, I mean, the the goal for him is get out there week one. And whatever it takes to get out there, you know, to start the season if he's able to do that. Because I think you you bring up a really good point, Lara, like his connection with Daniel Jones was the best on the team last year. Which is funny because a year ago, we're coming in being like, "Okay, well, like how is Alec Pierce going to mesh with Daniel Jones when Daniel hasn't really pushed the ball down field a whole lot in his career?" Turns out those two guys had the the best connection on the team of anyone. >> And what did Alec say that he's been doing when he hasn't had time on the field? He's been sitting with the quarterbacks. And he's been learning more so how they see the field. That was in your article. Right. Just to And so I think that that's only going to help further that connection. There's no replacement. There's no replicating on-field time. Certainly not. However, Alec is one who is going to say, "How can I use this time to still grow and improve and learn and gain benefit from this even if I do have some limitations on what I'm able to do on field." >> So, without Alec, you know, however long he may not practice, you are going to see Ashton Dulin, who I think was already in line to get more time with Michael Pittman Jr. now with the Steelers, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, Laquon Treadwell. Uh could be an opportunity for Deon Burks to get in there. I know Burks isn't your sort of typical outside the numbers X receiver at 5'9, but maybe he kind of slides into that sort of Pittman role. Maybe you got Westbrook-Ikhine and Dulin at the X. The thing that I want to go back to here though, Lara, is like you would love to count on every single player to play 17 games. But if something happens and Alec misses a game here and there during the season, these are going to be very valuable reps because you can't your offense cannot fall apart if Alec Pierce can't play. He's he shouldn't be like this pillar that if you knock it down, the whole thing comes tumbling down. So these are going to be really valuable to figure out how can we operate this offense if Alec is not out there in the event that he can't play. You hope it doesn't happen, but it's just good practice to get these reps right now. >> I also look to the fact that Tyler Warren is going to have a heavier role in the passing game as well this year, too. So when you're talking about the wide receivers, that's also someone who you have to take into account just how much his workload will only continue to increase because he's proven that he can handle it. He's proven that he can do more. You could see how Shane, as the year went on, just kind of added more and then became more multiple in how he uses Tyler Warren. So I think that that this creates that opportunity to to be a little creative with your offense and those pieces when you don't have Alec out on the field. You mentioned my Hoosier, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. I looked back and in 2024, this is when he was with Tennessee, he averaged 15.5 yards per catch with a long of 98 yards. So to me, that's >> like he caught like a 40-yard touchdown against the Colts every year. [laughter] >> I've so many of those that I can recall. So that's got to That was an interesting when I was like, "Okay, like I know last year in Miami wasn't the season he wanted to have and that's what really created the opportunity obviously for the >> he wanted to have in Miami last year, [laughter] let's be honest. >> Touche. But, that created the opportunity obviously for him to come to Indianapolis. So, I went back and you know, kind of saw what he was doing previously in Tennessee and that really gave some indication of maybe that, you know, type of skill set that he could potentially bring to Shane's offense. >> By the way, the the one wide receiver we haven't mentioned here is Josh Downs. We're going to get to him in a later storyline topic. Let's move on to number two though, Lara. Daniel Jones. Which again, this is 1B, right? And it makes sense, right? The Colts paid a lot of money to keep Alec Pierce and Daniel Jones together this offseason. Daniel Jones it just it comes down to what is he able to do from the jump, right? Like he was able to do seven on seven during OTAs. I am sure Daniel Jones tried to get on the field for 11 on 11 and everyone was like, "Ah, you don't need to do that." Um, but what is he able to do? Is he able to do 11 on 11? When is he able to do that? And then it's it's just how does he look? How does it feel out there with Daniel Jones behind center once again? >> I think it should feel exactly like it felt the start of the season last year. As much as possible. There's no reason to think that it shouldn't when you have the majority of those pieces back together. Obviously, you're going to have a little bit of rotation on the offensive line, but the majority of that offense is going to be intact. So, I think it should very much feel the same and you want Daniel when he's on the field to be out there running the offense with zero limitations because you have seen how much that offense hinges on his ability, his movement, you know, obviously like his ability to make plays with his legs, make throws on the run, all of those things. Once he had the fracture in his leg and his mobility was so hampered, you saw obviously the, you know, impact on the offense and what he was able to do. So, yeah, if he's out there, it needs to be full go and you need to be able to see absolutely everything in his arsenal because that's what the offense is going to be working with, right? It I don't know that it really gives you much benefit to say he's going to go out, but we're only going to stay within this scope of what he's doing out there. >> Yeah, he's not going to be a statue out there. >> No. >> Um I I think I've I've seen this and I've got this question a lot of like, okay, well, Kirk Cousins really struggled to move after the Achilles, after he did his Achilles. Aaron Rodgers really struggled to move after he did his Achilles. Well, Kirk Cousins was like 36. As a 37-year-old, I, you know, bump my knee and I'm like, I can't move for a week. Uh Aaron Rodgers was 41 when he did his Achilles. You're You're talking about a 29-year-old Daniel Jones who baseline is a better athlete than those two guys. >> Daniel Jones came out of Duke as one of the better athletes to play the quarterback position we've seen in the last decade. But this is where I think the mobility thing, we need to really clarify what that means. Because I think people look at Daniel Jones and they remember what he did with the Giants where he was running a lot. Um and that was kind of a big part of their For Daniel Jones, in 2026, he averaged 3.5 rushing attempts per game. That was his lowest since his rookie year in 2019. I looked this up on Pro Football Focus, designed runs that were called for Daniel Jones from 2019 to 2025. In 2019, it was six. Then 26 in 2020, 25 in 2021, 43 in 2022, 13 in 2023. I think that was his ACL year. 32 in 2024, last year, Lera, three. One of those was an aborted snap. >> The Colts had two designed runs for him in the first three weeks of the season. They just said, "Ah, we don't need this." Got rid of it in their offense after that. What the Colts were able to do with Daniel Jones and his mobility was get him on those kind of boots and half rolls that you can just like picture it in your head. Him just throwing to Tyler Warren in like an ocean of space on play action. So, last year, uh this is from Pro Football uh or Pro Football Focus, 36 play action dropbacks with a rollout for Daniel Jones. He completed 31 passes on those plays for 9.3 yd per attempt and a passer rating it off of 112.3. Against the Chargers, he went five for five on those and like that game I I highlighted that game in my mind because, okay, the first defense that Daniel Jones will see in the regular season will be Jesse Minter's defense, who is the Chargers DC, who is now the Ravens head coach. >> Yep. >> So, like you're going to need him doing that kind of right off the jump because that is a really big part of the offense. The The last thing here, Laura, cuz I Dude, I fell down a rabbit hole on this. Uh like I haven't I haven't fallen down a football rabbit hole in so long. I got so excited about it. Uh per next gen stats, Daniel Jones last year threw on the run. So, like on the run. This is like This isn't your kind of rollout. This is like picture Caleb Williams running for his life and probably throwing a touchdown to Cole Kmet. Daniel Jones threw on the run on 10.2% of his dropbacks last year. That was between Joe Flacco and Aaron Rodgers for the fourth lowest rate in the NFL. >> Wow. >> He's not throwing on the on the run run a lot, but he is throwing on the move a little bit. Last year, um he threw on uh he had the ninth highest designed rollout rate last year in the NFL. So, like again, it's it's the rollouts. It's not on the run. He's not going to scramble a ton. So, it's can he throw on those rollouts, on the move, not on the run, and then can he avoid pressure? Last year, his he had the 10th lowest pressure to sack rate in the NFL at 14.6%. So, this is kind of just little slides in the pocket. That's a very long way of saying those are the kind of movements I'm looking for from Daniel Jones in training camp. >> Absolutely. That's exactly what you what you need to see. And I also think that that's what that's how Daniel plays most confidently. So, that's putting him in the best position, too. >> And and I think that the thing that I I'm so just I I think about with this offense so much more than Daniel Jones' athleticism or his mobility. And I think there still is going to be that threat. Mhm. But, it's not like the Colts leaned into it last year. It was more just like this is a threat, you got to respect it, and it's going to help open a lot up for our offense. All right. So you have a lot of guys that you have made a big investment in that are all within that back end of your defense. Yeah. The Colts started last season hot. >> Seven and one? >> Well, I mean, but even just three and oh. >> Right? Where that had been kind of an issue. >> best offense in the league through the first month of the season. >> just the best offense in the league, it was historically good what they were doing. I think that the other thing I was thinking about though is like, okay, they had this hot start last year. But early in training camp, I mean, I remember like making the note over and over again of like, it's hard for them to move the ball through the air. Be and you know, Tyler Warren was showing up. title: Colts Owner Kalen Jackson on HS Girls Flag Football in Indiana
text: Hi everybody. Welcome. Is everyone having a good weekend? Yes. It's been so, so incredible to have this incredible NFL talent poll event here in our own backyard. Westfield, of course, has been such an incredible host. Um and I know everyone's been having so much fun. I've been out here every single day and the weather's been great. We were saying that we should just continue to have NFL events here because the weather continues to bless us. The Super Bowl was amazing when it was here and now this. So, um thank you guys for all being here. It's an incredible day for us and we're really, really excited to be talking to you about our special announcement today. Um obviously, it goes without saying, we feel football is an incredible and powerful sport. It creates so many different opportunities for youth um and adults alike. You learn so much from teamwork, leadership, confidence, resilience. And I think especially with girls, you find that leadership roles are able to happen that much more when they're able to be a part of the youth sports. And so, being able to create more of those opportunities through our girls flag programming is really incredible and is aligned with everything we hope to do in this state um and beyond. So, everyone obviously should have a chance to participate in this amazing sport. And for years, girls have not had that opportunity. And so, like I said, everything that we've been doing through girls flag is really for you girls. Um and it's really been fun to get to know some of you, get to meet some of you, get to meet your incredible parents who've been working so hard and signing petitions and and speaking out for you all and on behalf of you all so that you guys can have these pathways and opportunities past high school and into college and university, which we know that continues to grow. So, we began our efforts in 2023 with only eight original schools, which I know we have a representative from each of those standing here in front of you. And we grew to 27 schools in 2024 and then 78 last season, which is incredible. And I think the growth that quickly shows you the interest and the passion, the dedication that is there. But to be officially sanctioned by the IHSA, we had to get to 100 schools to be com- to compete. So, we launched the Road to 100 campaign, which I'm hopeful a lot of people know about, but we committed a million dollars to get this done. We're up to each school would get up to $10,000 of financial help, but it wasn't just that for us. You know, I have to give a shout-out to Annie Medias and our entire staff. They have done an incredible job. I mean, beyond what anyone sees. Calls, they would be visiting schools, not taking no for an answer, and that is how we have gotten to where we've gotten because of them. And so, I had to give them a shout-out because it wasn't just the fin- financial part. For a lot of schools, they needed refs. We hosted, you know, a free training for 500 referees statewide so that whenever this happened, everything would be ready for you girls. And today, I'm proud to announce we have arrived at 100 schools! Woo! Leave it to Blue to bring the the fun with the streamers. So, we are thrilled to announce that we officially have 108 high schools committed across Indiana. That means we are on track for girls flag to become a fully sanctioned sport in 2027. And I think that is deserves another round of applause. >> [applause] [cheering] >> But although the Road to 100 is complete, the road ahead is even more exciting and we're truly just getting started. So, everybody get ready. Yay! >> [cheering]

text: Okay, uh it's good to see everybody. Hopefully everybody had a good little break. Um couple things that I'll start off with. You know, we're obviously very excited to get going. title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba: "We Want To Create A New Story With This Upcoming Season" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Hello, hello. >> What's going on? >> Good, good. >> What if anything is different coming to training camp as a champ and the reigning MVP? >> Um You can feel the excitement, you can feel the energy, definitely. Um having a great year is definitely awesome and we want to repeat that, of course, but I think just coming in there's been a new energy, just a kind of a fresh start and ready to get going, ready for to take the next step, you know, as a team and a new beginning, so to speak. So, we're excited and um we're juiced up to to get it going. >> Is it hard to do that when you know what success feels like and tastes like? Wasn't that long ago? >> Yeah, it wasn't that long ago. Um you know, we want to create Of course, it's going to be a new story, but we want to create, you know, our a new story with this upcoming season and um because it's different and you know, we do have different guys, we got different people in the building, so it's going to be a unique story and yeah, a unique challenge different from last year, so we're excited to to take it on. >> What's the next step for you? >> Next step is, you know, to grow. You know, I want I want y'all to see a different level, uh almost a different player out there and just kind of a upgraded version. >> Different in what way? >> Um in all ways. I've I always say, you know, I can get better in all areas and I think year two with Sam Darnold and the receiver core that we have, um you know, just our group, you know, taking another step as we go into a new year is is something special and something that I feel like we can continue to grow. >> What about Shi Smith? What are your thoughts on him coming in last year mid-season? Do you think he's kind of a different version of him, more comfortable in the offense or anything? >> 1000%. I'm happy he gets, you know, to kind of have a full season, a full off-season, and a training camp. Um, you know, definitely excited for him. Uh, him getting connected with him as well, like I said, just taking that year or two step is going to be big for all of us, especially, you know, in the receiving room. >> You had four offensive coordinators in four years. Uh, when you talk to an OC, what gets you excited about their plan for you? >> Yeah, um, really just the excitement, you know, that, you know, Flory brings to the offense, you know, and him just understanding the players, understanding, you know, what we're good at, and, you know, having offensive coordinators and, um, in this business, you know, actions speak louder than words. So, you know, just getting out here, it's good to get out here and, you know, put your foot in the grass, catch a few balls, and, and see, you know, um, what we have, so, and where we're going. So, it's been it's been great so far. >> Saw the receivers doing some push-ups after practice. >> Yeah. A a little extra stuff, a little extra stuff. >> Been doing it for years. >> Okay. >> Leadership, how do you feel about your leadership? More expectations or just how is that evolved, I should say? >> Yeah, definitely going to evolve, you know, a lot more eyes, a lot more cameras, of course, and, um, just building relationships with my guys. We preach relationships is everything in this building. So, um, for me to grow that and, you know, to understand my teammates, you know, that's that's where I play my best, just understanding them and playing for them and and giving back to those guys and and [music] knowing, you know, they can count on me and vice versa, so, um, I'm excited for that that new step and kind of a new role. >> Did you have a a view of, uh, Cooper's catch down the left sideline? >> I did. >> What did you think of it? >> Man, that's Cooper Kupp for you, you know, great con- concentration with the left hand, diving. I mean, you know, really see that often. Um, you know, but him, he kind of makes it regular and, you know, brushes it off, but it's spectacular play and, you know, something he definitely has in his arsenal, still has in his arsenal. >> What beyond the just the play making with him? Like what what does he bring to the receiver room as a guy who's, you know, been around for a while? >> Yeah, I mean, he brings a high level of, you know, confidence and high level of just learning and understanding what we want to do and what the defense is trying to do it. Like I said it before, it's just like having an extra coach out there. So, um you know, for him, everybody trusts him. He's our He's our leader um in the receiver room and on the team. So, you know, if you follow him, you know, you you're doing something right. You're good. >> What can you already tell about Brian Flores' offense? >> Uh right now, I mean, you know, we're just putting in a lot of basic stuff and we want to be good at the basics. We want to be good at the fundamentals. We want to be good after the catch. Um we want to be great, actually, and um just take those short gains and and turn them into long runs and, you know, smashmouth football. You know, that's that's how we love to play and the defense is going to have to react to us and we're just going to keep punching it down their throats. >> When you're prepping for an opponent, how much how much do you guys are spending on the players versus the scheme? Which is which is good takes more of your time? really I I mean, I would say both. Um at first, I love to jump into the scheme and and what they're doing. And so, I'll spend, you know, a couple days doing that. So, I understand what they're doing and I can go into practice and kind of understand the looks and then I dive in deeper into the players and what they like to do, the tendencies they like to do, so we can exploit them. >> Mike Mike keeps saying he's he feels like the same guy despite having just won a Super Bowl in your two years as a head coach. Have Have you seen any change in him at all? >> No. And really, no one in the building. It's just kind of our DNA. You know, it was great. The Super Bowl was great, you know, love to have it, but at the end of the day, we got to brush that off to the side. You know, no one really cares once we line it up, you know, first snap this season. >> Jackson, with the prank coming into the season, what's the balance of trying to do things you're good at last year but still adapting, innovating, doing new things with him and the stuff that he uses? Like he kind of knows that he's got your back on >> Yeah, I love I love new new stuff and new perspective, you know, as a player, it's your chance to grow. And for me, I feel like whatever the coach asks, I can do it. And so, it's it's kind of cool just having a different mindset, a different coach, you know, in there. It's be able to grow my game and to an all around game, more all around game and that's kind of how we feel as a whole offense. >> It used to be that there was kind of a classic X receiver, Z receiver, slot. >> It's kind of changed now. People play all sorts of places. Did you have an idea when you were growing up what kind of receiver you wanted to be? >> Mhm. No, I didn't. Um always, you know, watch the ABs and the Dez Bryants and the Larry Fitzgeralds. And those guys really lined up everywhere. So, you know, I just wanted to be versatile to where I can line up literally anywhere, wherever the coach coach needs, you know, it's easy to get the ball in my hands and and turn up. So, that that's kind of the receiver I wanted to be. Yes, sir. Uh yes, sir, I got you. Of course. >> God bless you, young man. >> God bless you. >> Jackson, going back to the ability to play multiple receiver positions, what's the skill set you need? Balance, speed, what are those things, basic skills you need to be able to play the multiple receiver positions? >> Yeah, and I think I think uh what's great about it, we have a lot of receivers and our receivers that can play different positions, which allows me to line up anywhere on the field as well. And um you know, I try to make everything look the same. You know, I'm not the tallest receiver, so you know, I can I can sell and make everything kind of look the same like I said. Um and I think inside and outside, you know, that's that's kind of hard to detect and and to cover. >> Jackson, D-Law just just crashed your presser. You're a Texas guy. Since he got here last year, what's he meant to >> Man. Man, I I know there's a clip of me just saying, yeah, I'm so thankful to have him on my team. Um he's been a difference-maker, a leader. Um everything, you know, you would want in a superstar. And since he came in the building, he's been all about business and brought that just brought that killer mode another killer to the defense and into our team. So, that's been awesome. I don't know if I can say that, but yeah, he's not literally, but >> He's instinctively >> What's What was your Did I see you were in Japan at some point? >> Oh, yeah, yeah, I was in Japan getting my karate right a little bit. >> [laughter] >> What was that trip like? >> It was awesome. It was awesome. I got to go with family, with my brother, and just right after the season, just kind of get away. Um you know, eat some good food. I love the culture there. And just kind of sit back, relax, um enjoy, you know, Tokyo and everything that, you know, it brings. It's a special place. >> Did you Did it help your off season? I mean, did did you get your contract done when when you did and kind of get that off your the way off your shoulders? >> It was a blessing to, you know, get it done. Um almost seems like forever ago. Um but it's a blessing to get it done and and really focus on, you know, um this season and being with my teammates and just being here and and and pushing forward. >> Jackson, last year you went to Spain, as well. Is there something about going overseas, getting out of the country that that's something that kind of does it for you? And then what do you think you got out of those experiences overall when you've done when you've done >> Yeah, I do like to travel. I love to travel and just experience different cultures and different different places, different people. I think for me like it's good for me to to take a break, but I'm always learning and you know, trying to get better. That's just who I am and that Spain trip I got to to meet a lot of Real Real Madrid players and get with Vinny uh Junior and just uh learn, you know, what he does and how he goes about his business, which was which was um very inspiring and got to pick up a lot of things to add to add to to myself, my life and and what I do. >> Along the same lines of travel, Fashion Week in Paris, you got a lot of stars all in the same room. What was that experience like? >> Oh, it was cool. It was super cool. Um you know, great experience with uh Pascal the watch um company. Got some Sierra Leone ties in there and just uh to meet, you know, guys my brothers from the NFL. Um it was just awesome to sit down and you know, just chop it up in a in a new setting. Um you know, it's it is a brotherhood in the league, so to see, you know, the NFL guys around the world is definitely cool and it's a once-in-a-lifetime experience, yeah. >> All right. Thanks, Jeff. >> Thanks, Jeff.
