But nevertheless, it seems like he's found a a pretty soft landing spot there with the Colts. They brought back Alec Pierce. They have Ty Tyler Warren at tight end. Jonathan Taylor, Quenton Nelson, a road grader up front in the interior of their offensive line. So, the big question I'm still going to have and I I think because the sample size wasn't large enough last year is Daniel Jones being able to replicate what he was able to do. And I I I think because he's been such a polarizing player in his career, it's hard for me to fully dive in and believe in what I saw last year, but we'll see what Shane Steichen and the offense has up their sleeve. >> Are you out on Anthony Richardson? Like if he had a play, you think that he's a salvageable quarterback prospect? >> Nah, I'm kind of out on him, Mike. I I I think that a lot of his shortcomings have never totally been rectified. I understand that he hasn't really been much of a factor of late, but I I just haven't seen him take enough of enough steps forward to suggest to me that he's ready to be a starting caliber quarterback in the NFL or even give adequate production if he has to step in in the interim. >> You think about this, too, Andrew. They went eight and two. They averaged 32 points per game and then went 0 and 7 averaging 20 points a game. They were the first team ever to be six games over .500 and finish with a losing record and they're the first team since 1995's Raiders to start eight and two and miss the playoffs. So, a lot of that too, their defense. They traded for Sauce Gardner. They thought this team was legit, but their defense had all sorts of problems last year as well. >> Yeah, I mean they were a leaky group there and it's kind of it's kind of surprising when you think of it, but yeah, you mentioned Sauce Gardner. They lost safety Nick Cross in free agency to the Washington Commanders. I think Nick Cross uh again, I mentioned this with Jaylon Thompson, the Cowboys safety who they signed as well, but I think he is one of the more underrated younger safeties in the league, really productive. I'm curious to see how they go about replicating that production, but they have they have a lot of areas of need there. Um I do like Justin Walley, their nickel corner out of Minnesota. He's been a couple years in now. I like him quite a bit coming out of the draft and and he's someone that I think stabilizes that uh that nickel back role, but um yeah, they they still have some some room to grow there. I'm not quite sure that they have enough on that side of the ball to uh to take it to to take it as far as they needed to take it. >> Uh also lost Michael Pittman to the Steelers. We talked about him last week. Uh they drafted C.J. Allen for the defense, a safety as well. So, they did focus a little bit on the defense side. The Eagles will face them on Saturday, the 7th of the 19th. And we know one guy we didn't bring up, Jonathan Taylor. I mean, he was the one bright spot on that team. Dude's a absolute stud. Uh so, they will probably look to get him highly involved this year. And T.J. Taylor Warren, the tight end, is another guy who uh we didn't really mention much there, but Warren and Taylor, two of the better guys to do it at their positions. >> Yeah, yeah, I mean when you have cornerstone players like that, um and Alec Pierce, whatever you want to say about him, I I I don't know that he's a true number one, but he's certainly being compensated as such. He's someone who can stretch teams vertically. I I like his contested catchability. I think he's probably more of a complimentary piece, but they have players at at premier positions that I think can be difference-makers, and it's all going to come down to Daniel Jones and what they're going to be able to get out of him. Will he revert back to his previous form with the Giants, or is he going to kind of continue on where he left off with the Colts? And I'm sure the Colts are banking on him him returning to form because they have enough pieces there, I think, to to be able to put up some points. >> All right. Uh Tennessee, the Eagles will play the Titans on the 20th of uh September, week number two. And uh the biggest question we all know, Andrew, is can this young offense uh Cam Ward lead this offense to have a much better season than they had a year ago? >> Yeah, I'm I'm a little bit more optimistic on Cam Ward maybe than than some others are, and I certainly like what they've done surrounding him with with some talent. Uh Cornell Tate in the first round, and they have uh Calvin Ridley. So, and Wan'Dale Robinson they added as well. So, he's going to have weapons this year, and there's not a lot of excuses. However, at running back, you look at Tony Pollard. Uh I don't know that he's really going to move the needle. Uh Tajae Spears is really an undersized player, a complimentary piece, someone who can be a good pass-catching running back, uh you know, create yards after the catch, but uh I'm not overly enthused with their running situation right now, but yeah, I mean, I you have to be enthused with where they are with uh with their receiving options. >> Yeah, you mentioned uh Ridley. I mean, you got Wan'Dale Robinson you brought in, Ridley they drafted, Tate, Tony Pollard. So, we'll see there, but obviously the offensive line, uh that's one of the problem. When you get these teams with the young quarterbacks, they generally don't have the offensive line uh to stand up in front. So, that's going to be a big factor there. They did hire Robert Saleh, a defensive-minded guy. What do you like about this defense that maybe can make them competitive? >> Well, up front, John Franklin-Myers, uh he's not talked about nearly enough. You have Jeffery Simmons, who's one of the best interior lineman in football. And then on the back end, I I I I like uh Alontae Taylor, who they signed. Uh he's someone that I think could could make a little bit of a difference there. Uh he's comes over from the Saints. This is going to be an a more aggressive attack-style defense, I think, with Robert Saleh. They're going to play with an edge, and well, they they should have some energy. I still think that this is a young team, by and large, that they're not necessarily ready to take the next step just yet, but I think Cam Ward and the offense will will take some uh will make some encouraging strides forward and and give uh Tennessee Titans fans something to be optimistic about. >> Solid defensive guy. They got Cam Ward. Brian Daboll is the new offensive coordinator in Tennessee. So, uh he'll be kind of um working with the offense and Ward. Saleh with the defense there. The Titans are the worst team in the NFL over the past two seasons with six wins. They were uh last or near the bottom in almost every single defensive category last year. Uh so, we'll see if they can improve on that. They play the Eagles in week number two. A look at the Tennessee Titans. That is the AFC South. They will play the NFC East this year. All right, Andrew, as you take a look at those four teams, Jacksonville, Houston, Indianapolis, Tennessee, how do you see them finishing? >> Houston, Jacksonville, Indianapolis, Tennessee. >> All right. So, you're not buying a lot of these people think Tennessee is one of those teams that go uh you know, from worst play from worst to maybe first or even make a playoff. I hear a lot of people jumping on the Tennessee. You don't seem to be following that. I'm with you. I don't see Tennessee making a big leap. >> young. They're young. I I I can see the vision. I think they're maybe a year or two away from from checking off that box, Mike, but I love the Houston Texans this year. I like what they've done just sort of building around what they already had, some of the pieces defensively adding Reed Blankenship, and they just have so many interchangeable pieces on the back end. DeMeco Ryans there leading the way, and we'll see what C.J. Stroud is able to do. Will his confidence be shaken now off of that playoff performance? And do how how much are they ultimately going to lean on David Montgomery? But I I like what they've done in particular. >> All right, Andrew Checo Football Four powered by the Inside the Birds podcast, and of course our division previews continue next week with the AFC West. We'll do that here on the Sports Bash. All right, Andrew, thanks, man. >> Thanks, Mike. Take care.

title: Henry Josey Is An Eagles Training Camp RB Legend – And Eagles Fans Still Reach Out To Him
text: [music] >> Hello and welcome in to another episode of the Jaco daily a special edition of the Jaco daily because I'm joined by former Eagles running back Henry Jose who signed as an undrafted free agent in 2014. Henry, how you doing? >> I'm doing good man. Welcome and it's good to be welcomed back in definitely miss the Eagle tribe always but definitely good to get back in and just talk a little bit about my time there in Philly. >> Well, I'm really looking forward to diving in but before we get to your training camp stories going into your I guess after your junior season you decided to forego your senior year and go into the NFL draft. What gave you the the confidence? What was the pre-draft cycle like for you and what were some of the teams that were interested? >> A lot of confidence got a good rating for sure that definitely sparked my interest also started weighing in just my options for how long my knee actually was going to last after the injury I suffered in college and eventually that turned into a decision for me to forego that last year had my little one that was already here and running around the house so definitely was a decision where I sat down held his hand said a little prayer is like hey we're just going to go for it and that was my my decision to go forward with that had a multitude of teams that were interested of course I did a few visits off the top of my head where did I go Chicago Minnesota There was one more place I went to as well. I just can't it's been a little while. But definitely had a lot of interest from a a lot of different teams and mostly one of the I think one of the biggest key things that a lot of teams want to see was if I can actually pass block, which uh that was probably one of the common denominators, but uh definitely figured that out in the end that that was not an issue at all. >> So, you were part of the Eagles 2014 undrafted rookie free agent class. What did you know about Philadelphia? I understand that you had some Missouri alums there in Jeremy Maclin and Brad Smith, but other than that, Henry, what did you know about the city when you got there? >> That is funny. Absolutely nothing. Uh I think the only thing I probably could remember is uh the Rocky movies and that's the only thing that kind of rung a bell when you thought about Philly. I mean, then of course getting there and seeing the statue just kind of made all that stuff uh come into play and just make uh some childhood memories come back to me pretty good. >> Chip Kelly was the head coach there. What were your early impressions of his offense? >> Uh very similar to what I've been in my whole college career. Uh very uh fast-paced, up-tempo type of offense. Um very much enjoyed that part of it. A lot of just uh the simple ways to uh make things happen. So, uh definitely enjoyed that part of it and just the way it was definitely different. Um you talk about tempo, he uh he has a mastermind with creating tempo that probably doesn't make sense to most people um out in the world, definitely. Um you have to be on the go. Um you definitely had to take care of your body right after practice because you are going to be tired. I'm, you know, I can't even go back and think about how many steps or how many miles I ran um just in practice. I'm like, this is bananas. You know, we used to read uh have our little readings on us from uh some of the equipment back in the day and it's like, I am in the red every day. So, something is not right. Uh but, you know, you recover from it. You go back and do it do it again the next day and uh you go back and just keep that recovery process going. >> From a recovery standpoint, now that you mentioned it, what were some of the measures that you had to take to ensure that you were available and close to full strength every day at practice? >> Uh of course eating right is going to be the key. Um sleep is probably the hardest part for anybody. Um, but you got to at least try to get some rest. Um, I know I'm not one of those big guys on going to sleep and just crashing out. Um, so long as I lay down, close my eyes and got some rest, got some good recovery. Uh, do the cold tub, hot tub, you know, do that contrast. I'm any kind of extra things I could do at night before bed, stretching and rolling out. And then honestly trying to make sure I get another little shake in before I go to bed so I can get a little extra recovery in. Make sure my belly is full and my body's getting refilled the way it needed to be. >> Duce Staley was the running backs coach at the time, had a storied career in Philadelphia. Did he have a message for you as a young player to help you navigate and maybe put you in a in a certain mindset going through that first training camp? >> Uh, I mean he was very very open about of course his his his career more more importantly. I'm just very honest about things that we need to work on. I think that was the key thing. He never ever just, you know, beat around the bush about anything. Very straightforward, hey you need to do it this better. Hey, you need to do it this way. And then honestly if you did it that way it stuff started clicking and making sense. And that was probably one of the easiest things. Plus having those other guys that were older than me with the experience being able to piggyback off of them. And then you're around so much confidence in one room um, from the coach down to the players. Like it's just it's hard not to want to elevate your game. And that was one of the key things that helped me out throughout that preseason in my stint in Philly. >> Looking back, what do you consider to be your welcome to the NFL moment? >> Wow. Um, [snorts] I'll probably say my first pass blocking practice. Uh, with the guy who's probably I don't even know how tall he was. At least six something. I was like, hey, we got to block him and he's like huge. I'm like, holy moly. Like this is this is eye-opening. Um, and then I remember one it was I think we played the Steelers in a preseason game. Uh, Polamalu comes over and like barely misses me. I dove up under him cuz I knew he was coming, and I was like, "Hey, this is this is fast-paced. Like, this is not a game you can play around with. You know, you can easily be able to get down and protect your body, but seeing a guy at that magnitude, at his level of play, coming in that way, um and you know, getting out of the way was like one of the probably scariest things ever." >> Now, if I remember correctly, that summer Chris Polk, another running back, dealt with a hamstring injury, so he missed a lot of training camp, which gave you a lot of opportunities. >> Yeah. >> How do you feel that you fared during practices? >> Um I think that gave a a lot of balance for me. I think it's mostly in practice. Practice is something where I actually go out and I practice things. My practice play the game play are totally different. Um and I think that was probably one of the biggest eye-opening things for everybody. Like, I think one of the guys uh after one of my games where I had a big breakout game, he was like, "Man, I always thought you was hurt." It's like, "Nah, I'm just like I I'm processing stuff. I'm thinking about stuff on the go. Uh I ain't hurt. It's just, you know, it's just how I practice. Um it's not No, it doesn't decide how I'm going to play in the game. Like, my tempo speeds up. My everything goes a lot faster in the game, because you done all the work at practice. But, him going down definitely opened up a lot of opportunities for me. Like, maybe maybe to slide up in that spot. Um hey, when Sproles and them needed a break, I'd jump in and fill in for them. So, it just got me more reps. Um I had my own reps in with the ones and twos, and also I would have my reps with the threes as well by myself, and then whoever wasn't there, I'd have to fill in for it. >> Now, you mentioned Darren Sproles, and I'm sure you've drawn a lot of comparisons to him during your football career in stature, but also in skillset. Did you and Darren ever have those conversations, and how helpful was he uh during your early days there in Philadelphia? >> Oh, yeah. That's that's my big bro right there. He uh he definitely was helpful um from not just a football standpoint, um from the fatherhood side to, "Hey, this is the way the game works. This is the way the system works. This is the way the world works in this bubble of what we're in." Um so, he was very, very informational. Um, definitely led by example, but then also voiced as well um, just how he can be helpful and uh he was he was man, like I said, he was a big brother, man. He made life very simple for me. Um, I gravitated towards him just cuz of our style of playing and just also how well he showed up to practice and worked every single day. He was His numbers were three times higher than mine on on an average day for practice we were running around. So, you think about a guy at this age, this magnitude, he's been this doing this thing at this level for so long and you get to not only sit here and watch him do it, but also get to ask him questions, um get to have different feedback, um you know, when you're in your film room, you get to ask him certain questions and he sees things that other people are not going to see because he's been in the game so long. And just so it was great to see all that, understand how to read certain, you know, certain defenses and understand certain alignments. So, he he was very helpful throughout my whole um career in Philly. >> Now, were you aware that you were becoming sort of a a phenomenon around the city of Philadelphia? There was a lot of interest about you. Your name was making some headlines in practice and of course in the preseason. Were you aware of that, Henry, or were you sort of just locked in on the task at hand? >> Uh I'm always locked in, for sure. Um, you definitely hear the noise. You got to take note of it, though. I think a lot of people can get wrapped up in the noise pretty quickly and that can ruin just how your perception of what you need to do on a day-to-day and how that actually is going to play out for you. So, um I definitely heard the noise, but it was more of hey, I got to stay focused on what I need to stay on um cuz at any moment hey, I can get hurt and then there's next man up. That is the way the NFL works. Um, and once that next man up comes through, his opportunity outshines you, then you kind of just hey, I got to I don't know if I'm going to get a chance, but I got maybe one shot um to go out here and make it happen again and then sometimes it's just too late. >> Now, not including the preseason games, we're we're going to get to that in a moment, but was there ever a moment during practices where you sort of told yourself, I can play in this league? >> Yeah, yeah, definitely. Once I started getting more reps, once I started feeling like myself, that's when I started actually getting into it. I think that Patriots run we had, that was my first time being able to get so a lot more action, get a lot more confidence cuz that's, you know, we're going against ourselves all the time. And then once you finally go against somebody else, you not say lose the friendship aspect, but all right, I'm not going to, you know, go as hard this play or hey, this is my buddy. I'mma block him and I know he's going to do this. Just you know, you have certain people you have that relationship, you know what they're going to do and y'all getting to work in. When you go out and actually face someone else, you know, things kind of change, your perspective change, your mindset is on a different thing when you you have a different opponent across from you. So, I would say that Patriots run we did that joint practice was when I was like, all right, this is I'm I'm ready to go. It's It's time to time to make some things happen. >> What are your lasting memories from your first game at Lincoln Financial Field? >> Oh, it was awesome. Those are they're the best fans and they can also be the worst fans if you >> [laughter] >> you're not doing your job. So, I think the key for me with them is like I had a great time in Philly. I got the love from the fans. And also like they when I say they love you, they love you. And as long as you're doing your job, showing up, making things happen, making plays, bringing excitement to that field, it was awesome. I mean, the night I think we play Yeah, we did play some two at least two night games there, I want to say. Yeah, one day and one night game. The night game atmosphere was absolutely awesome. Seeing seeing out, seeing the open field, the lights shining. Like it was just an amazing feeling. Definitely. And then of course the weather felt very great at night. >> Now, in the preseason finale, you rushed for 121 yards on 22 carries. You rushed for in total that preseason 225 yards on 34 carries. What do you remember from that finale? And I guess how how did you process what was going on in the aftermath of that game? >> Um >> [sighs and gasps] >> I think more of just enjoying it. I think that was probably the biggest part. Like you come into the league and you're like you're so nervous about every single thing. I was able to be around Shady. I was able to be around Sproles. I was able to watch their game. I was able to watch how they took practice and then put it into play. And ultimately at the same time they were just being themselves. Um Deuce never stopped us from being ourselves. Now the only thing he would argue with us about is of course how we carried the ball. Uh if we didn't have it high and tight, but that's that elusiveness that just comes with the confidence. Like you know when to Um and I think that was one of the main things that made life easy for me in Philly because we were able to be ourselves and enjoy running the ball the way we wanted to. And that was that was a a a very big key for for me um especially being around those guys and just seeing how confident they were as soon as they got on the field. Like that was a a big boost for me. Um like I said that Patriots game getting there, finally getting in the end zone. Those were amazing feelings like that. Those are the things you need as a running back cuz it it it builds up some consistency. It builds up hey I can do this. And like that that was one of those things that stood out for me. Hey I just got in the end zone, man. I it's it's go time. And that was kind of it. The history was like me and hey this ain't the pudding now. This is time to go play ball. >> Now there was a a lot of outrage when you didn't make the team. I I I can recall that pretty vividly. But after that game, that finale, I'm sure you felt good about yourself. Did you feel you had the team made at that point, Henry? >> Um I had a great feeling about it. I think at the end of the day I wasn't wasn't I was not worried about it in that aspect of hey if I get cut, I get cut. I knew I would get another opportunity somewhere. Um but definitely wanted to be in Philly. Like I was out to eat with my um girl at the time and of course my son. Um and we were just enjoying uh enjoying a lunch down in Philly and then of course I do get the call to come into the office and like oh crap. Hey I got to go. Uh so that that probably is probably the hardest part, but at the end of the day I did enjoy it. Um my oldest now he's 15. Um he got to be in Philly. He got to come to a game. He got to get a a game ball. I think we still have a picture of him with a football in his hand. So, I think as far as the moments I had there, I enjoyed that fully. So, it really it didn't hurt me at the end of the day. It was just hey, wherever I go next, that's where I go. And that was the most thing I was most excited about. I got I'm living out my dream at the end of the day. I wasn't I was not supposed to play football again after my 2011 injury in college. So, to be able to get up and not only come back from that injury, people telling me I'll never walk again, to be able to play and then also be able to live out my dream and be able to play play in the NFL like I I I have nothing to complain about and I have nothing to regret about my career or time in >> Now, you bring up something really important that I want to touch on. And for those who don't know, in 2011, you dealt with a devastating knee injury that required three different surgeries. You just alluded to it, Henry. Could you describe what that whole process entailed? How did the injury happen? And what was the recovery process like? >> Uh well, it was a another enjoyable game. I'll tell you that much. Uh playing against a great opponent, Texas. It's crazy, two of my guys from here in my hometown playing against them. One of them my best friends. I've had a long extensive career. Quandre Dixon, he had a great career. So, being able to be on the field with them was a a big thing for us, you know, especially coming from our small little town here in Angleton, Texas. But it was it was a uh surreal moment for me. Just running out of bounds, normal play. I was like, yeah, I might squeeze like another yard out. I might have a guy who barely grabs the back of my jersey. I end up folding up under my left leg and dislocating left knee. Kneecap's on the inside of my knee. So, I got a nice little hole in my in my leg and I I looked at it a few times, tried to move it. Is this real? [laughter] Basically, I just started screaming. Uh so, that was a crazy thing to go through. Straight to the hospital right from the game. Um, and then of course the recovery time was over 370 something days, I want to say, maybe. I can't think of that number off top of my head, but it was a long process. Um, some long days, uh, some long mental days, very, very bad days. But, I had a a great crew behind me, even you know, through the tough times. I think we all probably shed a few tears together. Cuz some of the things they had to do to me, it was just like it was excruciating for me to go through and at the same time it's like, "Hey, I have to go through it if I want to pursue this again." So, um, and it was something that's definitely in my mind. It did take me a while to get up and start believing everything was real. Um, but eventually, um, I caught on to it, and I threw the pain pills in the trash and and jumped on it and said, "Hey, let's go. Let's go get after it. I got to go get healthy." And, um, once I had that mindset flip over, you could just feel everything around you kind of change in the people around you feeling your your confidence. And like ultimately, um, I think one practice I started running, um, and my coach didn't even know who I was. He's like, "Oh, he like who that?" And then of course he finds out it's me over there running up and down the field. I had to do 110s, uh, just to keep in shape as I started running. And he seen me moving and floating. He's like, "Okay, this is time's coming." So, I think that was probably the big key opener for everyone. >> I imagine an injury of that magnitude, it it sort of forces that that mental barrier that you have to get past. >> Mhm. >> How how did you go about doing that? Cuz there was a long layoff there, and you get back on the field. I imagine things are a lot different. >> Oh, yeah. Um, >> [gasps] >> there was a lot of help. Um, I probably still have pictures of it. I used to have the bucket still, but I had so many letters coming in. I mean, till this day, I'm about to sign three cards here today and send back to a guy that, uh, just sent me some stuff that is going through some stuff with his knee. So, I think having so many people inside this whole entire world sending me over letters from literally every state you can name possible and just giving me motivation. You know, at the same time I had my little boy at the time who was able to come up and spend spend some time with me. Mom let him come spend a summer with me as well. So having all those things tied in and understanding like hey, like someone's watching me at the end of the day not just I have him that also me watching every single day and he's going to mold his life after me but also have a lot of people out here in this world that are believing in me and and believing that I can get back out here and play. And once all those things kind of tied in together along with the the people I have around me. I don't remember the Abners who were very very very close with me and then of course me and his mom today miss Miss Abner she's still a part of my life and does an amazing job of staying staying in touch with us. Comes to the kids games all the above stuff. She was there for me in my whole entire career as well along with my family just believing in me and just having a lot of support from a lot of different folks. It just it made life a lot easier from every aspect. Doctors, girl at the time my kid being able to come spend summers with like it was it it made life easy and then my teammates man they they ain't never stop believing. I think at one point they were mad at me cuz I was I looked like I was ready to play and they could see me doing drills on the sidelines like hey, he's going to be ready week one. And I even myself I'm like hey, I will I am ready. Like I probably could play and then my my course my staff is like you're not playing this year. I was like okay. >> I'll chill out. >> Well, I think that's very important to kind of go back and and make sure that I made mention of that because that that's another chapter of your story and it adds to the adversity that you've dealt with in your career and the perseverance. But that didn't define you because you ended up going to the Jacksonville Jaguars a couple days after the Eagles waived you. You go to their practice squad and then you eventually get signed off of that practice squad by the Minnesota Vikings. What what was that like that whole process for you? >> Uh that was crazy, man. I I think I was just talking to somebody about that last week as they're you know going through different things with their career and just how it was spur of the moment things can change. Um I literally have my my kid and my girl there at that time. We getting ready for Christmas. Me and her just went bought all Christmas gifts. My folks are coming up um probably like a couple days later. Um and then all of a sudden like hey, I get a phone call it's like hey, you're you got to pack up. I was like what do you mean? Like you you're getting signed to the Vikings. Like all right, I mean it's one game. Like are you >> telling me I got to go right now? So like that all happened. Uh they end up still of course having Christmas at Chris- Christmas by themselves without me and then my family and they all drove back home. So you go from sitting on the couch getting ready to plan a Christmas day with your kid and your and your girl and then all of a sudden it's like hey, you got to pack a bag so you can go to Minnesota and it's cold. >> That was a big change. >> Hey Philly fans, game day is stressful enough. Parking, traffic, long lines. We've all been there. But when it comes to your cannabis, Camden Apothecary makes it easy. This is the dispensary for sports fans. Just minutes outside of Philly with plenty of free parking, you'll be in and out fast. No hassle, no waiting. And they don't just care about convenience. Camden Apothecary is all about the guest experience. Their staff makes sure you feel taken care of every time you walk in. Plus, they carry only the best quality cannabis at the fairest prices. So whether you're stocking up for the tailgate, the watch party, or celebrating a big win, you know you're getting the good stuff without overpaying. They even show love to the community with specials for fans, students, service members, and healthcare pros. Camden Apothecary, top quality cannabis, great prices, and an experience made for Philly fans 21 and up. >> And then your career ends with you go to the CFL, you play for the Toronto team, you play for Ottawa as well. At what point did you sort of you know, tell yourself I'm done. I'm done with football and I'm going to move on to the next phase. >> It was easy. It definitely was easy. Definitely miss my miss my family for sure. Very very big on my kids and also they they can't be with me like I want them to be that's always a bother for me. text: There's a lot of people over here. >> What's it kind of feel to be back out there? >> Feel pretty good. Um We got some good weather today. title: Robert & Dr. Dana Kraft Address the Media at Patriots Training Camp | Press Conference
text: How we doing? >> We're doing great cuz when we have Patriots Day, we know it's the start of the season. I I have a I'm so excited about this year, so very proud of my bride what she's organized here. >> [cheering] >> You want to tell her? >> Sure. >> Yeah, Danny, year number two of this event. How How How much fun is this year? As you go. >> It's great. We It's you know, we're very excited when you see 50 dogs that could find homes. It's sort of the start of a new beginning for a lot of families. And we're just so thankful for everyone who's here whether they're here to adopt or foster or volunteer or just to learn about our partner organizations. We're so thrilled that everyone could be here. And we're hoping to give these dogs all a second chance and families a chance to adopt a dog that provides unconditional love and joy for their house. >> And to see the Patriots players give away the dogs to the families. >> It's so to see these big guys with the little dogs is so much fun. Yeah. >> When you thought When you thought of this last year and you probably had some expectations, has it exceeded the expectations? >> It's totally exceeded it and it's driven by the fans being so enthusiastic about it and people really kind of from all walks of life coming together to support it. So we're really grateful for that. >> Robert, the fans they're jammed here and near today. This excitement after what happened last year. How excited are you to get this thing going? >> Well, number 1, Danny and I know we've been waiting all year. I think we had a great off season. Well, excuse [clears throat] me, we have to execute on the field. But I know the excitement in the locker room, so we'll see what happens when we go out to Seattle. >> And to see the fans? >> It's tremendous. >> Robert, with bringing in AJ Brown, I'm how excited are you to kind of down the film and [cheering] get a receiver of his caliber in the room? >> Yeah, we worked hard at that and we're >> [applause and cheering] >> we're excited about the potential, but we have that whole wide receiver room is pretty full. So, but we would we I know Drake is excited. >> Robert, along those lines, I know you've been working hard with Christian Gonzalez. Any thoughts on that as as you get him? >> We love Christian Gonzalez. We love him as a player, as a person. You know, that's why we made an offer to him that makes him the highest paid player ever to play that position in the NFL. And coincidentally, it's the highest contract in the Patriots franchise history. So, uh we're we're glad we drafted him and we just developed him and we hope he'll be with us for a long time. >> Are you optimistic >> Last question, guys. Last question. >> Are you optimistic to get a deal done? >> Well, we're here to talk about the Patriots. I'm glad that 50 dogs are going to be uh who were homeless are going to have a nice home after this and we're making this awareness. You know, I didn't realize till we got our little Heisman 5 years ago the impact that dogs can have and the joy they bring, especially in a world where there's so much internet and people isolate. Dogs really create that family togetherness and so we need more of that in America today. So, I'm very proud of it. Being up there setting this up. >> Well, and to all the players and to the coach for participating and a special shout-out to Bryce and Bella Beringer who are offsetting some of the adoption costs at all the shelters today. So, people have really gone above and beyond. >> on their own, so it's really nice. Well, we thank you all for being here and let's go.

title: Drake Maye: "I Try to Keep My Body In It's Healthiest Form." | Patriots Press Conference
text: All right. We're back. What's going on? How's everybody doing? >> How would you assess day one? >> It was great to be back out here. That's the first thing. Um shout out to fans. CD, we got two great corners. Um we got you know, Marcus inside. We got a great secondary, so our receivers and tight ends get some great work. >> How hard is it to turn the page from last year? >> Um I don't think it's I mean, obviously it stings, but I don't think it's very hard cuz you're still hungry. It gets to gives us a great mindset for camp of, you know, getting things and getting going early and you know, firing all cylinders. So, we got some uh some tough work, but you know, looking forward to it. >> How was your second year in this offense now? How does it that affected your comfortability and ability to see things this year that maybe you didn't see things last year? >> I think it's understanding the little things. I think, you know, going through the installs and understanding like the little details that coach talks about and you know, knowing them before he kind of tries to reiterate it to us and one of the biggest things is just seeing plays that we ran against certain defenses, you know, over and over again. I think you understand you know, better answers, better place to go with the football and just better timing. So, that's the nature of it. >> What do you know about DeAndre >> operating faster in the offense? We've heard that a lot from the coaches wanting you guys to go faster. What goes into that for you? >> Whoa, I think it's in the right play first. I think, you know, getting set under center, you know, getting ready to get in the gun. I think just moving faster. We got a good play that we like against the defense. You know, just train our guys to be hey, once we get down on the football and get set, we're going. I think that's the best thing of you know, we we kind of did a lot of great things in offense. We had a bunch of, you know, statistics that we, you know, did a bunch of things high in the league. I think just creating more plays. I think we could even create you know, more plays, snap the ball earlier in the play clock and get some things going. >> What do you know about DeAndre Hopkins and what's it like kind of seeing him out here helping the wide receivers out? >> Yeah, I mean, I'm from the south and DeAndre Hopkins was went to Clemson, which is 2 hours down the road. So, you know, anybody that of that player, that's kind of my era of watching college football and seeing him in the NFL and having him in my fantasy team. So, it's cool to shake his hand and his hands are twice as big as mine and just having him be out here and share some information and just be a kid, I mean, a a young adult and a great player in this league, a legendary player to play at a high level and share some information is awesome. >> What did you think about the DeAndre Hopkins catch there on the sideline? >> Yeah, I mean, it's nothing new. I mean, you got to see it every, I mean, all year last year and the year before and he just keeps doing things right and I'm proud of him for, you know, getting in there, jumping in there and he understands if he's got a something down the sideline and a a ball down the field that he's got a chance that's coming his way. So, great catch and I think that was the better start off camp with a little bit of a a deep one. So, we were one for one to start. >> Great catch. What were some of your biggest takeaways from having a full season handling protections and how do you want to continue to grow this season? >> Yeah, I think being on the same page. I think, you know, playing the game a a bit with some of these, you know, safeties, with some these linebackers, you know, Splaine likes to move around and try to hop on different sides of the center to try to mess with us. So, I think that's good work. Good work for us to be on the same page and the the biggest thing is just being loud. I think being loud, being communicative, and uh the biggest thing for these guys is, you know, they hear me and you know, understand the mic point and let's go. So, these guys have been great and uh just understanding like pressure patterns is uh another thing of, you know, where they like to bring guys and what the front looks like that. So, different things like that. >> pretty open about, you know, wanting a new contract. What's it mean to you as one of his teammates, the fact that he's out here and he's participating and he's giving you guys a look even though he doesn't have have that resolved? >> I think that shows his main focus, and that's football. You know, he's you know, the best corner in the league, in my opinion. He's um you know, he's not the big rah-rah guy. He does it his own way, but he does it at the highest level. So, I'm glad to be his teammate. Um around the same age and, you know, he was you know, the you know, I I tell him uh you know, Will, that he's my rook cuz he's I was first round pick and Will was the next, but you know, Gonzo's someone I look up to. You know, even at the same age, you know, I look up to how he does things, how he you know, handles himself and uh just, you know, his swagger he has in his own way. I think it's, you know, great to see him out here um playing around and I think you saw it in the locker room before, you know, everyone was wondering, "What's Gonzo going to do?" you know, and he's coming out here and first play he's guarding A.J. in man coverage. So, that's uh the Patriots. >> You mentioned being loud and and communicative. Has it been easier for you to do that now? Like we remember last year Mike was constantly pushing you to go celebrate with your teammates, go talk to this guy, go do that. Is Is it become more natural for you? >> It has to. I think for me, I think the biggest thing I kept on saying last year was like, I feel like I need to do something in this league, you know, before I start. And they kept on pushing me, said, "You got to expect that to happen." So, um I definitely got some more comfort in that area of pushing the guys and um I think I need to do it more and and celebrate and be louder and show my personality more. I think the guys will see that naturally. So, uh I think that's what camp's for and you build through it and uh you kind of, you know, get to new levels and that's the best thing about spending every day all day with each other. >> What's it like working with a new center? >> Yeah. >> the things that are important to you and how's that going with Jared? >> Yeah, I mean the last the snap in practice is my fault. I held the cadence a little long, but Jared is um he's natural there. I think you know Garrett you get to know a center for a year and you get to know his little things and how he likes things and if he's going left and I'm going right how it works and little under center things and how he understands Mike points, but you know Jared's he's smart. He's real smart. You know I wanted him to play with me in college. He went to the SEC. I don't blame him, but um I think he's done a great job of understanding you know what comes with playing center and uh you got to be loud. You got to be you know me and you it's our show. So I think he's done a great job and just getting used to you know little things under center and um you know how he likes to do silent cadence and stuff like that, but he's got a great feel for the cadence and and and saw Garrett do it last year which is a great you know look for him. >> What did you do in the off season and did you make any changes to your body like adding weight or anything and uh uh during during the time off did you and the guys get together to throw or anything like that? >> Yeah, I think I'm a you know my program's going to stay 6'4 225 and that's the that's that's how we keep it. You know you guys won't know if what I gain if I lose, so I think that's the the best part about you know having some inside information, so um you know I'm just trying to keep my body in the the healthiest form, so if you guys think it's I look like 230 I may be 220 it doesn't matter, so I know and our strength coach knows, so that's what's important. And then uh yeah we had the guys come to North Carolina again like last year. You know got on the lake and got some 3 days of work. It was good to have those guys there and I think it's huge in the off season kind of right before to get the get guys going and um you know have them I feel like we had a good group and some good sessions and it was fun work, so thank you guys. >> Thanks Cam.

title: Mike Vrabel: "It's Our Job to Recreate the Things We Did Really Well Last Year." | Press Conference
text: Hi, Mike. There's a history of teams of who loses the Super Bowl struggling the following year. Um Did you do any research, homework, calling any coaches who had to deal with that to to kind of navigate >> it kind of speaks for itself. I think that uh you know, things the expectations always get higher and we have tried to lay out the expectations when we got here. Um and what we wanted to do and I think just the the nature of the NFL and um based on success, uh the rules, the draft, the you know schedule, you know, all those things that that come into it and then it's our job is to recreate um the things that we did [clears throat] really well last year, the the culture, the ability to to win different ways and find ways to win and understand how to win and understand how to prepare and we're going to have a a more difficult journey. It That's just how it goes each and every year. That's what we're expecting. So we we want it that way and we'll prepare accordingly. >> Mike, following that up a little bit, um when you were a player, your teams were very good at putting whatever you did the year before away and creating a completely new environment and knowing that you haven't won anything. Do you get a sense that this team is like that that they can forget about last year and just and go but do you share that >> I mean I think that I we have that ability. We try to do that each and every week. That's not something that we focus on year to year. We try to focus on that each week, each day. We come in, we make corrections, we watch the tape, we try to look at the good, the bad, and the stuff that gets us beat. Uh we talk about eliminating stuff that gets us beat, being able to fix the the things that we didn't do very well, and then try to enhance the things that we did well. And so that's not just a yearly approach, that's a daily approach, that's a weekly approach. In this league, you have to take that attitude. It's difficult in this league. Um so, whatever you do on Thursday or Saturday or Sunday, whenever you play Monday, you have to look at those things, you have to address them and move on quickly. So, I felt like we did that last year, even with success. And so, we'll have to you know, we'll start that today. >> Like just watching the fans come running in as they usually do on that first day, it's going to be jammed out there today. What does that mean to you and the team as you go forward? >> Well, the support has been fantastic and and I said this when when we all got here is that we want to you know, we have a very knowledgeable fan base. They know what good football looks like, they know what bad football looks like and when we play good football, they they support that, they enjoy that, they they embrace that and um we were able to to do that and and give that to them and in turn, they gave us their support, their energy, everything that we needed, especially in those playoff games down the stretch. >> Over the last year, so what's impressed you the most about Elijah Ponder when it comes with growth and development? >> Well, just came in and didn't say a whole lot. He's not a you know, he's not not a boisterous person by nature. I think he just continued to get better. His confidence probably improved, it looked like that. He's a more confident player as the as the season wore on. He earned a role on special teams and then you know, continued to earn a role on defense and I think he just kept getting better. >> When you think about a center and a quarterback working together, what are some of the things you look for >> [clears throat] >> with that chemistry? >> Well, I think just the the unspoken communication, to be able to see it quickly, to see it the same, see it very similar, whether that's pressure or uh defensive front, to be able to set the defense or get us in the right play, communication, um being able to Yeah, I think that the the center is the conduit to the rest of the offensive line. And so, you know, when the quarterback needs to get something to the line, uh the center's the easiest way to get it. And then his communication to everybody else has to be great. So, you know, we're looking forward to to seeing Jared in that transition and working with Drake. >> Mike, any update on Gabe Jackson sitting out? >> yet. Not with Gabe, not yet. Uh not from uh when we met yesterday. >> Is he Is he local to you? >> I I do not think that Gabe is is local. I don't think that that he's in New England. >> Mike, how excited are you about the new guys getting started? AJ Epenesa, all of them. Reggie Gilliam, all of them. >> Well, I mean, we've seen their you know, I guess acclimation into our on our team and our program. So, not just excited about them. I'm excited about everybody to be out there uh in a training camp mode and just have it ramp up from where we were in mini camp. But certainly those additions that we made, we felt all felt really good about them and uh excited that they're here. And uh I know that uh they're going to do everything that they can to to help us win and help us prepare to win. >> What situations will you guys be emphasizing today and how will this kind of non-padded section be different from what you guys were doing in the spring? >> Well, we'll have a It'll be a few more runs. There'll be a few more runs. You know, we have to to get into that, we have to be able to practice without pads on. you know, admittedly, there'll be more uh zone runs, you know, to take away some of those, you know, double teams that you have in some of the the gap scheme runs. We'll we'll save pads for that. I don't think it necessarily does us any good to to install those runs uh and then work on them and maybe not have the right technique because we you don't have pads on and we're trying to take care of a guy. So, why waste, you know, a rep when you can't you know, use the right technique just because you don't have pads on. So, there'll be some of that uh with the outside zone. We'll work on first and second down. Uh we'll have uh tempo a lot. We try to talk to the players about uh practice in the same way that we want to play. You'll see everybody off on the sideline and subs will be running in, but if we hit a play, um you know, I I reserve the right to to go on the ball, you know, as long as, you know, we're not subbing. You know, those are things that happen, you know, if we offense a player comes onto the field and we want to go fast, they're going to stand over it. So, I explained that to the players, explained that to the coaches, but we want to, you know, we want to practice right now starting day the same way that we're going to look to play and uh we'll continue to add as we move on and get into third down and get into the red zone, uh two-minute, short yardage, and then at some point in time there'll be a there'll be a call it, you know, period once we get the first week installed and we'll go out and not have a script and I'll just say whatever situation we have. >> You feel like he can handle some of the different things that you guys are throwing at him in the spring? And how do you continue to push him that way? >> Yeah, I think that the the defense has done some added some things and so that that'll come naturally, I think, just from the looks that that he's getting there. you know, just continue to try to operate and and get us and be more urgent and and get everybody just functioning just a a little bit quicker. And we don't want to go fast. We we want to just whether we huddle or we go on the ball, whatever that looks like, you know, to be able to try to dictate the defense a little bit and and not just um you know, we we just the urgency in which we operate, I think, is something that we've all talked about. Uh the communication, always taking care of the ball. We we talked about the the games that we lost last year, you know, whether that was the the quarterback rating, you know, Josh Allen had a better rating than than Drake. And that's just not on the quarterback. That's defensively our ability to affect uh their quarterback, our our ability to help our quarterback. Uh whether it was the the Pittsburgh game where the turnover margin uh wasn't where we needed it to be. That's the reason that we lost that game. Um you know, and obviously in the Super Bowl, the turnover margin uh and their ability to run the football and our ability not to be able to run the football. And then we get into all the different, you know, critical situations, 2-minute, 5-minute. you know, Buffalo being able to set the table a little better on special teams. You know, they their kickoff return was much better than ours was. So, those are all things that we look at and um you know, that we're going to focus on and that's how we want to practice and that's how we want to play. >> Mike, last year I'm >> I'm just curious um >> with him starting on PUP, >> Yeah. >> threaten his availability to start the season or do >> Uh so, if I could I couldn't not going to predict that. I'm not going to pretend to predict that. I think when he's ready, you know, we're going to talk about injuries that they're going to happen. They're 100% in football. At some point in time, everybody's going to get hurt. Uh the expectation is that they all work extremely hard uh to get back, that they're where they're supposed to be when they're supposed to be there. Uh they focus on what they can do as opposed to what they can't do. Uh very comfortable and confident in our return to play. Um so, where Harold's at at the start of the season, you know, I I wouldn't be able to tell you right now. I know that he won't be practicing, but he'll be working uh and hopefully uh we'll we'll get him back. >> There were a lot of clips last year during the spring and summer that the team released where you were pushing Drake to be more of a leader. You know, interact with your guys. Go celebrate. Do those things. How have you seen him grow in that regard? And do you feel like you're going to have to still maybe push him in that direction? >> I'm probably going to try to coach everything that I possibly can. Uh that's what they pay me to do is to to just to coach the team uh where I see. um And if I just if we don't celebrate, I'll be telling them to run down there and celebrate even though, you know, we scored a few touchdowns last year. Um don't take those for granted. Um and again, it's really hard. I can try to put myself in his position or any player's position that I'm coaching. You know, there's a lot on his plate and he's focusing about you know, doing the right thing and being as perfect as he can be and you puts a lot on himself and uh then it's like, "Oh yeah, I just threw a touchdown." But it's like, "No, like we're going to go celebrate." And there's, you know, I think you can really define yourself as a leader uh by how you handle yourself and and your teammates when things aren't great. And it's easy to go celebrate, but is it uh it's it's harder to to stand up there and say, "You know what? I I screwed up. I might have made a mistake in the huddle which caused another player uh not to do his job." And even I I was able to adjust for my mistake in the huddle or miscommunication, but this other player had something else in his mind and that led him to go the wrong way. And you know, when you stand up and say, "Hey, you know what? That's on me." You know, it takes a lot of pressure off everybody else. So, I'm excited about where Drake's going to be and and his uh you know, just his growth and and Josh and Ashton and you know, just the offensive coaches. We're We're everybody's in just a better position and you know, just because we're more comfortable, that doesn't mean that we can't, you know, we still have to go and we have to push each other and you know, the the challenge is to compete but take care of each other when we're out there on the practice field. >> Speaking of staff, what does having almost complete continuity from year one to year two maybe enable you guys to do this summer that you couldn't do >> Probably just operate a little quicker, you know, just going through the tape probably a little quicker for the coaches and then, you know, being able to to get on, you know, make the corrections, look at the positives and then you know, move on to the installation in the afternoon. We have a pretty similar schedule most every day where we'll practice and then give the players a little break for them to get treatment or lift and recover or whatever they need. And then we'll meet and then we'll have walk-through and then get them out of here. So, that's kind of how we've structured things and I think everybody's a little bit more comfortable with that stuff. >> Mike, A.J. Brown is still relatively new to the team. Just how's he looking? How's he fitting in so far? >> All right, we did the run test, so he passed that. which was expected. I I couldn't, you know, again, I I enjoy having A.J. here. I I I I really love him personally and and he's going to he's going to help our football team and so, but we're we're going to go out there today and we're going to build and he's going to be involved in some plays and then we'll go from there, but you know, he's had a great attitude and a willingness to to learn a completely new system in a in a short amount of time. >> Mike. >> Mike, uh you have talked about culture and relationships since you got here a lot of times, right? With so many new players uh coming this year, what part of like the culture you want to you you do you expect to see the the returning players to carry over from last year and what do you expect us new players to contribute this year? >> Well, again, we've always talked about having a you know, a singular mindset on on winning and and what our identity needs to be. And then the personalities, uh there's going to be different personalities. And our job and my job is to find out where where everybody's sweet spot is and where their optimal performance is and their attitude. Some guys are going to be sky high, some guys are going to be a little bit more even keel. and that's fine. But, uh that's what makes it a great, you know, experience and makes it a team is that everybody's different, they come from different places. Uh but, we're going to have one goal and and try to build one identity. >> Coach, can you learn Last question? >> Couple of DC you on the roster now. You drafted Q, you signed Jeremiah. What are you hoping to see from them and what's their weight coming out of college? >> Well, I mean again I got a lot of respect for for Bellio at Boston College and you know, Jeremiah is somebody we had a local day. We took a lot of you know, we looked at him a lot and the numbers were probably not in his favor at the time and then now I think they're a little bit more favorable and we're able to bring them in. I think he's uh continued to improve and looked like he'd been working out. I think he's gotten stronger since uh since March and uh certainly with Q was you know, somebody on the edge always looking for for young pass rushers that that can help you and you know, those guys will have to to learn special teams pretty quickly and given their body types and uh that that process has already started for Q and and Jeremiah will start that today. Thanks, guys.

I got to get with the speed. meaning we will go fiveminute blocks on Gabe Ais, Christian Gonzalez, Drake May and the offense as a whole, which I think is going to go a little bit faster and I'll get to that in a minute. To lead off though, it was probably a little bit of an overdue conversation and definitely the biggest breaking news here today. Gabe Bakus is going to be a real football player for the Patriots. Signed a four-year, $8.6 million contract that's broken by Jordan Schultz, confirmed by my guy Doug Ky, uh, who was not here, left as soon as they said, "Hey, I'm going to do a live podcast. You want Nope. See you." It was like the Roadrunner just out the door. Gabe Ais' contract, and I'll let you take it from here, has never been about the raw guaranteed money. Patriots didn't give that to Gabe Bakers. It is in that language, the guarantees and all the little details for the double lives. But as far as we know, Gabe Bakers could be here as soon as tomorrow. We don't know what shape he's in. And personally, I'm just happy to put this to rest, which has been a very strange contract negotiation and standoff or whatever you want to call it. Yeah, I'm fascinated when we get the details of the contract, you know, when we get to dig into the uh the fine print, if you will, uh because I do believe that this is injury related and the guarantees as tied to the injuries and whatever happened with this first. It was a procedure yesterday. Mike Vrabel finally called it a surgery that he had this off season. Was that team approved? Did the team know about that before they drafted him, etc. certainly felt like there was a disconnect there and that sort of led to this um I don't want to call it a hold out. It wasn't a hold out, but this this process not getting sped up and getting done and quite frankly him losing valuable time even if he couldn't have participated on the field this spring and at mandatory mini camp. He could have been here and he could have been in the playbook and he could have learned his teammates and learned the area and done that whole thing and now he's coming in and he's going to get a ton of stuff dumped in his plate and we're going to see if he can sink or swim and how quickly he can swim because as I've mentioned before and I'll say it again, they didn't trade three picks to move up to 55 for Gabe Bakis to be behind Braden Swinson and maybe even be behind everybody's darling right now and Elijah Ponder. They made this selection cuz they thought this dude could help them this year and beyond. So, how quickly can he get up to speed? >> Well, and that's the interesting part of this standoff. It's not just about I want more money. We don't want to give you that amount of money. And yet, there's still real leverage on both sides. like in the conversations that were had as you know Gabe Atkins is a guy who had a hamstring injury during the pre-draft process and then teams according to our guy Mike Reese at ESPN you know concerned about a shoulder in a laboral tier and then there was a serious foot injury and again the timeline of the surgery is very important the fact that Mike Greyel volunteered that to me makes it central to what has been going on and the thing is though even if let's say Gabe Ais was in the wrong which is broad and could mean a number of different things but it pertained to this surgery. What is a couple extra million dollars guaranteed to you? I did my job. I got drafted. You picked me. You have my rights for four years. But, um, nobody knows how healthy or what kind of shape he's in, but we'll we'll we'll find out soon. >> Yeah. Well, the Patriots pick them and he doesn't sign so his agent is greedy or he doesn't know what he's doing or etc. The player is getting bad advice. The the player is protecting and the agent is protecting the player's rights. Why should he sign everything away? Oh, you don't like the timing of the surgery or the nature of the injury or whatever? Why should I just put this language in the contract or let you put this language in the contract and just sign off on it? No, I'm not going to do that. Like that's and again, we'll see what ended up happening and and whether the the sort of the deadline of hey, training camp has started that the boys are taking off on the bus. Do you want to be on the bus or do you want to sit on the sideline and keep watching? Like if that spurred him to to do something about that, but like I can't stand that sort of narrative like oh the agent or the player is being greedy. It's like, no, you know who's greedy in this whole thing? The team. Because the team is the one that makes billions of dollars. They're and they're and they're trying to to haggle over whatever 50,000, 100,000, 500,000, a million, whatever it is, that's small change. Whereas to him, that's big money, >> right? And again, you know, the devil is in the details. So is in the reason why they might not just want to do the deal as it was expected. And not all of these second round picks, in fact, most of them are not fully guaranteed. So, this is not, I think, them nickel and dimming, but clearly there's a concern that's injury related and the timing of the surgery, the nature of the surgery was not to their liking. Anyway, they're going to move forward soon. We will ask questions if AIS, who I'm sure is going to be handed a dusted off Bellich media rules of you say nothing, you move forward, you be in the moment. And that is our five minutes on Gay Backas. Okay. Um, where do you want to go next? We have Chris Gonzalez, the offense, practice takeaways, verbal/popery. >> Well, I mean, let's go Gonzalez because I thought today was interesting in that I wasn't sure if he was going to be a full participant. title: George Kittle's comments raise questions about NFLPA leadership | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: Chris Simms interviewed George Kittle yesterday, the 49ers tight end. A lot of great topics that they addressed, and one of the obvious ones to address with Kittle because he's been at the forefront of this conversation in the summer of grass in the NFL because of the World Cup. All the examples of stadiums that ripped up temporarily their artificial turf put in grass to placate FIFA and then out with the grass, back with the turf. I want you to listen to about 25 seconds of what Kittle had to say when it comes to what it will take to turn this preference for grass into a bargained for win by the NFL Players Association to get grass in all stadiums. Here he is. >> You know what? In all honesty, it all depends on the star power of the NFL. >> Yeah. >> You know what? If our If our best players specifically the quarterbacks >> Right. >> make noise about it, they'll do it. Like if you have Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford if you have Lamar Jackson if you have the main guys speak up about it there there'll be an issue and like it'll help. >> You have Myles Garrett talk about it, that'll help. >> That's an important point because that mindset within the union is pervasive. And Kittle was providing it as a tangible example of what it would take to try to push grass over the top. I still don't think it would work. But the reason I point this out there has been this chronic frustration that never really manifested itself in a full-throated finger-pointing. I'm mixing metaphors, but my point is the union needs star players to be more involved. It can't just be Drew Brees, Peyton Manning, and Tom Brady putting their names on the lawsuit that was filed in 2011 against the NFL after the union basically shut down and they challenged the NFL's lingering rules as antitrust violations, which is what happens when the union goes away, anything the NFL does as to the workforce becomes the same kind of antitrust violation that NCAA rules are for the college players. You can't just put your name on a lawsuit. It helps. You need to have star players, predominantly quarterbacks, you need to have them taking a stand on behalf of the other players. The problem is when you consider how much money the quarterbacks make. And when you consider the basic reality that they're the closest thing to management that a football team has in the locker room. And it's easier to see the quarterbacks kind of align with management principles. They're typically the highest-paid guys in the locker room. And there's a level of trepidation. We don't want to step too far out of line here because we don't want to find ourselves in a position where all of a sudden they don't want to pass. Now, Colin Kaepernick is an extreme example of what happens when you step out of line as far as the NFL management is concerned, but look at Lamar Jackson. All that talk about fully guaranteed contract and he's available back in 2023 under the franchise tag. Two first-round picks would be the compensation if you sign him to an offer sheet the Ravens don't match and nobody talked to him at all. I think there is at some level an unspoken concern by the star players that they're going to put the money that goes with their stardom and in turn their stardom at risk if they stick their neck out. And I know because I've heard it enough times over the years that Kittle's comments are just a small slice of the broader frustration that exists among union members and people who are in management positions with the union about the failure of the stars to step up and speak and act and lead the way on these issues. I still don't think it will make a difference when it comes to grass versus turf. And I don't believe that viewing that as a CBA issue is going to prevail because once you do a dollar figure gets attached to it and the league will pump it up and they'll say, "Hey, you want to share this? This extra cost, lost revenues, expenses of having high quality grass. We'll share it with you if you want to do that. Otherwise we're going to stay with what we have." you should listen to the whole interview. I'm going to write something about this. Kittle had some very good points as it relates to consistency of turf surfaces. That there should be one uniform accepted artificial turf. So, when you play on it, it's the same from stadium to stadium. That's still not ideal but it's better than what they currently have. And he he confirmed a lot of the things that we talk about all the time. It's not about injury rates, it's about how your body feels the next day. And he specifically pointed to playing on artificial turf on a Sunday and then turning around and playing on artificial turf on a Thursday. Because it takes longer for your body to recover from the wear and tear and the pounding of playing on artificial surfaces. And he even said by Wednesday you practice again on a normal week if you're playing the following Sunday and you still don't feel like you got the most out of practice cuz you're still recovering from playing on artificial turf on Sunday. In a truncated week of preparation for a Thursday game if you're playing on turf again and you haven't completely and fully recovered from that and then you go out and play on turf again, those are the issues. title: Jacoby Brissett doesn't hold-in, practices with Arizona Cardinals | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: The most recent CBA from 2020 made it virtually impossible for players to hold out, so we have seen more and more players hold in. Many believe that Jacoby Brissett, the starting quarterback of the Arizona Cardinals, would show up for training camp, but not practice. Mike LaFleur, the new head coach of the Arizona Cardinals, said yesterday that he expected Brissett to participate in Thursday's session. Now, they have a break-in period and they're really not jumping into 11-on-11 right away. It may be when it's time to do 11-on-11 drills, Brissett says, "I'm not doing that until we get this contract worked out." But, he didn't show up and refused to do anything. And there has been some reporting that the two sides acknowledge there needs to be a fix. That's the first hurdle to overcome. When you have a player who says, very reasonably, "You're paying me to be a backup and you want me to be the starter. I signed to be the backup. If you want me to be the starter, you need to pay me like a starter." And if the team says, "No, we're not going to do that." kind of ends the discussion. The Cardinals acknowledge they need to do something. Now the challenge becomes figuring out what something looks like. There's a wide range between where Brissett is at 6.5 million per year and where Patrick Mahomes is at 64 million per year. And for veteran starters, the bottom end is 20. I mean, I think that they could get this done for less than any other veteran starter is making cuz it would still be a significant increase. Just triple his pay. Make it 19 and a half. He's still making less than any other veteran starter, but he's getting paid like a starter. And we'll see how hard Brissett pushes it as this process goes forward and it's time to go to the full-blown 11-on-11s. We get deeper into camp. He's missing opportunities with new coach, new system, new everything, really, as it relates to the coaching staff in Arizona, as they prepare for a 17-game season that probably results in no playoff berth, so they may as well accept it. Get themselves in position to have Arch Manning tell them no thank you next April. I I think I'm kidding, but who knows. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube.
