I'll say Rob Jones done an excellent job since being here as well. Those two guys have really set themselves apart from the other guys. And then Don Poon's had an awesome off seasonason as well. So first day of camp short still it's like another OTAA practice. We'll see how it goes. But Conor still doing well. And as far as like one ones, >> yeah, you look at it from >> Oh, all of it. I'll look at obviously with this uh with this I've always I've always been asked to to look at both sides and and that will continue to look at the defensive line. What's my opinion on CJ Day or this guy, you know, that type of thing. So I'm always involved in the process. But you tell the study [snorts] >> really good. Yeah, Enrique has been a real plus. Everybody in the building's pleased with him. You know, people come up out of nowhere um from all over the building say, "Gosh, that Enrique is doing a really nice job. He's really professional, really working on He's a learning curve like all the young guys do and uh he's got a he's got a long way to go, but he's done all the right things to this point." >> Chris, have you ever had five in a room? that makes like Jake and Trent and try to, you know, get those guys to try to take more of a lead offense. >> They do a great job. I mean, but it is it is fun. It does take you back to ground zero a little bit. We have to go back for everybody. It's not it's not bad for Colton or or or Jake or those guys, Trent, to go back and start at at ground zero again. It also I approached the offseason differently this year. I I kind of let those guys take some time away and I met with them individually, the older guys, because I had to do more of the the base stuff. But those guys do a great job of letting those those players know exactly what I'm looking for. So if there's any question or hesitation to have three, four guys in the room that could tell the five new guys what we're looking for, it really helps. >> I love it. If if I had if if they said, "Dude, I we I like to I say it's over. You don't get that play back." In other words, and I and as coaches, you hate that because you're like, you hate losing the rep, but I want, you know, the importance of the rep is that we stay on sides. And the way to learn to stay on sides, you know, we don't get the rep back. So, you don't get a rep to show us what you do on film. We've traditionally done, which is I've been everywhere else, and that was a long time ago when that was like that. Um, now we usually bury the rep. Sometimes we get back up and run again. The problem is sometimes you showed the play. So, there's the whole dilemma of you show the play, you do it again, and Fred knows what the play is. If you flip the play over and then run the risk of it's not run right or d and then you say what I what we did we decided today we just take it to the end of the little block of four or five plays that the ones are going and then repeat it at the end. That's all speeches. Obviously Kyle has >> believe it or not. I don't like big speeches. I like to I coach and talk a lot about football and I like talking about technique and fundamentals and players and and and and what's important about playing the game of football. speeches as far as you know that it's it's hard for me. I that John made fun of it yesterday. I'm not sure he didn't think I was a breakdown guy and uh I challenge grumpy but I think maybe I am a little grumpy but I do know that he said it was uh I don't like and I don't love the big breakdowns after practice. The problem is after practice I may have an impression of practice based on one or two plays and I could be completely wrong if I talk to the team afterwards about practice. That's my opinion. So I'm always I'm very careful to say this was a good or bad practice. Let's go watch the tape and we'll decide if it was a good or bad practice. I can have an impression, but I I'm I struggle with that's why I struggle with the big speeches. >> I got a little fired up today because I was challenged yesterday. So, I got a little bit fired up and told them how fired up I was to be a part of this team and and how much I love the way they practice and the energy they bring every day and and got a lot to work on. We'll keep working. >> Chris, this time is it going to be like you're calling Kyle at night, he's telling you things that he wants to see or is this truly kind of removed outside of just around the facility. >> Well, he's here. He's he's he's a part of things. When he's here, he's listening to everything. When he's not, he knows what's going on. This is, like I said, I don't want to say autopilot, but but when you get into the schedule, you barely have time. You know, you go to lunch, you go to meetings, and the meetings are scheduled and planned, and you're barely getting everything done. You go to practice, now you have this tape to watch, individual tape. So, as far as a point of emphasis or something like that, over the course of time, there may be some things that start to come up, and he may notice or some other coach may notice, hey, let's let's talk about that. But we don't it it really doesn't need to be like directed at this point at least right now. >> Chris, going back to left guard, is it an open competition or if Connor just latches on to it and gives you no reason to take him off the field? Is it going to be his job? >> We're going to play the best five players as we can and then left guard there is we we brought guys in to compete at the left guard spot. Now he's the incumbent and that wasn't going to there nobody else has done anything to beat him out to this point. So right now what you're saying is true because he's held it, but we've yet to get to live bullets and see what's happening out there. So >> it's only been one practice, but how do you think some of the veteran players have responded to the situation with Kyle? And do you bring, you know, that that leadership group together and talk to them specifically about maybe you have more focal responsibility because we don't have our head coach right now or how how's that dynamic working? >> You know, I think, you know, it was addressed yesterday. John addressed the team to begin with and I think we have a great core group of leaders and like I said we have a bunch of guys that love playing football and they just want to go out and practice and get better and play and be coached and and Kyle's leadership is obviously going to be missed. We nobody knows the length of time and so how much of that needs to occur at this point. Right now we're just going to work and and filling in for Kyle as we can as a group and the players are doing the same thing. There's obviously they feel for Kyle and they want him back out there. We all do. But they're they're going to come to work. They're pros and they work their tails off every day and they're a great group to be around. There's none of that. Well, what if the no excuse making? Well, Kyle's not here type of thing. These guys are are awesome that way. >> When and how did you learn you were going to be taking on this role? And was that at a different time than when you learned of the accident initially? >> Uh, when did the statement come out? That's when I saw my name. Okay. That's when I saw my name. I knew that I knew that we'd all have to pick up the slack. So, I knew that once Kyle wasn't, you know, we didn't know. You just don't know. Every day the thing could flip and he can do more and more. So, we just don't know how it's going to be. So when I saw my name on it, I said, "Oh, okay. It's going to be that." And then, but it was going to be the group effort. I always, we always knew that. We were talking for days before, "What if he couldn't do it?" Clay, Kyle, Raheem, Boyer, and I, we were all talking about how we could fill in the blanks if needed. And then, uh, then obviously the yesterday they said, "You're going to be doing the pressers?" I said, "Well, don't think I'm doing the pressers." And then, well, here I am. So, >> what was your initial reaction when when you heard the news? >> Oh, shoot. I'm fired up. I'm I'm excited. Not not from the standpoint of I'm fired up from the standpoint of um you know like it's oh Kyle's down this is my big ch No, it's just like I love the opportunity to help. I my thing what I learned a long long time ago I believe leadership is is you serve in leadership you you help people by serving and servant leadership is any way I can help. Anyway I can help Kyle. Anyway I can help the 49ers anyway I can help John Lynch. Anyway I can help my players anyway I can help you guys. Anything I can do to help that's that's where I get a charge out of life that I learned that through a lot of difficult times in my life that that being a being that way. So, this is another opportunity to stand up here. And you guys were here before. I I don't I like getting up here and talking about football. I'm not It's not about me. I like talking ball. I like I like sharing football. I think it's a it's a great game. It's a great sport and a lot of people don't understand it. And and if you have a chance to learn a little more, I like to talk about it because I love the game. >> Just I noticed a lot more people, a lot of staff and maybe even some coaches shaking your hand at the beginning of practice. Uh >> was one practice enough for you to start feeling comfortable in your new role? are going to take time as this evolves. >> Uh, it's going to evolve. I'm the line coach out there. Just uh I have to break the team down. Have a couple other responsibilities right now. We're doing as a group and who knows tomorrow we'll be shaking Raheem's hand. I mean, it's not it's everybody's kind of it's it's kind of tongue and cheek. Hey, head coach, how you doing? You know, that type. No, I'm the line coach and I'm helping us helping along as we go. >> What have been your early impressions of Mike Evans? >> Man, I love having him out there. The guy's a uh you know, obviously he's a real pro. um his skill set and the things he does well are going to add so much to our football team. We saw play today in the red zone and OTAAS. There's just so many places where Mike's gonna help our football team and I'm very excited to have him. >> What conversations have you had with with Kyle and how has he talked to you about approaching this position? >> Which one? I'm sorry. Which position? >> Kyle >> with my position >> conversation with him. >> Yeah, I did. I had the one conversation and I I think what I what he said to me was, "Hey, you do whatever you want. I have a lot of confidence in you. You know how we do things. you do whatever you want to do and if you don't want to do it, delegate it to somebody else. Man, he said, you just you do what you feels right and uh and and lead that way and and he said, I trust that you'll anything you want to do and anything you want to delegate, delegate. >> Have you delegated anything? >> Uh yeah, I delegated this morning's team meeting out to offense and defense and uh we decided to do it that way today instead of doing a team meeting and we'll see as we go each week, each day what it is. And um that's that's about it right now. Chris, how important is continuity on a coaching staff in a situation like this? You guys have been around each other for a lot of years. >> Phenomenal. It's awesome. That's the great thing. And even with Raheem being new, Raheem, he knows how we do things. We had to spring together and these guys have known each other for a long time, man. Continuity is everything with the players, with the coaches. Like I say, I don't want to say autopilot because it's never autopilot. We got to work our tail off to get good and compete every single day. We obviously, you know, it's a it's a tough tough tough division and a tough league, but but these guys, having these guys that have been here, knowing how we do things, man, it's day after day after day. We know the routine. We know the tempo. We know what it should look like. And uh boy, there's no there shouldn't be any loss of any we lose one step in this process. >> If Kyle's absence lingers into the season, do you feel like this staff would be uniquely equipped to survive um the absence of a head coach? >> I think that's we're going too far. I know it's hard to say at this point, but I mean I think one thing I will say from a I will say that of all the guys that have worked with Kyle uh in that offensive coordinator passing coordinator role, Klay Kubak has been the most uh prepared, most most uh really really good. Klay does a hell of a job with with what he does and that's that's been that's where this is really kind of seamless when you get to the the scripting and the game and calling it into practice and stuff like that. Those two have been lock step. They've really co-done things a lot. It's been a really cool thing to see. >> Chris, you and Kyle go way back. How scary, just on a personal level, was it to get that initial phone call? >> Yeah, I don't I'm not gonna, you know, uh, cry up here in this first one. Okay. So, tough question. I'm not afraid to cry. But the the thing is the guy's uh he's family to me, this whole organization. Um, you know, Kyle, I've known Kyle for a long time. Um, he's one of my best friends in the world by far. There's not many people that I call friend and uh and for a lot of reasons. and Kyle's one of them. And uh he and his wife Mandy are like family to me. This organization did some things for me and pulled me in at a time in my life when nobody would really want to be with me. And Kyle along with John and and the whole York family have stood by me. And that loyalty is never going to be forgotten. And he's he's a close close friend. And it scares the crap out of you when something like this happens to to somebody so close. And I can only imagine I was thinking the day after this was Mandy. I'm thinking his wife. I I felt like you know gosh what's she going through to to pull up and you know whatever the situation I'm not sure of all the details but I just think the whole thing is just very very tough and it was difficult for me obviously. >> Take three more guys this offense would be tough for a young wide receiver. What have you seen from Dej Stribling effort that is football I think >> he's awesome man. He's phenomenal. He's everything that that I think they we thought he would be and and more when he came out just mature strong fast physical understands the game. uh lines up the formations, very professional about things. He's been so so good and everything we thought he could be. It's really nice to see. >> Question for Ken Black. >> Oh, same thing. Very mature, older. Uh I think he's an older I think his age is older. I think they're just mature and and he he's got a great understanding of the game, a very very professional attitude about everything he does. >> What have you seen from Osa Otisa? >> Uh he's done very well so far. He's our guys are he's he's he's been he's been his presence has been felt since the minute he's got here. >> Good. Thanks, coach. >> Thank you, guys. [music]

title: John Lynch Addresses Kyle Shanahan's Recovery and Training Camp Preparations | 49ers
text: Welcome guys. Appreciate you working through the the traffic and the change with the concert tonight. Um First of all, welcome to to training camp 2026. Hope you guys had a a great uh great summer. Um couple things I thought would be appropriate before we get started. I know we have a lot to cover. Number one, Aldon Smith. Since we last talked, you know, Aldon passed and uh you know, anyone who saw Aldon play the game knows that he was a special football player. Um this one hit especially hard because he was a valued member of our organization. Um but right pri- right prior to him passing, he had spoken to our rookies and really poured into those guys and it was it was extremely impactful. And so, our our our prayers, our thoughts go out to the Smith family as they continue to grieve with that. Um on a more positive note with our organization, you know, and I in a 10 days or so, Roger Craig will be going into the Hall of Fame and we couldn't be more excited for Roger. Um long overdue. Um special football player who changed the way that the running back position was played and I'm so thrilled for Roger and the Craig family. I know the faithful will show up in Canton. I'm going to have an opportunity to go out there and we'll have a big contingent from our organization and it uh was on with a Zoom with the alumni and I I know how excited those guys how much love they have for Roger and the appreciation to the Hall and everyone for for doing right by him. And putting him in in the Hall where he belongs. On to Kyle. So, it was released today, you know, via statement of what happened and here's the great news. It looks like everyone's doing all right. >> [snorts] >> you know, the other driver seems to be doing all right. I don't want to speak to that because that's just second-hand knowledge. Uh Kyle is doing good. He's got some bumps and bruises. Um he did suffer a concussion um in the um in the accident. Um has some lingering effects um from that concussion and you know, we're kind of treating this. We don't have a protocol for staff members when it comes to concussions, but we do with players and it's become very helpful. So, Kyle basically is going to be like in the protocol and Doc Nino and all the great doctors we have are giving him great care and uh we're going to let uh you know, the condition the doctors dictate how he comes back, when he comes back. Um he's been in the building, so we've seen him. He's you know, it's kind of like it we do with our players, a phased back approach. Um you know, number one for Kyle and the Shanahan family is getting him back right. Um he's a tremendous head coach. Um but this is bigger than that. This is about his well-being. And uh we're going to take the time necessary and I think we're very equipped to do that. In his stead, Chris Foerster um is our assistant head coach. He will kind of assume those duties in conjunction in concert with our staff. Um we're not going to blink. We feel like we're well equipped uh for something like this. We we understand what a tremendous leader we have in Kyle. Well, like Chris Foerster, been in the NFL for 34 seasons, 13 of those with Kyle. He knows Kyle inside and out, what Kyle wants, what Kyle needs. Um we've got guys like Clay Kubiak, Raheem Morris, obviously who has head coach experience, Brad Boyer. It The list goes on and on and I think one of the great things Kyle does, aside from coaching his team, is leading this organization and and you know, I think he's tremendous developer of his staff and so um we're not going to miss a beat. Um Um, you know, we will uh, keep you uh, abreast of of, uh, Kyle's progress as as, uh, appropriate as we deem appropriate. And you'll probably see Kyle out there on the field some when, you know, kind of to what he can tolerate. Um, but um, you know, we're going to give the duties of actually running the team over to some other guys and and, um, we have a really good plan. And I'm excited for Kyle to get back, but only when he's ready. So, that's that and I'll I'll I'll be happy to answer any questions. Just a couple more things uh, before we do open it up to questions. Brandon Aiyuk, I I know you guys going to have a lot of questions. Um, Brandon is on a left squad designation. As such, he's not on our 90-man roster. And, um, you know, I'm uh, personally and we as an organization are going to focus on the on the players that are here. And so, I I I don't have, uh, anything to say on that, anything to add, uh, to that. Uh, we wish him well, we wish his family well. Um, to help you guys out with a couple transactions, I think you guys saw we had waived with a non-football injury Khalil Dinkins. Uh, we're bringing in Tanner McClain, uh, who was with Cincinnati last. Um, you know, in his in his, uh, spot, uh, Evan Anderson was released, uh, today uh, or will be later today and, uh, we'll let you know the the, um, corresponding transaction to fill that spot. For PUP, for the active PUP list, we'll have four players start there. George Kittle being one of them. George's rehab is coming tremendous. I know, um, you guys have heard from him. And, uh, he's doing really well and and that's that's very exciting. He's he's doing everything possible to be ready for week one. And, uh, we're thrilled with his progress. Isaac Gurrindo is on is going to start on the active PUP. He's doing very well. MyCole Williams, uh, doing extremely well. Um, and you know, what I would say with Mykel, uh, he's making every effort to be ready for week one. We'll see if that's a reality and uh, we'll let we'll let the uh, the markers and the medical staff kind of dictate that. Alfred Col- Collins will start on PUP, but we anticipate him back in about the second window. Um, you know, don't hold us to that timeline, but that's the plan right now. Can uh, you know, and and if he keeps hitting the markers, that's about when Alfred will be back and um, you know, with that I'll open it up for any questions. >> Uh, John. So, what is Kyle able to do as far as what's his involvement behind the scenes and did you guys or did he basically have or did the coaches put together the the camp schedule and kind of plan before they broke? Like, how does that all work? >> So, that's done long in advance. Um, you know, so a large part of the off season, especially as you um, before we take off, you know, those things, even the installs are put together. Um, so yes, that that is all um, you know, been taken care of. You know, I I think the best way to kind of explain what Kyle's been doing, just like our players, I think, you know, concussion treatment has changed. We don't talk a lot about it cuz we're not supposed to talk about the protocol. Like I said, there's not a protocol for staff, but what they've learned, um, that maybe is different from the past. Like, when I was playing, you had a concussion, they stick you in a dark room and say, "Hey, you know, put a towel over your head and and come out when you're feeling better." Now, they know that it's much more proactive. So, actually getting back to work is a positive thing. Um, but he's not ready yet to be talking to you guys. He's not ready yet to be talking to our team. So, those are kind of the duties that will be assumed. He may be out at practice. You guys will see him. You'll see some, you know, some He did break his nose and so he's, you know, the black eyes are getting better. Um I broke some ribs, that's painful, but that's not what's keeping him away. It's the concussion, and and like I said, we'll continue to evaluate him, phase him back, and as he can tolerate things, we'll expand those, and and that will clearly be dictated by the doctors and and nothing else. >> John, just what was your reaction? It's nothing you can be prepared for. I'm sure you're prepared for many other things. Was it Kyle who called you, or how did you find out, and just what went through your head initially? >> I got the call from our director of security. Um and so obviously the first thing is is everyone okay? Is Is Kyle okay? Uh you know, then I learned there was another car involved. Are they okay? And then and the great news was yeah, you know, absent some some bumps and bruises, it sounds like everyone as far as I know. I don't want to speak for the other um person, because that's not appropriate, but it sounds like everyone's okay, and that's the great thing, and uh so um you know, that that was that. I was down in San Diego, and I I thought, you know, Kyle had last told me that they were coming down there. I think plans changed, so they were up here. >> I just I know you can't know, and it'll be based on what you hear from the doctors, but is there a chance that Kyle does not go to Melbourne, and a chance he's not coaching this team to start the season? >> Well, that's not what we're anticipating. That's not what I've heard from the doctors, but you know, just like we talk about with players, the timeline kind of takes care of itself. So he's got to meet certain markers, but I I I think the expectation is that long before that he'll be better. But again, everybody responds to these things differently, and you know, we're going to do whatever it takes to have him right when he comes back, and and it's the right thing to do. >> Hey John, what have you seen from uh Nick Bosa and Fred Warner this offseason, and what does it mean to get those guys back? >> Uh just tremendous. Um you know, those guys are diligent, hard workers, not only incredibly talented players, but uh they kind of tone setters for the way they work. Uh that's inspiring to their teammates. I mean, Fred you know, I called Dustin Perry a lot during the off-season. How are the guys doing? You know, and and it's strictly voluntary. We we can't mandate that they're here. A lot of them are here and a lot of them are here, I think, because Fred Warner's here. And uh you know, Nick, you know, kind of changed his routine. In the past, he'd go back to Florida. He's stayed here this off-season for the most part. And I think he's feeling really good as a result. So, it's wonderful when your best players are your best leaders. And I think we've got uh we've got great examples of that in those two players. As for their injuries, Nick's doing tremendous. I think we'll see you know, Nick has always had um you know, a different schedule. He's got a great um sense, a great instinct for his body and what he needs. He'll probably start in a phase, you know, individual first, and then we'll we'll add as as we see fit, as he sees fit. Uh Fred you can't hold that guy back, and and he wants to be full throttle, and I think he will be. He's uh you guys know how close he came to being ready at the end of last season. I think all that hard work only made it better as he entered this off-season. So, I would tell you, not speaking for Fred, but I I guess I will speak for Fred cuz I've talked for Fred uh with Fred a ton. He basically was a healthy player just training this off-season. Not not He obviously given some care to the to the ankle, but that's in his mind behind him, and that's a that's a testament to the type of worker he is. >> Y- John, obviously, you weren't there, but as it was explained to you, can can you just kind of lay out details on on what happened with Kyle's accident? How how it >> Yeah, I think I'm going to leave that to Kyle. I think that's more personal because everything second hand. I don't want to get in because other people were involved in exactly what happened. There's a report out there, and and I I I'll just stick to that. >> Thank you. >> Um I know you wanted to avoid Brandon Aiyuk questions, but as a reporter I'm obligated >> should ask you a couple. Um is the intention to keep Aiyuk on that reserve left squad list? Uh A and then B, you guys are playing the Commanders on in week six. He's He's been adamant that he's going at some point to join the Commanders. Is this part of your calculus that you're not just going to release a guy so that he he winds up on on the opponent's roster? >> You met I I understand you got to do your job. I understand, but you know, as I as I said at the start, he's on that list. That means he's not on our roster and I'm going to focus on the guys that are and stand by what we've said already. >> What went into the decision to name Chris Foerster the interim head coach while Kyle's recovering? >> Yeah, so I think what I talked about Grant, I you know, he's been in the league for 34 seasons. We have a tremendous amount of respect. He's been around Kyle. Uh he is our assistant head coach. I I can tell you that yes, you know, in talking with Kyle cuz we had these discussions. you know, we we see it. Yes, Chris is the acting head coach, but it is going to be very much a collective effort. So like yeah, he's going to be out front. He will I'll address our team first. I'll hand it over to Chris. Uh we'll probably do you know, less team meetings uh because Kyle usually sits up here and talks football for 30 minutes. We're not going to try to replicate that. I believe, you know, our culture kind of speaks for itself and we believe what our culture is the people and Chris is one of those who we think very highly of. He's equipped to do this. Our staff is equipped, but it will very much be a collective effort. >> Hey John. I you know, there's been comments that George could be ready for week one. How much do you have to take into consideration you're flying to Australia and that's a lot on his body while, you know, tempering those expectations? >> I All that will be taken into consideration. And with, you know, tremendous players usually comes a collective will that they're a little different and they're going to want to push the envelope. They also, great athletes tend to heal at a different rate and you know, I had the occasion to see in Dr. Al Attarash who did the surgery and he just he went on and on about how how fast George was was healing. Now, I think we kind of take ourselves out of that. We let the doctors, we let the um the the measures um you know, such as like, you know, is there a discrepancy from one side to the other? All those things kind of dictate the readiness. Um everything is involved in that decision as um you know, very much like a trip um that's that's different, you know? So, we have to take everything into account. George knows that. Our doctors know that and we'll be very careful. Um but yet if he's ready, he's ready. And you know, I think that's what he's eager to show us and you know, excited for that process. But he has been tremendous in the process and and uh it it kind of speaks to who George is. >> John, maybe without needing to get into much detail, what's Kyle's mood been like? When you've talked to him, is he joking about it? Is he angry? What what where is his head been at? >> You know, I'd say um I'd say you know, Kyle lives this, his family, football. And so, um very eager to be there. But he But he knows he's not ready to be. So, that's difficult for any competitor. And so, um you know, some emotions that that get come with that. But uh you know, he's he's been at work. You know, visit him over at his house and and um you know, he's he's handling it the way he should, but I I think uh he goes through a process like we all do to get ready for a season like players do. And um you know, it's it's not ideal, but he understands that he's got to kind of let uh the symptoms, the doctors, um he he's understanding of that, but none you know, it's hard for him not to be in there as well. And so, um you know, we we see players go through the similar thing and it's it's no different when it's when it's our head coach and we'll support him through that and uh I think it gives him great comfort to know that like we've got it. We got your back, Kyle, until you're ready. >> And we've talked a lot about the veteran nature of this team, maybe even extra veteran nature of this team. I assume this is a time when it's especially valuable to have 35-year-olds, 32-year-olds, multiple Pro Bowlers who you know, if there's any step in any misstep in leadership, there's going to be able to take over? >> Yes, uh absolutely. I was with Fred the other day. We went over to local firehouse and did a little um you know, we hung out with those guys and and uh you know, Fred got back to Kyle right away and said, you know, his message was we got this, coach. Like like the thing's going to we we got this, you know, trust us. And and so, absolutely the Trent Williams, uh Kyle Juszczyk's, the Fred Warners, we we're we're Christian McCaffrey's, we're Brock Purdy's and then just it's we've got tremendous leadership. Um and uh you know, um different circumstances, but I I'm like I said, we're not blinking. We're our job is to be at our best and um you know, this team has had a focus all off season that I've been very excited about. I know that we've improved our team, um but what gives me a ton of confidence is our approach. And so, prior to this, uh the approach, the the readiness, the the preparation um to be at our best, we understand that um you know, uh we play in a tremendous division that's going to be incredibly competitive. I was sharing that with Kyle right about when Miles Garrett joined the Rams and he was going, "Man, that's really cool." And as we were speaking that came out and Kyle said, "You know what? F John Wooden." >> [laughter] >> So so you know, that's we understand what we're going up against, but we're more more focused on being at our best and and and that we think it's going to be pretty damn good. >> John, I know how much he respects you and talking about how competitive he is. We've talked to everyone. We know we have a really good plan. They don't change. We'll be we'll be ready in Australia. We understand we're we're facing a really great team in in the Rams and and we got to put the work in to be ready for that, but to be ready for the the season at a whole and and really excited about that process. >> John, Seattle [clears throat] won last year obviously and they they were really good in explosives. and it seems like your guys off season that might have been one of your guys themes get more explosive. There's a lot more explosive receivers, running backs. Was that, you know, a thought process here, let's try to be better in that in that area. >> Yeah, we've always been an explosive team and probably fell off there a little and so in your personnel, you go attack that. Mike Evans has been a tremendously explosive player. But I think the bigger approach Larry has been collectively, you know, cuz explosives come in a lot of different shapes and sizes. They come in the run game and we fell off there. The explosives weren't there as much and so that's all 11 on the field. That's your entire team and that's what you emphasize and and I think we spent a lot of time emphasizing that. We did address our personnel. I love what we were able to get accomplished this off season and now we got to go to work and you got to earn everything in this league and explosives are no different and they are an important part of football limiting them on defense and and going out there and being an incredibly explosive team on offense and on special teams and and you know, we we always focus on that, but there's been a heightened focus on that. >> John, I got two questions. One about Kyle, how did you guys spread the word to the team and was it addressed in a meeting early this morning as well, but and like I guess the past 11 days leading up to >> Yeah, well, you know, I think we we kind of wanted the Shanahan family and Kyle and Mandy to kind of do that on their own pace. I I do know that Mandy reached out to some of the captains and some of the players we've known for a long time. Shortly thereafter, I think over the over last weekend and so I think it starts to trickle out. But really we haven't, you know, some guys have been working out, but you know, the the only time the NFL really shuts down is right before training training camp for that month and so people haven't been around. So this this meeting we'll have at 1:00 will really be the first time we've addressed it as a team collectively. >> Uh the other thing you mentioned back at the the league meetings that in terms of the player health, you guys would you've obviously done a lot of studies on the injuries. You said that you might alter some things for training camp. Um >> Yeah. >> Anything that >> Yeah, I won't I won't get into the details. I'll I'll let Kyle when he's back and healthy, um you know, if he chooses to. But I I think you guys will see some different things. Just we we kind of audited everything. Not because we always do that. I do know, you know, I talked about it at the league meetings. I I think $9 million went into our hydro area back there. It's beautiful. I went in there. We got like the whole team in in in there right now, and and they're loving it. And so, um you know, credit to the Yorks. A thank you to the Yorks for always giving us every resource that we need. We've added personnel to our health and performance staff. Um but but we take a hard look at everything. And there's a lot of different dynamics this year with going to Australia later in the year, with going to Mexico City, with the season. Um you know, but we took a hard look at training camp. And there will be some adjustments that uh you know, some of them minor, but but everything counts. And so, you you try to do your absolute best um to give ourselves the best chance to stay healthy. The reality is this league, people get hurt. But uh you know, we've uh I'm real proud of the changes that we have made, and uh we'll keep doing the things we've done well. And uh we'll uh see where it ends up. >> John, if you can kind of talk about the intended or the expected impact of the shift. Obviously, you guys are well-oiled machine, but you're Is Chris Foerster kind of taking it over? Does that pull him away from the offensive line at all? Or what is the >> No. >> What is the weight of >> I don't I don't think that will be the case, you know. Um you know, like I said, we may not have as many team meetings as we typically do because Kyle sits right there in this room and just talks football. Now, you know, should we should we that's different from a lot of places I've been where the head coach gets up, looks at the schedule for the day and says break up. So, we may be a little more let's break up try not trying to replicate something uh so that Chris can coach his guys, but what I do know is Raheem Morris has been a head coach on a couple of occasions. He'll have the defense handled along with his staff and Clay Kubiak um and and Chris and all those guys will have our offense. Brant will take care of the special teams and when we need to come together, we'll come together. So, you know, that's what I mean by a well-oiled machine and uh we'll uh you know, when appropriate we'll come together as a team, but a lot of it will just be all right, we'll miss that, but um when Kyle's back, we'll get back to that and and uh you know, I think we're think we're going to be fine. >> Hi, John. This is year 10 for you. So, what are you most looking forward to seeing unfold at camp this year? >> Uh I just know you. You know, you never climb a mountain the same way. Every journey's different and I love that about this league and I you know, the reality is the teams change so much every year. Um we're fortunate here. We've got a solid core of guys that have been here for a while. So, we have tremendous continuity. Um I love a lot of the additions we've made because of the talent of the players, but more so for who they are as people and their approach and so uh you know, that's what I'm um every year comes challenges. We're talking about one right now with a a tremendous head coach. A guy I think is uh if not the best, right up there. Um so, that's a challenge in of itself, but there is always challenges in this league and um you know, I I find the best players, the best teams find a way to work through that. So, every journey's different and I look forward to that. Um how you going to earn whatever you whatever you uh whatever you want to earn and um I I know the collective will of this group is is is going to be special, and I'm I'm looking forward to that to unfold. >> You said Kyle's been in the building since the accident and maybe on the practice field here and there. Is it important as he recovers to just show face and be around the guys even if not in that official? >> Well, his health is most important, and so he's already seen some of the players. They stop in. you know, but um I think what's most important is his health, and so again, uh that will be dictated, you know, by all right, try to do a little more today until you have symptoms or whatever. And and that's kind of how we do it with players, and that's that's the approach we're taking with Kyle, and that's not me. Um that's Kyle, that's Doc Nino, and all the different specialists that we have kind of assessing and monitoring that, and it's a fluid plan that will that will change and and uh hopefully in, you know, in short time uh he's feeling better and uh and he's back, but but we're going to give it whatever time is necessary. >> John, regarding Chris Foerster, does the assistant head coach title come with any defined responsibilities, or was it more just a reflection of Kyle's respect for him? Kyle um Kyle always talks about, you know, there's no absolute. So, just because Chris was the assistant head coach doesn't mean that's who is going to assume the responsibilities, and as I've said, the way Kyle's thinking about it and has communicated to me that he wants to see things done is that it's a collective effort, but somebody does have to be out front, and you know, but I know like Chris Chris is kind of a grouchy guy. He doesn't really believe in like breakdowns and all that. So, Breheen may do the breakdowns. Fred may do the breakdowns. I think a lot of that will take care of itself, but I think it's probably a reflection, like I said, the 34 NFL seasons. Um His His acumen, he's respected throughout our building and and uh he's kind of earned that. So, you know, we're rolling with that, but everyone will be a part of it. >> Hi John, just one more about how Kyle will be replaced here for the time being. Clay called plays last year during the preseason. Is that going to be what happens on the practice field uh this year and and did Kyle assigning that to Clay, does that better prepare you for >> Yeah, I think what I'd say, Dave, in training camp, I think Clay typically is doing that. Kyle will have suggestions, but Clay usually does the script along with along with the staff. So, nothing different there, but you're right in in past pre-seasons, there's been times where he said, "Clay, call it." Um you know, a lot of coaches in this ling league do things a year out. Kyle kind of does it by feel, and so I don't know what his plan was, but probably Clay was going to call uh the preseason, and uh you know, Clay's certainly capable. Clay's an excellent football coach, and um we're fortunate to have him. >> Jo- John, one more unwanted question about Brandon. I know I know you um a couple weeks ago he had mentioned you specifically had gone to to visit him. Um and he he he [snorts] made it sound like it was unwanted. Can you Can you just clarify if if that indeed that happened and and what your intent or goal was in that situation? >> Yeah, again, I I just If I'm not going to answer one, I don't want to, but you know, I can tell you that, you know, at the at the forefront of our thoughts with any players their well-being, and so I'll just leave it at that, but um you know, we we wish him and we wish his family well. >> Obviously, the defensive line is a is a big deal for you guys in the NFL. 20 sacks last year. I know Bosa coming back is a big deal as relates to that. What level of confidence do you have that kind of you have what you need there now? I mean having the draft and Osa and all that. >> Yeah, uh good question Eric because I think uh when we've been successful here, our our offensive alignment or excuse me, our defensive line has has wreaked havoc. And uh I think that's pretty consistent around the league. We weren't good enough last year. And there's a lot of reasons for for that, but ultimately all those reasons are just excuses. So, you have to address it. I feel confident with the way that we addressed it. Yes, Nick Bynum back is a difference maker, but it was bigger than that. And so, we'll do some things schematically um without changing Raheem's background comes from Monte Kiffin. So, very similar to um uh to what Saleh has done for us and who we've been. But, there will be some expanded things, some more versatility. Um but we've kind of turned over this defensive line over the last couple years with players like Alfred Collins and C.J. West and this year Grayson Halton, Rhamondre Height, Keion White who came in last year. I'm I'm really excited to see that group together and uh see what they can do, you know, because um that certainly is a priority. When we've been at our best, uh we've made the life miserable on the opposing offense from the defensive front. They they, you know, everything starts there. I I knew that as a player. I was a better player when I played with Warren Sapp uh than when I went to Denver and and didn't have that, you know, so I I get that, believe me. And we've made a concerted effort to improve that. Now now we got to go show that we have. All right. Thank you guys. >> [music] [music]

title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 1 of 49ers Training Camp
text: The 49ers just finished day one of training camp. Here's who stood out. The good, head coach Kyle Shanahan. He watched roughly 45 minutes of practice while standing next to John Lynch. He walked out to the field after the media had put away their cameras and walked off the field 20 minutes before the end of practice. It's unclear if that's all he was physically capable of watching or if the 9ers didn't want anyone to take pictures of him while he's recovering. If that's the case, here's what he looked like. He had a wrap around his broken left hand. He wore sunglasses and he walked gingerly when he moved. Clearly, he's not fully recovered yet. But the fact that he could watch practice at all is a good sign. Quarterback Brock Purdy, he didn't miss a beat without Shanahan calling the plays. He spread the ball around, connected with each of his playmakers, and completed a deep pass to Mike Evans who beat Deommodore Lenoir. More on him in a minute. Purdy is entering his fifth season in the league. It would be nice to see him protect the football better than he has in the past. So far, so good. Wide receiver Mike Evans, he made two catches during 11-on-11s. First, he lined up in the slot and beat Malcom Epps with a deep curl route. Next, he lined up at X across from Lenoir who was in man-to-man coverage and Evans blew right past him. He seems fully healthy and in terrific shape. If he can stay healthy, he will have a big season as the 9ers number one receiver. Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall, he caught two passes during team drills. Both catches came against backup cornerbacks, which means the 9ers helped Pearsall look good. Still, the most important news is that he's healthy. The past couple training camps, he missed roughly half the practices and was limited when he did participate. Today, he wasn't limited at all. He seemed fully healthy, which is important because he's the best route runner on the team. Wide receiver De'Jon Stripling, he played with the backups and instantly established himself as Mac Jones' go-to guy. First, he caught a deep pass near the left sideline after beating Darrell Luter Jr. with a deep crossing route. Next, Stripling made a sliding catch after beating Jack Jones with a fade route from the slot. Stripling isn't as quick as Pearsall, but Stripling is bigger and faster than him and will be extremely difficult to cover on play-action passes when he runs deep across the field. Safety Marquis Seagull, he started at safety and intercepted a pass over the middle thrown by Mac Jones. More on him in a minute. Last year Seagal would have pulled a Jaquaski Tartt and dropped that pass. Today he caught it easily. The coaches seem high on him. Safety Malik Mustapha, he took a few reps with the starters and nearly intercepted Purdy who threw a deep pass to Ricky Pearsall running up the left sideline. Mustapha was in center field playing single high coverage. He read Purdy's eyes, broke early on the pass, and arrived with plenty of time to pick it off. He simply dropped it. Great range, but he needs to finish the play. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw, he suited up in practice without any limitations. If the Niners get a full season from Greenlaw, watch out. He's that important. Cornerback Jack Jones, he broke up a pass over the middle from Mac Jones that was intercepted by linebacker Jaylen Graham. Jones is outstanding in practice. In games, he gets burned. Defensive end Nick Bosa, he suited up and participated in warm-ups and positional drills, but not 11-on-11 team drills, which is understandable. No reason to rush him back on the field in July. Still, he seems healthy. Running back Christian McCaffrey, he seems noticeably quicker and faster than last year. Remember, last year he injured his calf week one and never seemed to quite recover. This year he seems fully healthy, at least for now. And the offense still revolves around him, for better or for worse. Running back Khalen Black, Jordan James looks good, but Black looks better to me. Faster, quicker, more decisive. The Niners have have to find a role for Black in their offense this season. He has the talent to keep McCaffrey fresh. The not so good. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, he had a brain fart and let Mike Evans run right past him on third down. It's one thing to let Evans catch a pass over your head. He's big. It's another thing to let him run by you because he's not fast. Lenoir hasn't seemed fully focused since he signed his extension last year. He needs to step up and play better. Right now Renardo Green is the best cornerback on the team and Utton Stout might be the second best. Wide receiver Christian Kirk, he didn't catch any passes during team drills. I didn't see him run any routes, either. He doesn't seem fully healthy, which is a problem considering camp has started. He also didn't participate in any special teams drills. I'd be surprised if he makes the team. Linebacker Marcelino Hightower On the line of scrimmage he looks very skinny. In space he looks stiff and mechanical. Today he tried to stop McCaffrey in the flat and couldn't touch him. Remember Hightower didn't have to tackle McCaffrey, he merely had to tag him and couldn't. Hightower is a 25-year-old rookie who had one good year in college at the age of 24 while playing opposite a much better edge rusher. He might be a mirage. Left tackle Vedarian Lowe, he appeared to injure his ankle during team drills and did not return. The injury didn't seem particularly serious though. Quarterback Mac Jones, he threw two interceptions. One was tipped and one was not. Of all the players on offense, Jones seemed the most affected by Shanahan's absence. >> [music]

title: 49ers NEWS: No PUP for Nick Bosa | George Kittle update...
text: The first roster news of this 2026 49ers season and training camp is here. So, I'll be the first to key you in. Look at the color of that water here in Shaver Lake. We will see with Isaac Guerendo who suffered a torn pectoral muscle over the course of this off season lifting weights. The 49ers might have Guerendo fully healed off of any injury list, but if there is any question, they're going to put him on the PUP list, and that is going to mean that he cannot practice until they remove him from the PUP list. Now, anybody who is placed on the physically unable to perform list can be removed from it at any time over the course of training camp. They still count against the 90-man roster, but it leaves optionality in case they're still on the PUP list when there's a 53-man cut down because that's the only way they can be transferred over to the PUP list in the regular season, which means they don't take up a roster spot. So, 49ers I don't think plan on any of these players who are going to be officially placed on PUP to remain there for the regular season, but they will maintain the optionality, and the good news is they can remove them from PUP at any point during training camp. The off season recharge has finished. I joined Camp we talked about a ton 49ers stuff to set up this training camp. First practice is going to be on Sunday. We started with the quarterback position and moved to the receivers and everywhere else on this roster. So enjoy the appearance on KNBR. Pizza grilling season, lake season coming to a close. Off to the Bay Area for the start of what should be another great 49ers journey. >> And I know David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard is right there with us. He joins us on the Uma guest line. So we appreciate your time and it's good to reconnect. How are you? >> Yeah, I'm doing well. How are you doing? >> Yeah, we're doing well as well. Excited for the season to get going and as long as you just got the sun hat game ready to go. I know Matt Maiocco and Larry Krueger were fighting about that last week. You know, the internet is something that dominates the NFL off-season or or the NFL in season and videos of George Kittle in his rehab process have been something that have getting fans excited. What's your pulse on Kittle and his return timetable? Do you think there's a real shot he could be good to go by week one in Australia? >> Well, he's been doing the stem cell stuff too. He posted about that from Panama which might help accelerate this recovery. I know that the recovery time tables aren't the same that they were even 5 years ago and especially for a player of Kittle's caliber, you look at him and you say you know, that this guy can potentially be back sooner. Now, the question I think is going to come down to whether or not the 49ers want to risk putting him on a 15-hour flight to Australia because as we know those are not good for muscle injury recovery anything. I think he's doing everything he possibly can, but I would expect him to start on the pup list to begin training camp, and they can activate him at any time, and maybe they do activate him, but I think it's an entirely separate question uh regarding whether or not they put him on that flight to Melbourne. >> Uh David, that's obviously one of the big story lines. I think I think Australia will be a big one. How do the 49ers prepare for that? Is training camp going to be different, and in what ways? And of course, you know, can can Kittle come back and at what point? I'm sure the 49ers don't want to telegraph all too much of that ahead of time, and they won't allow us to report on specific scheme stuff from training camp. So, the public probably won't know that until September or so once they do play the Rams. But, you know, something's really interesting to me. You know, we look at a cornerback like Jack Jones, free agent whom the 49ers added. I was just talking about this on Twitter a little bit earlier this morning. He was one of the best zone coverage corners in the league last year. Like, it was he was very productive in zone coverage, but he also was one of the worst man coverage corners in the league last year. So, you know, if he is going to challenge for some playing time, and you would think that he would challenge Renardo Green at at outside cornerback for playing time if if that's going to be a battle, and he's going to have either have to be a much better man coverage cornerback, or maybe the the the 49ers are going to be running a whole heck of a lot of zone under Raheem Morris. So, I think that he can bring some variance to what the 49ers are running. >> What is your sense, David, as to just where the 49ers are at with Renardo Green specifically and and the potential of of him maybe falling out of favor over the course of of last year? >> I The cornerback was not the issue for the defense last year. I think he was okay last year. I don't think he was as good as he was as rookie year. I think that it was a little bit of a sophomore slump, but if you look at the problems of the defense last year, corner was at the very bottom of the list. A, they didn't have a pass rush. They only had 20 sacks, fewest in the league because Bosa got hurt and MyCole Williams got hurt and they didn't have a defensive tackle pass rush really to begin with. Uche Nwosu was supposed to give him a little bit of juice there, but he also was injured for most of the season. B, they weren't good on the second level because Fred Warner got hurt in week six. And C, I thought safety was an issue last year. Now, it might have been an issue primarily because they didn't have a pass rush in front of it, but you know, all the way at the very bottom of the list was the the cornerback issue. The bottom line is that they just didn't have the the troops in that game. I mean, they just too many injuries and they're playing one of the great defenses of all time. Besides that they they got killed by by Seattle in in the playoffs, but I think that Ream will will obviously begins as cornerback two, but somebody like Jack Jones has started games in the NFL before and the goal is to create as competitive of a camp as you can. And again, if Jack Jones can show more proficiency in man coverage, he can theoretically challenge Ream Green for that job and that's a good thing for the 49ers. I I just think that Ream's obviously the favorite to hold on to that cornerback position. >> Talking to David Lombardi of the SF Standard on the Uma guest line getting you ready for 49er football training camp starting this Sunday with the first practice. So we were talking about pressure to perform in terms of being available, but knowing what someone could do versus pressure to perform in terms of leveling up their game or bouncing back from a down year. The secondary fit more of the latter which is yeah, these are guys that are fighting for their jobs or maybe another contract in young safeties, you know, Deommodore Lenoir had a lot on his plate last year. You just talked about Ream Green. With Raheem Morris coming over and taking the place of Robert Saleh as one of the big offseason losses losing Saleh, is the secondary the unit you're going to be most fixated on to watch in terms of just how Raheem can get the best out of these guys and you mean, you mentioned it. He he's done a lot of diversion with his scheme, so we don't know exactly how that's going to work until we see the tape, but is that the unit that you said you got the most eyeballs on? >> No, I would say the whole defense because even with the fronts that they've already shown some hints that there's going to be some more three three four stuff that if they run this year. They're talking a lot about Raheem Morris height the second round pick as as a weapon who they can either drop into coverage or brush from the edge which is obviously his natural position or even line up against guards in some instances. And this is a lighter fast edge rusher and I think that when you look at the fronts that Raheem Morris has coached and the variation that he's coached over his career, this is a a good weapon to be able to to employ in in whatever Raheem Morris wants to run whether it be five-man front or anything else. So, I I think that there's going to be variation in the secondary and I think Raheem Morris starting his coaching career as a DB guy. He was the assistant DB coach in Tampa when John Lynch was a player there. So, there I think Mike Tomlin was the head DB coach. So, there's some cool history there from a few decades ago. Raheem played safety at Hofstra in college. I think that that's probably the the position that people naturally wonder about regarding you know, his background as a coordinator. But I think that the entire defense could throw some interesting wrinkles out there and I'm excited to see it because they have added a lot of young adaptable talent over the past two years. You know, the defense was the oldest in the league in 2024 and they said enough with that. You know, this defense is not good against the run. We need a younger, faster, hungrier defense and they have really stuck to that plan over the past two offseasons and they've gotten a whole lot younger. They're one of the youngest defenses in the NFL now and they've got a defensive coordinator like Raheem Morris who I think is looking at a lot of moldable clay. >> David, switching gears to the offensive side of the ball. De'Jon Struble, how do you think they're going to look to to use him? and do you think that that he's somebody that's going to have the potential to be a factor you know by week one. He's obviously going to have to earn it. We know all young wide receivers have to do that with Kyle Shanahan, but but do you think he's equipped to be able to be a factor come come game one against the Rams? >> Ooh, so that's the hope and a common theme through a lot of this 49ers draft class. The guy we had just talked about Romello Hightower played for six different colleges in six years, which meant that he had to learn six different playbooks. So Deebo Samuel played for three different schools, right? He played at Washington State, he played at Oklahoma State, and then he played at Ole Miss. And all three of those offenses asked him to do different things. So if you watch a lot of the Ole Miss tape, he's either running screen passes and and then taking it to the house cuz he's fast. He's he's got 4.36 speed or he's running some of the go balls. He doesn't do a whole lot of intermediate stuff at Ole Miss, but at Oklahoma State if you put on that tape, he is wearing out the middle of the field. He's more of a position intermediate guy who obviously has the speed to to turn on the jets and and pick up some yards after the catch. So I say all this to imply that that the guy has already shown that he could pick up new playbooks. He's already shown that he could be a adaptable type of weapon and those are exactly the type of characteristics that you're looking for when you need a player to pick up the NFL quickly. When you need a player to be able to you know, you're drinking from a fire hose early on in the NFL. Everybody is drinking from a fire hose, but how quickly you can adapt to it, I think is very very correlated to what you've already shown that you can handle. And since these guys and you're seeing a lot of it in college football now because of NIL, A, they're staying in college for longer. B, they're they're switching teams very often. And and C, these colleges are trying to model themselves after NFL teams and NFL offenses. Well, because of all these things, like you're seeing more ready-made talent, and the 49ers made it a point to go after ready-made talent over the course of this off-season. And you know, just from an analytical perspective, when you talk about contracts and salary cap efficiency, the the first 4 years of a player's career, when you draft them, they come at a very affordable rate because the rookie wage scale determines the contract. These guys can't negotiate their contracts. So, you think like if it takes a guy three or four years to develop, you miss almost all of that window where he's coming to you for cheap. But the 49ers have a bunch of players, and I think Deebo Samuel is Stribling is is one of them, they think that they can get in there right away and get very, very efficient production given the fact that his salary cap hit is only going to be a couple million dollars this year. It's just the nature of football. You have to run the ball effectively to take the the steam out of opposing pass rushes so that you're playing the game downhill so that your offensive linemen aren't left out on a hopeless island. So, I mean, you look at the 49ers offensive line from last year and you also look at the fact that Brock Purdy was the best quarterback in terms of avoiding sacks in the entire league last year. This is how you can replicate my system to be a successful head coach elsewhere. And what was born of that was the Bill Walsh coaching tree, which is the most successful coaching tree in all of NFL history. Kyle Shanahan is technically part of the Bill Walsh coaching tree through his dad Mike Shanahan who worked under George Seifert with the 49ers and Seifert obviously worked under Walsh but Shanahan, Mike, was with the 49ers from '92 to '94. So Walsh set his successors up for massive success and I philosophically Kyle Shanahan, I think, tries to do the same thing. title: Paige Sinicki details her battle against cancer & return to AUSL | Women’s Sports Sundays
text: So, the Athletes [music] Unlimited Softball League, it just wrapped up its second season. So, let's just catch you up on all things AUSL. Kim Eng was named the AUSL commissioner in April of last year after becoming the first female general manager of a men's team >> She's a badass. >> North American sports history. See? Shortly after, Major League Baseball [music] announced a partnership with the AUSL last summer, and there were only four teams in the league a year in a season that ended with the Talons [music] beating the Bandits in the finals. Two teams were added, and that is the Oklahoma [music] City Spark and the Portland Cascade. And now, we are joined, and we welcome in a member of one of those expansion teams, the Portland Cascade infielder Paige Halstead. Hey, Paige. Thank you so much so much for spending some time with us here today. >> Thanks for having me. >> It has been a heck of a year for you. It was 8 months ago that you shared that you had been diagnosed with stage two breast cancer. Can you take us back to to that moment, to your diagnosis? You have been so vulnerable in in your journey and your story. >> Yeah, I found found a lump in October and went back home and uh got some testing done, and sure enough in November I found out that I had the bad news that I had breast cancer, and my whole family and I were just in shock. I was always this healthy person and felt great. I just played at the College World Series, and the next thing you know, my whole world just switched, and I mean, it's just so emotional to think about just from the diagnosis to now where I am now. It's just such a crazy story. >> And you're 23 years old. You were diagnosed when when you were 22, and it's a trend that we're seeing in in young people right now. Were you scared? Were you confident immediately that this was something that you were going to beat? What was what was that feeling? >> Yeah, I think I was really scared. I didn't really know what to expect. I mean, really never had any family go through anything like it, and I always knew though that my parents and my family and my friends are going to have my back through the whole thing, but I wouldn't be lying if there was many nights of crying and just the feeling of unknown. I love playing the game in softball. I just played all these amazing games of the College World Series and the next thing you know, I'm doing treatments and doing chemo and infusions and then surgery and it was just something that I never would have thought I would have had to go through at 22. >> Yeah, I can't I I can't imagine having to go through that, to hear that and to to know yourself to be an athlete and this healthy person and and yet fast forward to this month you were cleared to play and then you were back on the field with your team. What was that like for you? >> It's a feeling that I still can't describe to this day. I remember putting on the uniform and I just cried and cried and I was with my trainer who helped me get through that last part of recovery and I just cried and cried. I was just happy to be there and then as soon as I got on the field, I felt like I was playing with football again. And it was just such like a great experience to just be able to be out on the field with my girls doing what I love. >> Can I just talk about a moment I cried? And that was the triple that you hit. And uh first of all, Portland Cascade I yeah, I went to their home and the fans are incredible for all women's sports in Portland. That that doesn't even need to be said. So, shout out to them. But she hits this triple and it is such a magical moment of every single fan, every single person watching understanding not just your battle, but what you represent. >> Get back on that field. That was like a week after. You had not been playing chemo, radiation, surgery, everything, Paige. Can you tell me about that specific moment? >> Yeah, I just like want people to know that like nothing can take you away from what you love and I didn't want cancer to take away the joy that I had from playing the game and doing my everyday. And so when I was on third base, like I was holding back some tears. I was trying to wait till after the game, but I look around and there's just people standing up and you see the dugout and all the girls are just smiling and it's just like a feeling that I won't forget and I would do that over and over over again just to experience that. It was so unbelievable. >> You've been vocal about just that, the community that you felt rally around you from softball as you were going through this. What did that mean to you to know that while this was something that only you could walk through, that you wouldn't be walking alone? >> Yeah, softball gave me the opportunity to get through cancer the way I did. I think about how it reminded me of just conference like games and stuff, how you go weekend to weekend and your body's tired and you're exhausted and you just kept showing up. And I would go to days when I'm in the infusion center and I'd be like, I kept showing up and showing up and showing up for the teammates when I was at Oregon. And I'm going to do the same thing for my family and for myself. And so I think just knowing that they weren't going to leave my side that whole time, it really just pushed me and propelled me to get back on the field this summer. They they made me know that it was going to be able to happen. And so that was just so cool. >> You've started a foundation because of this, the one for one, and that goes and walks through some of your treatments, how you were able to get through it. Now you're sharing this, raising money to try to help others. Tell us about your foundation. >> Yeah, we're in the works of starting a 5013C, and we're just trying to advocate and educate people on what to look for with breast cancer. I think we do all these tests and screenings when you go for concussion tests to get like cleared to be physically active in college, but I want to do more screenings to just see if like you can catch something earlier. Even if it's saving that one person that didn't know, like I had no family history, no nothing, I'm healthy, we think we're all fine, but it just takes one person that can get caught with it, and I just hope to just change their story how it changed mine. So we're excited to just continue to educate people and like teach them what to look for, and I'm just so excited to use this hard time in my life for something better, because I just feel like that's what I'm called to do, and um I know I wouldn't want to go through this again, but it's taught me so much, and I've just grown so much, and my family and I've grown so much and we're excited to just change people's lives and and just get this on a bigger platform. People need to know about breast cancer and how to get through it and the resources and just to get those screenings done. >> And that you've inspired. I mean, you hear moms that are in the stands talking about your story. People you've never met. What are some of the stories of people that you've heard from that are just just you playing? I mean, by the way, batting 420. I mean, this girl is like [laughter] comes back, makes it look like >> it's it's remarkable. I can't It's really it's actually it's incredible to even try to wrap my head around what you have accomplished here. >> Yeah, that day when I went three for three, my doctor at Oregon, Maggie Dough, she went through breast cancer as well and she was at that game that day. She flew up from Eugene. And so after the game, that was like a story I'll always remember. Like, I was like, we did this. It wasn't me. Like, we did this together and just to share that moment with her and see her just smiling in the stands. Like, I could see her right from third base and it was just like I got chills. Like, I never would have thought that we were going to be doing something like this together cuz when we were senior when I was a senior and she was there, like, we were just having fun and doing our thing and now our whole lives are just different, but we're just proud of the people we've come out of from it. >> And we were chatting before we we came on just about what our intentions were in in chatting with you today and you said that I just want to make sure that I can help. I want to make sure that people know my story and I'm sure there is someone watching right now, whether it is a young girl, someone who was just diagnosed, someone who has someone that they love who was just diagnosed. What would you want them to know? That person right now that is where you were. A little bit scared, doesn't know what the future is going to know to hold, want them to know about what they're about to go through and what you came out the other side of. >> Yeah, one for one. I wrote it down on a sticky note when I was going through my eight treatments. And instead of going one out of eight, two out of eight, I was like, one for one, two for two.
